# The Book of
## Gates of Light

**Which** was composed by the sage in the wisdom of the Kabbalah <note>The Jewish mystical tradition</note>, the divine Kabbalist, our teacher and Rabbi
**Joseph** ibn Gikatilla <note>Joseph ben Abraham Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305) was an influential Spanish Kabbalist. "Sha'are Orah" is his most famous work, providing a systematic map of the ten *Sefirot*, or divine attributes.</note>, may his rest be in Eden and peace. And until now it was like a sealed vision, its depths not fully understood, until there arose the great Rabbi, whose name is well-known in the gates, our teacher and Rabbi **Mattathias** Delacrut <note>A 16th-century scholar from Poland who lived in Italy; his commentary helped make Gikatilla's complex mystical ideas accessible to a broader audience.</note>, may his memory be a blessing. He brought its mysteries to light through a wide and full commentary which he made for the aforementioned work; through him, the whole land shall be filled with understanding, knowledge, and wisdom regarding this book, for he reveals all that is hidden, and its benefit is as clear to the eyes as the sun in the middle of the sky.

---

Prepared for the press a second time with the addition of the "Explanation of the Reasons," and proofread with great care to remove all errors. In this, it surpasses the previous editions, and in all respects, it has achieved a perfect beauty and a typeface the likes of which have not been seen in many years past. And whoever investigates it will find it worthy of praise at its source, and [published] with the agreement of the distinguished communal leaders.

# The Approbation of our Teacher and Rabbi, the Renowned Genius, 
# Abraham Broda—may his light shine—Chief of the Rabbinical Court and Head of the Yeshiva in the Holy Community of Frankfurt am Main

**In** former times in Israel, the precious and valuable book **Sha’arei Orah** <note>Hebrew: "Gates of Light," a fundamental 13th-century work of Jewish mysticism by Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla</note> was the key that opened the way into the Torah, allowing one to enter the study of the wisdom of Kabbalah <note>Jewish mystical tradition</note>. These are ancient matters, yet they have long been hidden in silence. We did not inherit them except for "one in a city or a family" <note>a reference to Jeremiah 3:14, meaning rare individuals</note> who sustained its existence, and even those copies that were marked were entirely worn and tattered. Now, God has stirred the pure spirit of the Torah scholar, Rabbi Benjamin, son of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shemaya, of blessed memory, to spend gold from his own pocket to return and print it. 

He followed the laws of the officials <note>the local governing bodies</note> so that no one else would infringe upon his territory—the territory of Benjamin <note>a play on the publisher's name and the biblical tribe</note>—to print it again. In this matter, he labored and troubled himself to ensure it was properly handled. Therefore, he sought the presence of our teacher and rabbi, the renowned genius, Chief of the Rabbinical Court and Head of the Yeshiva of our community, Rabbi Abraham Broda—may his light shine—to grant him his permission and the strength of his decree. This was to ensure that no person, whether Jew or otherwise, should cause him loss by infringing on what he has printed. 

It is well known and publicized that our teacher and rabbi has refrained for a long time from giving his approbation for the printing of books for his own hidden reasons, and especially regarding books of Kabbalah. However, since this book is so very desirable and precious, and because it is famous that the Holy ARI <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria (1534–1572), the most influential figure in modern Kabbalah</note>, of blessed memory, spoke of the importance of studying this holy book *Sha’arei Orah*, the Genius Rabbi has commanded the undersigned scholars to issue this document. It is written to grant permission to print it and to advocate for him and assist him, for there is great wisdom within it. May those who assist be honored among women <note>a biblical idiom for merit</note>, and may they merit to see the completion of this holy book in the coming days. 

The Rabbi has also decreed with the authority of a Rabbinic injunction that no other person in the world may print this book, *Sha’arei Orah*, for a period of fifteen years without the permission of the current printer, the scholar Rabbi Benjamin. "He who breaks the fence <note>violates the decree</note>, a snake shall bite him" <note>Ecclesiastes 10:8, a traditional warning against breaking Rabbinic law</note>. To those who listen, it shall be pleasant, and a blessing of good shall come upon them. 

These are the words written and signed by the order of the Genius Rabbi, Chief of the Rabbinical Court. Issued from our hands on Thursday, the 7th of Tevet, [5]475 <note>December 13, 1714</note>.

The small Shimon, son of my father and teacher Rabbi Moshe, of blessed memory, Scribe and Trustee in the Holy Community of Frankfurt am Main.
And I, his small student, Meir, son of my father and teacher Rabbi Feibush Schiff, Cohen of Righteousness, of blessed memory, Trustee of the Holy Community of Frankfurt am Main.

# The Approbation of the Great Genius, Rabbi Samuel HaKohen, Chief 
# of the Rabbinical Court and Head of the Yeshiva in the State of Darmstadt, 
# residing in the "Tent of the House of God" in the Holy Community 
# of Frankfurt am Main

**Furthermore**, for this reason, after he sent to us his labor in the Torah to listen to this righteous man who provides merit through the holy book *Sha’arei Orah*—when the Torah scholar Rabbi Benjamin, son of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shemaya, of blessed memory, arrived—he "restored the crown to its former glory" <note>a Talmudic idiom for reviving an old tradition</note> by bringing this book of wisdom to the printing house. Just as it was established by the decree of the leader, a man such as yourself should not be encroached upon in his territory. 

Therefore, I have also come to join my hand with him to agree that the decree shall be fixed: no other person shall put this book under the printing press for fifteen years after the completion of the printing of this book here, without the consent of the scholar Rabbi Benjamin mentioned above. 

Issued from my hand on Thursday, the 7th of Tevet, in the year 5475 <note>1714</note>.

Samuel Kohen Shatin, residing in the "Tent of the House of God" in the Holy Community of Frankfurt am Main, and bearing the burden of the residents of the State of Darmstadt.

# Preface

**Matityahu**, son of the honorable teacher Rabbi Solomon Delacrut, says: The author known by my name, our teacher Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla, called this book of his *Gates of Light* because he begins his words with the "gates" through which one enters and ascends to delight in the Supernal Light. Anyone who reads it must be careful, Heaven forbid, that it should enter his heart to believe in changing attributes or in corporeality <note>original: "gashmiut"; the belief that God has physical form or substance</note>. For anyone who believes in corporeality or change denies the fundamental principle of faith. Anyone who imagines any separation among the <term>Sefirot</term> <note>The ten creative powers or emanations through which the Infinite God acts in the world.</note> "cuts the shoots" <note>An ancient Jewish idiom for heresy or causing a division within the Divine unity.</note>. Rather, they are all a pure and clear light and a complete unity; they are nothing other than the emanation of His powers (may His name be blessed) and His attributes to act and lead His world through them. One should not contemplate them in the heart except as a flame tied to a coal, as is stated in the *Book of the System* <note>Sefer HaMa'arekhet</note>.

Because the intention of this author was to awaken students who are beginning their investigation into this wisdom, and the way of learning is to start with an easy path and a coarse conceptualization, and later to guide them little by little toward the path of negating material descriptions and to be precise with them regarding the internal essence of these matters—therefore, this author did not hesitate to speak in this book about the Sefirot by way of allegory using physical terms. At times he calls this one "Father" and that one "Mother," or "Son" and "Daughter," "Male" and "Female," "Poor" and "Rich," and similar terms, in order to "break the ear" <note>An idiom meaning to use language that is easy for a human to understand.</note> of the beginners in study and to speak with them through metaphor.

He did not mention matters concerning the <term>Emanation</term> <note>Atzilut; the highest level of divine manifestation.</note> or the subtle nature of these things—for the scope of the study of the Secret of the Fifty Gates, the Ancient of Days, and the secret of the 32 Paths of Wisdom, as they appear in the *Book of Formation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*) and especially in the *Zohar* in many "Tikkunim" <note>Aramaic: arrangements or sections of the Zohar.</note> and in other books of Kabbalah—but rather he relied on the books that come after this one in the order of study, which would sufficiently fill the void. Thus, the students would come to understand the subtle and internal aspects of the matters. His intention was to create a sort of preface by explaining the names of the Sefirot according to their kinds, each one under its banner with its reason and its interpretation. This allows the investigator to understand other books that were brief in their explanations and spoke to their audience through concealment and hints.

Nevertheless, he "locked the gates" when he reached certain subtle insights and matters. Therefore, I—the youngest of students, a gleaner of stalks at the entrance of the gates—decided to warn about these things in their proper places so that the fallen should not stumble, and to "build a fence" <note>A metaphor for creating a protective explanation to prevent misunderstanding.</note> around it. I will explain and reveal through hints the places of hidden mysteries, "revealing a handbreadth and concealing two," so as not to deviate from his intention, and so that it may serve as a memory for me in my old age of what I received in my youth from the mouths of scribes and from books during my wanderings to the far-off land of Italy in the year 5310 [1550 CE]. For I feared that forgetfulness would prevail—especially during the difficult and diminishing path of exile—and it was not my intention to compose a formal book, for I am not accustomed to such things. I did not seek wonders or things too great for me; I only recorded the truth as I received it from those who spoke it and as I found it collected in books, and not from my own heart or logic.

Perhaps my colleagues of my age will rejoice in me, those who receive benefit from this utility. I ask the Source of Strength to enlighten my eyes in His Torah, and may He forgive my errors; may the Lord be with my mouth and my heart always.

Because the author did not speak at all about the process of Emanation, I saw fit to record a bit of the order of the Sefirot and Emanation according to the opinion of most Kabbalists.

**A Great Principle:** Before anything else, God (may He be blessed) is first of all and prior to all and exalted above all. He is called the **Cause of Causes**. Before the world was created, all things were hidden and concealed with Him, and it was not known what was in His power. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "Before the world was created, there was only He and His Name alone." For they related all ten Sefirot to the Essential Name <note>The Tetragrammaton (YHVH).</note>, as will be explained further. This means that nothing was known except Him and His Name in its simplicity, but not in its manifestation, for the attributes were all hidden and tucked away in the <term>Ein Sof</term> <note>The Infinite; God's essence before any creation or revelation.</note> in His simple unity until it arose in His thought to create a world of creatures who would recognize and know His ways and actions. He revealed Himself to each one according to the essence of their power to perceive and see the publication of His truth.

This He revealed through the Sefirot, which are the essence of His glory and His attributes through which He acted and worked. For the recognition of God is through His actions, in the same way that—as an analogy—the soul's truth is seen and recognized through its powers and actions in the limbs of its body. Do not think that this was an innovation in Him or a change of will in Him or separate matters, for these Sefirot are His powers...

It is found...

# Preface

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut headpiece consisting of three horizontal bands of repeating stylized foliate or fleur-de-lis motifs.</image-desc>

**Behold**, it is well-known and famous that this book, **Gates of Light** <note>original: *Sha’arei Orah*</note>, is a key to open the eyes of the blind to see into the "shining mirror" <note>original: *aspaqlarya ha-me’ira*; a kabbalistic term for a clear prophetic or mystical vision, often associated with Moses</note>. Through it, we are able to direct our hearts and understand our prayers as we stand before the Creator, who is the Master of the Palace, to whom we constantly offer praise and song. It allows us to understand every hidden wisdom, and from it, light emerges. As was said of it by the Godly, holy man, our teacher Rabbi Isaac Luria <note>Isaac Luria (1534–1572), known as the "Ari," the most influential mystic in modern Kabbalah</note>, of blessed memory: "The book *Gates of Light* is a great key for entering the Wisdom of Kabbalah, enlightening the eyes, beautiful and pure." Because this delightful book could only be found "one in a city and two in a family" <note>A biblical idiom from Jeremiah 3:14 meaning something is extremely rare</note>, and it was a great lack for the Children of Israel, I therefore girded my loins like a hero to bring it **to light** and to print *Gates of Light* with a commentary to benefit the public. My thoughts stirred me to include within the text and the commentary the notes of my lord and father, the Kabbalist, the honorable Rabbi Elijah, of blessed memory. For it is known that my father was a great master of this wisdom. Our teacher, the great and famous genius, Rabbi Abraham Broda <note>A prominent 17th-century Talmudist and head of the rabbinical court in Frankfurt</note> (may his light shine), the head of the rabbinical court and the academy of the holy community of Frankfurt am Main, knew my father and was a faithful friend to him all his life, testifying to his greatness and justifying his words. However, at first, when I showed a few pamphlets with my father’s notes to the aforementioned famous genius, he prevented me from placing my father’s notes inside the main text of the book, saying instead that I should place the notes in the margin <note>original: *be-tzara*; literally "in the side" or "the narrow space"</note> and not within it. But because of the speed of the printing work and various distractions, the master printer did not want to go to the trouble of placing them in the margin. Therefore, I restrained myself from including all of my father’s notes, including only what was necessary and absolutely essential to correct errors, as well as providing citations and references to show the source of the matter in the *Book of Splendor* <note>The Zohar</note> or from other books of Kabbalah. I placed these citations according to the letters of the alphabet within the text and the commentary to make it easier for the reader to find what they seek. I also placed text between two half-circles like this ( ) because without them, even one who has read and studied would not know what he has read. I also proofread the text myself to remove every obstacle, for the entire substance of *Gates of Light* that was before me was covered by the "thorns of error." In my poverty, I have corrected the distortions to the best of my ability. If I have erred, may the good Lord forgive me. It was completed and finished on the day it was said "it was good" twice <note>Tuesday, the third day of the week, which in the Creation story of Genesis contains the phrase "God saw that it was good" twice</note>.

->To the arrangement and date: **God** Almighty **appeared to me in the land of Canaan and blessed me** <- <note>A chronogram using the numerical value of the Hebrew letters in this verse (Genesis 35:9) to indicate the year of publication</note>

->The words of the small and humble Benjamin, son of the honorable Rabbi Elijah Segal <note>Segal is an acronym for *Segan Levi*, indicating he is of the Levite lineage</note>, of blessed memory<-

He describes the technical challenges of the printing process and his use of parentheses and citations to make the mystical text more accessible.</summary>

# Preface

There are thirty-two paths of Wisdom <note>original: *Lamed-Bet Netivot Chokhmah*; the foundational paths of creation described in the early mystical text *Sefer Yetzirah*</note>, and this luminous spark did not cease until it gleamed and was emanated from Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the second Sefirah, representing pure intuition or "the seed" of thought</term>. Likewise, in gradual stages, a spark was called Understanding <term>Binah: the third Sefirah, representing the processing and development of the initial spark of wisdom</term>; it bursts into fifty sparks called the "Fifty Gates of Understanding," and the letter *Heh* <note>The second letter of the Divine Name, Y-H-V-H</note> was revealed. Similarly, from Understanding, a power gleamed and was emanated which they called Kindness <term>Chesed: the fourth Sefirah, representing expansive love and grace</term>, with its seventy-two sparks forming seventy-two bridges. These are called the "Seventy-Two Holy Names," which are well-known and derived from the verses: "And he moved," "And he came," and "And he stretched out" <note>Exodus 14:19–21; each of these three verses contains 72 Hebrew letters, used to derive the 72 names of God</note>.

Similarly, from Kindness came Dread <term>Pachad: also known as Gevurah, the fifth Sefirah, representing judgment, restraint, and divine power</term> with forty-two sparks. They called upon them the well-known "Name of Forty-Two," which is derived from the beginning of Genesis until the word "void" <note>The first 42 letters of the Torah are used to form a mystical Name of God</note>. From this, Beauty <term>Tiferet: the sixth Sefirah, representing balance, harmony, and the heart</term> gleams into seventy sparks called the "Seventy Branches of the Tree." These are included within two colors—white and red—forming "two faces" which are the seventy-two, and they are included in the twelve names of the Divine Name <note>original: *Havayah*; the four-letter name Y-H-V-H</note>. For the Name in its cycles equals twelve, and in its combinations equals seventy-two. As it is said, it is impossible for the twelve branches to have fewer than six directions each (six times twelve is seventy-two): Up, Down, Right, Left, Front, and Back—totaling seventy-two.

Corresponding to this is the "Name of Twelve" derived from the verse: "The Lord reigns, the Lord has reigned, the Lord will reign" <note>original: *Y-Y Melekh, Y-Y Malakh, Y-Y Yimlokh*</note> through the variation of their vowel points. Others say it comes from the combination of the twelve letters of the names *Ehyeh*, *YHVH*, and *Adonai*. Then, Splendor was revealed from Kindness, and from Beauty emerged Victory <term>Netzach: the seventh Sefirah, representing endurance and conquest</term>. From Victory emerged Splendor <term>Hod: the eighth Sefirah, representing majesty and submission</term>, and from Splendor emerged Foundation <term>Yesod: the ninth Sefirah, representing the channel of connection and procreation</term>. Afterward, the power that binds all powers and leads everything emerged; they called it Sovereignty <term>Malkhut: the tenth and final Sefirah, representing the physical world and the manifestation of divine rule</term>. Then the final letter *Heh* of the Name was revealed.

They gave them a visual form: the Crown <term>Keter</term> at the top; below it, Wisdom on the right and Understanding on the left. Below them, Kindness on the right and Dread on the left, to indicate Judgment and Kindness, and the Path of Good. They depicted Beauty below them in the center, acting as the decider, though leaning slightly toward the right because it leans more toward Mercy. Below Beauty, to the right is Victory, and to the left is Splendor. Foundation is below them in the center, also acting as a decider, leaning slightly toward the left. Below Foundation is Sovereignty, leaning further to the left (see the book *Pardes* <note>Likely *Pardes Rimonim* by Moses Cordovero, a major 16th-century Kabbalistic work</note> in the "Gate of their Arrangement"). They depicted "right" as corresponding to a person’s right and "left" to their left; this is according to the secret of "You shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen" <note>Exodus 33:23</note>. Understand this. And this is for you:

[The following is a visual representation of the divine structure]

**The Diagram of the Sefirotic Tree**
->(Ilan HaKodesh)<-

*   **Crown** (Keter) - Top Center
*   **Understanding** (Binah) - Left | **Wisdom** (Chokhmah) - Right
*   **Dread** (Pachad) - Left | **Kindness** (Chesed) - Right
*   **Beauty** (Tiferet) - Middle Center
*   **Splendor** (Hod) - Left | **Victory** (Netzach) - Right
*   **Foundation** (Yesod) - Middle Center
*   **Sovereignty** (Malkhut) - Bottom Center

This is their form according to the order of their "Chain of Succession" and their branching out, like the likeness of a tree with its branches and boughs; this is why they called it the "Tree of Kabbalah." The reason for this gradual order is from the perspective of the "receivers" <note>The beings or worlds that receive divine energy</note>. For it is known to them that a physical thing is inferior to the spiritual, and the spiritual force appointed over Good is in some way more complete than that appointed over Evil. Therefore, they said that Understanding is like the "Form" to the "Action" on the side of Kindness. For Wisdom and Understanding in a person are more spiritual activities. Similarly, the activity of Kindness is like the "Form" to the activity of Judgment <note>original: *Din*; another name for the Sefirah of Pachad/Gevurah</note>.

The activity in the existence and preservation of all things collectively is like a "Form" for all of them, because this proceeds from a state of total balance. Thus, they said that Beauty is like a "Form" for the others. However, the activity in unchanging existences—which is Victory—is like a "Form" for the activity in the celestial spheres, which is Splendor. And the activity in the celestial spheres is like a "Form" for the activity in souls and in primordial matter <note>original: *hiyuli*; a philosophical term for the most basic, formless matter</note>, which is Foundation. All of them are like a "Form" for the binding power that leads and supervises specific physical things. Therefore, he depicted them in this gradual order, using terms like "Giver" <note>original: *Mashpi'a*</note> and "Receiver" <note>original: *Mekabbel*</note>.

They also called the three highest Sefirot by the name "Soul" <note>original: *Neshama*</note>, the three middle ones "Spirit" <note>original: *Ruach*</note>, and the lower ones "Vitality" <note>original: *Nefesh*</note>. Sovereignty is the power that leads everything according to the actions seen from Him, may He be blessed. This is according to the analogy we gave regarding the soul. And as we said, the intellectual mind cannot grasp the power of pure simplicity except through the way of physical forms and visions. We have already warned that they are all one in complete unity, powers emerging from Him, may He be blessed,

->and remain<-

# Preface

They [the divine attributes] were actually always present within Him, but they were hidden and unified with Him as one. These are the attributes of His actions and His essence which were revealed later; they were not a new creation, but rather a revelation of the truth of the hidden thing. This was revealed to created beings through various levels because perceiving His absolute simplicity is impossible. The human intellect cannot grasp things except through essential attributes, accidental qualities, or through actions. Similarly, the revelation of the Blessed One occurs through His actions and relationships within these intermediary attributes. Although they are counted as ten, they are all one; they emerge from His unique power and unto Him they return.

One should contemplate this by looking at human actions: how they emerge from the source of the soul, which rules them through the limbs of the body. In truth, the soul has no intermediary; there is only the place where its power is revealed. The beginning of the expansion of the soul's power is in **Thought**; through the power of thought, it becomes **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah: the flash of intuitive insight</term> and begins to ratiocinate. Afterward, it **Understands** <term>Binah: the analytical process</term> what is appropriate from what is inappropriate. These functions are attributed to the brain and are specifically called the *Neshama* <term>Neshama: the highest level of the soul, associated with the intellect</term>.

Furthermore, there emerges from the heart a feeling power that moves all the limbs to their actions through the "spirit of life." Afterward, it awakens toward good, evil, or a middle path. Sometimes it awakens to show favor and kindness—acting as a person of benevolence—and sometimes, when it sees an evil deed, it awakens to anger, and "smoke rises in its nostrils" to take revenge with cruelty. When it sees a good deed, it draws will and satisfaction from the brain through the spinal cord to show mercy and to do good with justice and righteousness. These powers are specifically called the *Ruach* <term>Ruach: the middle level of the soul, associated with emotion and animation</term>.

Furthermore, there emerges from the liver a power that nourishes and causes growth, and another that desires. This power is called the *Nefesh* <term>Nefesh: the most basic level of the soul, associated with physical drives and biology</term>; it leans toward material things and maintains the body for its allotted time. We should also consider the power that binds all these things together and leads them appropriately; this is the "Temperament" and "Nature" found in every individual according to their unique composition.

It is well known that all these actions come only from the power of the soul and are attached to it; they are its very powers flowing and revealing themselves from it. Even though we call one "Spirit" and another "Vital Soul," this is only in terms of their proximity to the physical; the *Neshama* itself is always indivisible and unseparated. It is a single, hidden essence, and its true nature is unknown to us; we only say that it is the "power-holder" over all these actions. Just as the nature of the source must be found in that which is hewn from it, so too—conversely—as human actions are revealed through the aforementioned intermediaries, we can imagine the **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: the process by which the Divine flows into the universe</term> (or "expansion," or "glow," or "spark"—call it what you will) that was revealed to His creatures from the truth of His essence. This is the power of Divinity, attributed and described through these intermediaries which emerged into actuality gradually, from emanation to emanation, for the sake of the created beings. Nevertheless, it all occurred without time and without division.

Therefore, the Kabbalists established and received—and arranged for us—the Order of Emanation. They called them *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot: the ten divine attributes or channels</term> based on the terms for "purity" and "brilliance," derived from the phrase "as the whiteness of the sapphire" <note>original: *Livnat ha-Sapir*; see Exodus 24:10</note>. Just as forms can be seen within a sapphire stone, so too the *Sefirot* are the mold and form of all existing things. There is no "addition" of substance in them, just as the appearance of things in a sapphire occurs without adding anything to the stone itself.

The sage Rabbi Azriel <note>Azriel of Gerona, a famous 13th-century philosopher and Kabbalist</note> said that the *Sefirot* are a power equal to every thing and its opposite; as opposite things are reflected equally in a sapphire, so too the hidden existences in the depths of the "Nothingness" <term>Ayin: the Infinite, Unmanifest Godhead</term> are revealed in them and acted upon through them. They do not constitute an addition or a multiplicity in our **Cause of Causes** <term>Ilat ha-Ilot: the Primordial Cause, God</term>, just as all things revealed and acted upon in a sapphire to the eye of the beholder do not add to or multiply the stone itself.

Thus, it was permitted to describe the Blessed One with these attributes. They said that when the Blessed Name desired to publicize His truth and create a world, a power sparked from Him whose light shines upon creation. They attributed this to "Thought," just as a builder (as an example) thinks about his building, becoming wise and planning the construction during his contemplation. They called this the **Supreme Crown** <term>Keter Elyon: the first and highest Sefirah, representing the Divine Will</term> because it crowns everything. Then the "tip of the [letter] *Yod*" <note>The smallest point of the first letter of the Name of God, representing the start of manifestation</note> was revealed from the Essence, and that light sparked (with the reason being like the horn of a crown) into 624 sparks of light <note>The numerical value of the word *Keter* (Crown) is 624 in some traditions or 620 in others; here the text specifies 624</note>. This was not sufficient for the Crown until there sparked <insert>and see further the explanation of the nature of the *Book of the Kingdom* in *The Maggid* page 13 and 11 regarding the source of the Crown, etc.</insert> from it, in gradual stages, the spark of **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*). Then the "thickness of the *Yod*" was revealed, sparking also into thirty-two sparks, which they called

->Heart<-

# Your Request

<note>The original Hebrew text displays this word inside a decorative floral border.</note>

You requested of me, my brother and friend of my soul, that I illuminate for you a path regarding the matter of the names of the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "הק"בה ית' וית'", an abbreviation for HaKadosh Baruch Hu—the standard Jewish way of referring to God</note>, so that you might fulfill your desire through them and reach your intended goal. Because I have seen that your intention is upright and even better than your request itself, I felt compelled to inform you how the "light is divided" <note>A reference to Job 38:24, here meaning how divine influence is distributed</note>, and what path the Lord, may He be blessed, desires or does not desire. Once you reach the knowledge of this matter, then "you shall call and the Lord will answer." You will be among those close to Him, you will love Him with all your soul, you will delight in the Lord, and He will grant you the requests of your heart.

**Have** you not known? Have you not heard? The Lord is the Eternal God. The upper and lower beings tremble before Him; the earth quakes from the fear of Him; and before His wrath, who can stand? Who can rise against His burning anger? If He does not trust even His "holy ones" <note>meaning the angels</note> and the heavens are not pure in His eyes, how much more so is man—who is loathsome and corrupt, drinking iniquity like water? How then shall one born of a woman use His Holy Names and make of them "an axe to cut with" <note>A famous rabbinic idiom meaning to use holy things for personal gain or practical use</note>? Who is this, and where is he, whose heart has emboldened him to do such a thing—to stretch out his hand toward the crown of his King and make use of it? 

Behold, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Anyone who pronounces the Name of the Lord according to its letters <note>original: "ההוגה את יי' באותיותיו"; this refers to the phonetic pronunciation of the four-letter Name of God (the Tetragrammaton), which is strictly forbidden in Jewish law</note> has no portion in the World to Come." Consider the holy and supreme Rabbi Hanina ben Teradion: he did not pronounce the Name by its letters for any mundane or practical use, but only in a respectful manner in order to learn and understand the ways of the Lord. Despite this, he was punished. How much more so should we, who are impoverished and lacking, be careful? Do you not see what the Torah wrote: *You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain*? Although this comes to warn against a false oath, the Torah expressed it in language that implies you should not carry His name upon your lips idly. It could have simply said, "Do not swear by the name of the Lord your God falsely," but by writing "You shall not take [or carry]...", we learn two things <note>both the prohibition of false oaths and the idle mention of the Name</note>. When Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, ascended to the heights, he learned the secret of mentioning the Lord’s Name from the Ministering Angels, and he warned Israel about this, saying: *When I proclaim the name of the Lord, ascribe greatness to our God.* If the angels on high are careful in mentioning the Name of the Lord, how much more so should a "maggot and a worm" <note>a humble metaphor for a human being</note> be? 

This applies especially to one who contemplates using the "Crown of his Creator" <note>the Divine Names</note> for practical ends. This is a "how much more so" argument, given that in this time, there are none truly expert in the mentioning of the Name and its uses for the sake of an "Action" <note>meaning "Practical Kabbalah" (Kabbalah Ma'asit): the attempt to use divine names to perform miracles or magic</note>. 

<insert>This refers to Practical Kabbalah <term>Kabbalah Ma'asit: the use of Hebrew names and incantations to effect physical change</term>, through which one might try to draw down influence via Holy Names or charms. This is a great study, as written in the book *Kav HaYashar* <note>original: "קב"י", likely referring to the ethical-kabbalistic work Kav HaYashar</note>, to diminish the study of the Zohar and similar works... no simple person can reach the greatness of the Lord except through understanding.</insert> 

If so, nothing will result for the one who mentions the Name except the loss of his soul.

The reason is that every letter indicates a specific Sefirah <term>Sefirot: the ten divine attributes or emanations in Kabbalah</term>. This will be explained further in this book. Thus, one who pronounces the Name by its letters is like one who "separates that which is joined" <note>meaning they break the unity of God's attributes</note>. Therefore, the High Priest in the Holy Temple was the one who knew how to direct his intention toward the Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divinity</term> and the flow of divine influence in its general and specific aspects, bringing blessing upon all the "vessels of the world," as explained later in Gate 5, page 39b.*

# You Have Asked

My brother, friend of my soul, you have asked me to illuminate a path for you concerning the names of the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Ha-Kadosh Barukh Hu" (The Holy One, Blessed be He), the standard Rabbinic way of referring to God</note>, so that through them you might fulfill your will and reach your desired destination. Since I have seen that your intention is upright and even better than your request itself, I found it necessary to inform you how "light is divided" <note>A poetic reference to Job 38:24, here referring to the distribution of divine illumination</note> and what is the path that the Blessed Lord desires or does not desire. Once you reach the knowledge of this matter, <unclear>then</unclear> <unclear>you shall call</unclear> and the Lord will answer; you will be among those close to Him, you will love Him with all your soul, you will delight in the Lord, and He will grant you the desires of your heart.

**Have** you not known? Have you not heard? The Lord is the eternal God; before His presence the upper and lower beings tremble, from the dread of Him the earth shakes, and before His wrath, who can stand? Who can endure His fierce anger? Even in His holy ones He puts no trust, and the heavens are not pure in His eyes—how much less so man, who is abominable and corrupt, who drinks iniquity like water? How then shall one born of a woman make use of His Holy Names and treat them as an axe with which to cut? <note>This is a reference to a famous teaching in Ethics of the Fathers (Pirkei Avot 4:5) warning against using the Torah or Divine Names for personal gain.</note> Who is he, and where is he, whose heart has emboldened him to do such a thing—to stretch out his hand against the crown of his King and make use of it? And you [surely know] what our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "Anyone who pronounces the Name [of God] by its letters has no portion in the World to Come." <note>original: "Ha-hogeh et ha-Shem b'otiotav." This refers to pronouncing the four-letter Name of God (the Tetragrammaton) as it is written, rather than using a substitute like "Adonai."</note> Even the holy and lofty Hanina ben Teradion <note>A 2nd-century scholar and martyr who was burned at the stake by the Romans for teaching Torah.</note>, who did not pronounce the Name by its letters for secular purposes or for [magical] use, but only out of honor in order to learn and understand the ways of the Blessed Lord—even so, he was punished. How much more so for us, who are impoverished and lacking. Do you not see what the Blessed Lord wrote in His Torah: "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain"? Although this comes to warn against a false oath, He expressed the matter in language that implies you should not "lift" <note>The Hebrew verb "tissa" (תשא) can mean both "carry" or "take" and "lift" or "utter" on the lips.</note> His name upon your lips idly. He could have said, "You shall not swear by the name of the Lord your God falsely," but by writing "You shall not take," we learn two things from it. And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, when he ascended on high, learned from the ministering angels the secret of mentioning the Blessed Lord's name, and he warned Israel about this, saying: "When I proclaim the name of the Lord, ascribe greatness to our God." If the celestial angels are cautioned regarding the mention of the Blessed Lord, how much more so for "maggots and worms" <note>A common liturgical expression of human humility before the Divine.</note>—and certainly for one who is enticed by his own mind to use the crown of his Creator. It is an even greater "how much more so" given that in this time, there are none expert in the mentioning of the Lord and its uses according to the "way of action." <gloss>Meaning: Practical Kabbalah <term>Kabbalah Ma'asit: the use of divine names and incantations to effect physical changes in the world</term>; one can harm oneself through the Holy Names and longings. This is a great foundation hidden in the book "Kemi" <note>Likely referring to a specific amulet or mystical manual, or a misspelling of a known title like the "Kaneh."</note> according to the custom of the Kabbalah of the Zohar and its likeness. These names are not to be used for one's own benefit, for you can only [rightly] know them to understand the greatness of the Blessed Lord, as I will explain later.</gloss> If so, the one who mentions it will achieve nothing but the loss of his world, bringing upon himself a ban of excommunication.

# Preface

And they remain attached like a **flame bound to a coal**. Therefore, they are called *Atzilut* <note>original: אצילות; a term for the highest world of "Emanation" in Kabbalah</note> from the linguistic root meaning "beside," for they are beside Him. Since He clothes Himself in them, serves as a soul to them, and acts through them, how could He be divided? For He is distinct and simple with the **ultimate simplicity** <note>In medieval philosophy, "simplicity" refers to being absolute and indivisible, not "easy" or "basic"</note>, may He be blessed forever. They, too, are from the truth of His simplicity and His actual power; they are not a created, physical thing, but rather **emanated light**.

For by His own action, without their existence, things would not be withheld from His perfection; for no action emerges from Him that lacks perfection. Everything will be explained there.

# Preface

And they remain attached like a flame bound to a coal; therefore, they are called *Emanation* <note>original: "אצילות" (Atsilut)</note> from the expression "beside Him" <note>original: "אצלו" (etzlo)</note>, for they are beside Him. There is no separation here at all—neither from their Emanator <note>original: "מאצילם" (Ma'atsil) — referring to God as the source of the emanation</note>, may He be blessed, nor from one to another. For He acts through His attributes <note>original: "מדותיו" (middotav) — the divine qualities or Sefirot</note> like a craftsman with his tools, or like a soul within the limbs of its body. Since He clothes Himself in them and serves as a soul to them, acting by their hand, how could that which is One be divided? He is separate and simple with the ultimate simplicity <note>original: "פשיטות" (peshitut) — the philosophical concept that God is non-composite and indivisible</note>, blessed be He forever. They, too, are truly of His essential simplicity and power; they are not a created, physical thing, but rather an emanated light.

These matters are deep, and this is not the place for their full explanation. As we have said, this book was composed only for those who are beginners in this study. We shall yet explain in the book *The Order of Divinity* <note>original: "מערכת אלהות" (Ma'arekhet Elohut) — a classic 13th-century Kabbalistic manual</note>, which follows this one in the order of study, all these matters with a deeper and more subtle explanation. This includes the reason for the number ten <note>referring to the ten *Sefirot*, or divine emanations</note>—neither less nor more—and the necessity of their emanation. For if He acted by His own essence without their mediation, things would never cease from their own perfection <note>The author suggests that without the "filtering" effect of the Sefirot, the world would be overwhelmed by God's infinite perfection and could not exist as a finite realm</note>, for no action could emerge from Him that was less than His own total perfection. Everything will be explained there.

->wonders from His Torah<-
->Amen.<-

# Gate 1

Rather, it is because "he knew My name," for knowledge is the essence. And afterward, "he will call Me and I will answer him"—meaning, when a person needs to speak and directs his intention toward that specific Name upon which the matter he requires depends, then I will answer him. Do you not see that in a time of distress, our forefather Jacob mentioned the Name **El Shaddai** <note>original: אל שדי; often translated as "God Almighty"</note> and said, "May **El Shaddai** grant you mercy" (Genesis 43:14). And Daniel, when he prayed toward the Temple, said, "Cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary, for the sake of the Lord [*Adonai*]" (Daniel 9:17). And even though our Sages of blessed memory interpreted this in the tractate *Berakhot* as "for the sake of Abraham who called You 'Lord'," we still require further explanation <note>original: למודעי; a term suggesting a need for deeper or esoteric information</note>. And Hannah, when she prayed that the Lord would give her "human offspring," it is written: "**O Lord of Hosts** [*YHVH Tzevaot*], if You will indeed look on the affliction of Your maidservant" (1 Samuel 1:11). Even though the Sages interpreted this in *Berakhot* as they did <note>א</note>, there is still a core and an inner root to the matter. I have not come to provide homiletic interpretations, but rather to get to the root of the matter. Since this is the case, I must place in your hand a core principle and a root upon which to lean:

**Know** that all His holy Names mentioned in the Torah are all dependent on the Name of four letters, which is **YHVH** <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter Name of God, considered the most sacred and the source of all other Names</term>. And if you should say <note>ב</note>, "Is not the Name **Ehyeh** <note>original: אהי"ה; "I Will Be," the Name revealed to Moses at the burning bush</note> the essence and the source?"

**Know** that the four-letter Name [YHVH] is like the image of the trunk of a tree, while the Name **Ehyeh** is the root of this tree <note>ג</note>, and from it, the branches spread out.

---

And immediately his folly will be spoken. This is part of the practice of the Wisdom of Kabbalah, for our wisdom and our language are not like general openings and merits, because the **letters possess life and spirituality**. They are universal matters, may He be blessed. This is what is meant by the saying "the letters fly in the air" (cf. Talmud, Avodah Zarah 18a). In prayer, we learn that "His words are living and enduring." Therefore, all the letters, words, and verses of the Torah also possess movements and unique properties. Through their combinations, blessings are activated; they act like medicinal recipes or specific intentions. Therefore, there is no language like this known language, and everyone understands it. The little we have achieved, we have no desire in it except as explained. 

Jacob's mention of **El Shaddai** is explained further on in Gate 2, page 15. In the explanation of **El Shaddai**, they mention the unique properties of that Name specifically for Jacob, in the context of the connection of all the *Sefirot* <note>The ten Divine attributes or emanations</note> to grant him a blessing from that word, but internally for that matter to which he was bound, as explained further on in Gate 4, page 86, where the matter of Hannah is clarified. 

In the Jerusalem Talmud, it is said that once a certain wise man came to a scholar, and the scholar was Rabbi Nuri the Levite, one of the Kabbalists who directed their intentions in one blessing toward a specific "extension" and in another blessing toward a different "extension." For there are laws regarding the *Sefirot*—to pray that they should grant [petitions]. He replied, "Heaven forbid that prayer should be to anything but the **Ein Sof** <term>Ein Sof: The Infinite; God as He exists prior to any manifestation or attributes</term>, blessed be He and blessed be His Name, for He is like the Cause of all Causes <note>ד</note>." 

This matter is like a person who has a legal dispute and comes before the King to seek justice. Jacob understood this cause well regarding the verse "Justice is His" (Deuteronomy 33:21). If a person directs their heart toward a specific appointed minister, their mission might be a mistake if there is someone else to oppose him from another place. This is what is meant by "He who looks toward the appointee." However, if he seeks the essence of the King, he will find favor. This is the matter of prayer: it is always toward the Infinite (meaning the actual *Ein Sof*). However, the thinker intends to draw the flow (*shefa*) to the specific *Sefirah* associated with the thing he is requesting. For example, when praying for the righteous, one intends for the *Sefirah* that receives **Chesed** (Loving-kindness), which is the attribute of Mercy. When praying regarding heretics, one intends for **Gevurah** (Strength), which is the attribute of Judgment. So too with the rest of the blessings. This is the intention of the pious Kabbalists. 

It is very good if you are prepared in all this. However, it is better to pray simply to the Lord with intention, and He will know to which "gate" the request belongs. As the verse says: "Commit your way to the Lord; trust in Him, and He will act" (Psalm 55:23). For the essence of prayer takes the place of sacrifice, and the purpose of sacrifice was to arouse the "inner powers" and to direct them. Behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, placed power in the hand of man; while he is a chosen being, he arouses things according to his will, as suggested by the verse "And He will do the will of those who fear Him." This was also His intention, may He be blessed, to benefit His creatures. The "Chariot" <note>the Divine system</note> is modeled after a human and his limbs; all the systems act and are aroused through his choice toward the good, as will be clarified shortly. Therefore, the early masters, who knew the distinct gates and the order of the progressions, would direct their prayers according to the mentioned order to arouse the "inner powers" and the attributes through the process of emanation. But for us, who do not have a clear tradition from a wise master, but only a refined explanation of a few *Sefirot* that have been left to us through hints and riddles, it is better for us to pray to the Lord simply, and He in His mercy will lead us.

<note>א</note> *Explanation according to the Truth (Kabbalah):* Hannah built the Temple, which is the "Secret" and the "Palace" for the Name of Blessing. The Kabbalah teaches that there are three "Temples" and "Palaces" in the Name *Yedid* <note>meaning "Beloved"</note>, as discussed on page 6. Regarding the Temple, and these are "God will grant us" etc. And our connection is to the Name YHVH, to reveal it. They brought forth Abraham himself in the Name of four letters [YHVH], as explained at the beginning of Gate 149.

<note>ב</note> *Is not the Name Ehyeh the essence:* Meaning, because it is the Name of **Keter** <note>The "Crown," the highest Sefirah</note>, from which everything is born toward the Name of four letters [YHVH], which is the Name of **Tiferet** <note>"Beauty," the central Sefirah</note>.

<note>ג</note> *And from it they branch out:* Meaning, the Name **Ehyeh** is like a point...

<summary>This page explains that while God has many Names (like El Shaddai or Ehyeh), the Tetragrammaton (YHVH) is the central "trunk" of the Divine tree. It also offers a crucial Kabbalistic perspective on prayer: while one may direct thoughts toward specific Divine attributes (Sefirot), the ultimate address of prayer must always be the Infinite God (Ein Sof).</summary>

# Gate 1

**And now**, my son, listen to my voice and let your ears be attentive to my counsel. <gloss>My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent</gloss> <note>Proverbs 1:10</note>. My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent. If they say, "Come with us, and we will hand over to you Names and incantations <note>original: "shmot vehazkarot"</note> that you can use," my son, do not walk in the way with them; keep your foot from their path. For all those Names and their uses are various kinds of nets and snares used to hunt souls and lead them to destruction. Even if the early Sages truly possessed the Holy Names received from the mouths of the prophets—such as the Name of 72, the Name of 42, and the Name of 12 <term>72, 42, 12: Specific combinations of Hebrew letters believed in Kabbalah to represent profound levels of Divine power</term>, and many other Holy Names—and were able to perform signs and wonders in the world with them, they would only use them for a great need, such as during a time of religious persecution or for the Sanctification of the Name <note>original: "Kiddush HaShem"; an act that brings honor to God, often involving self-sacrifice</note>. 

An example is Rabbi Meir, who rescued his wife’s sister from a brothel <note>referring to a famous story in the Talmud, Avodah Zarah 18a</note>. He said to the guard, "Whenever you see yourself in trouble, say: 'God of Meir, answer me!' and you will be saved." Yet even though he said this to that non-Jew in a time of need, when Rabbi Meir himself was in danger, he did not use the Name but instead fled, as recorded in the first chapter of the tractate *Avodah Zarah*. This is similar to the stories of Honi the Circlemaker, or Raba before King Shapur as recorded in the tractate *Ta'anit*, or David when he dug the foundation pits of the Temple and the deep waters rose up and threatened to flood the world, as recorded in the chapters *Ha-Chalil* and *Sanhedrin*.

**The boundary** of truth and the tradition of the covenant is this: One who wishes to achieve his desires through the Names of the Holy One, blessed be He, should strive with all his might in the study of the Torah to understand the inner meaning of each and every one of those Holy Names mentioned in the Torah, such as: 
*   The Long-Suffering One <note>Arich Anpin</note> for the **Crown** <note>Keter</note>
*   **Yah** for **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>
*   **YHVH** for **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>
*   **Adonai** for **Kingship** <note>Malkhut</note>
*   **El** for **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note>
*   **Elohim** for **Strength** <note>Gevurah</note>
*   **Shaddai** for **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>
*   **Hosts** <note>Tzevaot</note> for **Victory** <note>Netzach</note> and **Splendor** <note>Hod</note>.

One should begin here with just these nine Holy Names. Know that they have been tested, and the secret of them is like the moisture and freshness of a branch. A person should know and understand that each of these Names acts like a key for every single thing a person needs for any trouble or matter in the world. When one contemplates these Names, he will find the entire Torah and its commandments depending on them. When he knows the intention of each Name, he will recognize the greatness of Him who spoke and the world came into being. He will then feel awe and fear before Him, and he will yearn and long to cling to Him through the knowledge of His Names, may He be blessed. Then he will be close to the Lord, and his prayer will be accepted. Regarding this, it is said: "I will set him on high, because he has known My name. He shall call upon Me, and I will answer him" <note>Psalm 91:14-15</note>. The verse does not say "I will set him on high because he *mentions* My name," 
<gloss>but rather</gloss>

rather, it means because he *knows* it. It is enough for him <unclear>...</unclear> forever. For the main point of establishing Divine Kindness was not, Heaven forbid, merely to write about his Creator to honor Him, but to follow his Master and be blessed by Him. The primary purpose of his study should be to know and recognize his Creator and to contemplate His greatness and the quality of His goodness. For His power, wisdom, and goodness are great; one should long to follow His attributes and to pray so that he knows how to direct his intention in prayer until his prayer is pleasing and accepted before Him, as will be explained in its place. All this is not merely about having His Holy Names on one's lips, but rather to walk in glory and awe in his heart, to learn the way of conciseness and concealment, for "in a multitude of words, sin is not lacking" <note>Proverbs 10:19</note>. 

There are three categories of Holy Names mentioned in the Torah: For these Names are the honored Names of God, names that transcend the Divine Emanations <term>Sefirot: The ten attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe</term> that we mentioned in the introduction. Every name in the Torah is a combination of the letters of these Names, based on the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet. All of them are attached to the Great Name of four letters <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter name YHVH, the most sacred name of God</term>. Because these ten attributes <note>the Sefirot</note> have many aspects, all Names draw their sustenance and activity from them, cascading down into various titles and descriptions. The entire Torah is filled with these Names and titles. Every Name and title has its own direction and leadership, and acts with great kindness toward all existence according to the will of God, who acts through them for judgment, kindness, or mercy. These are the "Upper Heavens" of the Holy One, blessed be He. Through them, God rules the lower world to act upon those below. When a person is pure and prepared, and knows the secret of the "mentions" of these Names according to the order of their kingdom and appointments, and knows the nature of their unique properties, he will have the power to act through them according to his will and his prayer, performing signs and wonders in an instant. <note>Regarding the matter of oaths/adjurations</note>: For they all stand in various Palaces <term>Hekhalot: Heavenly palaces or chambers described in early Jewish mysticism</term>, and each one has specific angels in the world of the messengers. Every specific detail is moved by an angel through the Name appointed over it to perform a specific action. Immediately, the spirituality and the flow of the life-force spreads downward into the world of action through the decree of those letters, titles, and seals.

<summary>This page warns against using Divine Names for magic (Practical Kabbalah), arguing instead that true spiritual power comes from a deep, internal understanding of the Names as representations of God's attributes (Sefirot). It explains that the Tetragrammaton is the source of all Names and that correct prayer requires "knowing" rather than just "reciting" these holy titles.</summary>

**The written word** is a sign corresponding to that specific substance and known form called "Reuven son of Jacob." <note>The author uses this name as a generic example of a human individual.</note> And because the Blessed Name <note>original: "Yitbarach Shemo," a common way to refer to God</note> desired to grant us merit, He created within the human body many hidden and revealed limbs in the likeness of a sign for the **Work of the Chariot**. <term>Work of the Chariot: (Ma’aseh Merkavah) A form of Jewish mysticism focused on the visions of the Divine throne-chariot described in the Book of Ezekiel.</term> If a person merits to purify one of their limbs, that limb becomes like a **throne** <note>original: "kiseh"</note> for that internal, supreme matter called by that same name—if it is an eye, then for the Eye; if a hand, then for the Hand; and so too for all the rest. # Gate 1

And that they take root and branches spread to every side; and all the other Holy Names are all like the likeness of branches and twigs extending from the trunk of the tree, and each one of the branches produces fruit according to its kind. And aside from the known Holy Names which are forbidden to be erased, there are several other appellations <term>appellations: (kinnuyim) descriptive titles or attributes of God, rather than His essential Names</term> attached to each and every Name. For example, if you ask: Who are the appellations of **YHVH**? They are **"Awe-inspiring,"** **"Bearer of iniquity,"** and **"Forgiver of transgression."** Who are the appellations of **EL** <note>original: "A"L," a Name associated with kindness and greatness</note>? For example: **"I Will Be"** <note>original: "Ehyeh"</note>, **"Judge,"** and **"Justice."** And for each one of these appellations, there are other appellations attached to each and every one of these, and they are all the other words of the Torah. Thus we find that "the entire Torah is woven upon" the appellations, and the appellations upon the Names, and the Holy Names are all attached to the Name **YHVH**, and all of them are unified in it. It follows that the entire Torah is woven upon the Name **"YHVH."** Therefore, it is called "The Torah of YHVH is perfect." <note>Psalm 19:8</note> Thus you find that when you understand the intent of the Holy Names according to their families and grasp the appellations specific to each of them, you will then see that everything depends on His Great Name, may He be blessed. You will then long and yearn to cleave to Him, and you will fear and be in awe of Him; then you will "understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God." <note>Proverbs 2:5</note> You will enter the fellowship of those about whom it is said: "I will set him on high, because he has known My name." <note>Psalm 91:14</note> Then you will understand how great is the punishment of one who mentions the Name of Heaven in vain, all the more so one who pronounces the Name according to its letters, and certainly one who makes practical use of it <note>a warning against "Practical Kabbalah" or using Names for magic</note>. And before I begin with the intent of this composition, I must place before you one introduction, which is this:

# General Principle
Know that the truth of the Essence of the Creator, may He be blessed, is not grasped by any other being. Among all the heavenly hosts, none knows His place, let alone His true Essence. Do you not see what the heavenly angels say? "Blessed be the glory of YHVH from His place" <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>—meaning, in whatever place He may be. If this is so for the upper beings, how much more so for the lower beings! If so, all those matters that we read in the Torah, such as **"Hand,"** **"Foot,"** **"Ear,"** and **"Eye,"** and all others like them—what are they? Know and believe that all those matters, even though they indicate and testify to His greatness and truth, no creature can know or contemplate the essence of that thing called "Hand," "Foot," "Ear," or the like. And if we are "made in His image and likeness," let it not enter your mind that an eye is in the literal form of an eye, or a hand in the literal form of a hand. Rather, these are internal matters, truly internal to the reality of the existence of YHVH, may He be blessed, from which the source and the flow <term>flow: (shefa) the divine energy or influence that sustains the universe</term> emanate to all existing things by the decree of God, blessed be He. But the essence of the [Divine] Hand is not like the essence of a [human] hand, nor is their form equal, as it is said: "To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" <note>Isaiah 40:25</note> Know and understand that there is no likeness between Him and us in terms of essence or form; rather, the intent is that the forms of the limbs within us are made in the likeness of signs for hidden, supernal matters that the mind cannot know, except as a likeness of a memory. Just as one might write "Reuven son of Jacob"—for these letters are not the man himself, nor is this the actual form of Reuven son of Jacob, his shape, his structure, or his essence, but rather a memory of the line of Reuven son of Jacob.
**The written word** <meta>catchword: הכתוב</meta>

Every appellation for Him is a word from the "Attributes," which are the *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot: the ten divine emanations or attributes in Kabbalah through which God interacts with the world</term>. <meta>Continuity: This page transitions from the general metaphor of the Divine Names as a tree (discussed on the previous page) to the specific study of the first "Gate" or Name: Adonai. It moves from abstract theology to the practical preparation required for prayer and spiritual ascent.</meta>

# O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall declare Your praise
<note>Psalm 51:17. This verse traditionally precedes the Amidah prayer, inviting Divine aid in speech.</note>

The secret of the Lord is wisdom, and the root of Kabbalah <note>original: "Kabbalah," meaning "received tradition" or Jewish mysticism</note> is faith in the Lord, may He be blessed. "If the Lord is your Law," the intention of "His way <gloss>my thoughts</gloss>—then you shall walk securely in your way and your foot shall not stumble." The first Name among the Holy Names is the Name called <term>Adonai: (Lord)</term> <note>This Name is associated with the Divine attribute of **Malchut** (Sovereignty or Kingship)</note>. King Solomon, peace be upon him, said: *“Watch your step when you go to the house of God.”* <note>Ecclesiastes 4:17</note> He informs us in this verse that a person must examine themselves and be careful when they wish to pray before the Lord, may He be blessed. One must see and understand if there are "accusers" or "hinderers" preventing their prayer from being accepted. One must clear the path and remove obstacles from their way.

This is comparable to a person going to the King’s court to request a favor. Such a person must be careful to know if there is any trouble or danger on the road. Furthermore, they must consider how many gates are in the King’s house—one after another—and recognize the guards appointed to watch those gates. One must be liked by all of them and know if there is any enemy among them who might exert power over them. Beyond all this, it is proper for the person to look at the clothes they are wearing, to see if they are fit to enter the King’s courtyard in them, as it is written: *“For no one may enter the King’s gate clothed in sackcloth.”* <note>Esther 4:2</note> In addition to this, one should examine if they are worthy to speak before the King, the ministers, and the deputies who stand before Him—and if the King will have mercy on one whose request might be challenged. Likewise, one must consider if they can endure staying in the King's palace for an hour or two if they are delayed. 

Our Sages of blessed memory found it necessary to awaken us to this, and they stated a great principle: "The earthly kingdom is like the heavenly kingdom." If one must be so careful in a kingdom of flesh and blood, how much more so when entering to greet the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. A person must understand and know that from the earth to the firmament there is no empty space <note>original: "makom panui"</note>; rather, everything is full of "troops" and multitudes. Some of them are pure, masters of kindness and mercy; but below them are many impure creatures, damagers and accusers. They all stand and fly in the air. From the earth to the firmament, there is no empty space; rather, it is all full of multitudes—some for peace and some for war, some for good and some for evil, some for life and some for death. 

The "Song of Plagues" <note>Psalm 91, traditionally recited for protection from spiritual harm</note> is based on this: *“You who dwell in the shelter of the Most High... For He will rescue you... with His pinions... You shall not fear... from the pestilence that stalks in the darkness... For He will order His angels...”* All these camps between the earth and the heavens are like a person walking a path in a place of <margin>danger</margin>.

## The First Gate

"The Secret of Wisdom" and the "Root" of Kabbalah. Regarding the Sukkah of the Lord, may He be blessed, etc., as mentioned previously regarding the hint of the 33 Holy Names. These are the primary forces that influence one who walks on the proper path and manages personal affairs through the "Secret of Sovereignty." This is the path of drawing down Divine abundance <note>original: "shefa"</note>. The Name **Adonai** is the first because it denotes lordship and dominion, coming from the word for "Lord." It is the final "attribute" <note>the Sefirah of Malchut</note> which receives the crown to distribute and manifest in the lower world. It is also called "Kingship" <note>Malchut</note>, as will be explained further. It is the first Name because it is the first one close to us as we go from below to above. 

(2) This space is full of troops. I found this also at the end of Gate 3, page 27: these troops between heaven and earth are created from a person's actions and intentions. Whether the deed is good or bad, it gives birth to a force or a spirit—either good or evil. A person should humble themselves and know how to build their spiritual stature. This is the secret of the saying: "He who performs one commandment <note>mitzvah</note> acquires for himself one advocate; he who commits one transgression <note>aveirah</note> acquires for himself one accuser." Through the power and spirit of a good deed, a "defending angel" is created and emerges. The opposite happens with a transgression. This was the intention of the prophet when he told David: *“The Lord has also passed over your sin; you shall not die.”* <note>2 Samuel 12:13</note> He did not say the sin was "erased" or "taken away," but "passed over"—meaning he removed that specific "accuser" created by the sin so that it could no longer bring charges. This is also the secret of what is said here: that every person who comes before God must deal with the "camps" created by their own deeds.

# Gate 1

The <term>Merkavah: (Divine Chariot)</term> is nothing other than the Patriarchs. How so? Our father Abraham, peace be upon him, took hold in purity of the "Right Side" and inherited the "Right Hand" of the realms above, which is the attribute of <term>Chesed: (Loving-kindness)</term>. Concerning this, it is said: *“And Abraham traveled, going and journeying toward the Negev [the South].”* <note>Genesis 12:9. In Kabbalistic geography, the South represents the Right side and the attribute of Chesed.</note> Isaac took hold in purity of the "Left Side," which is <term>Pachad: (Fear or Awe)</term>. Concerning this, it is said: *“And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.”* <note>Genesis 31:53. "Fear" is used here as a Name for the Divine attribute Isaac embodied.</note> Jacob took hold in purity of the "Middle Line." Concerning this, it is said: *“And Jacob was a simple man, dwelling in tents.”* <note>Genesis 25:27</note> Between the tent of Abraham and the tent of Isaac, the three Patriarchs were found to be a "Throne" for the Chariot. In this manner, one should contemplate the matter in its clarity and see the Creator in His established place.

**And now**, we must enlighten your eyes regarding a matter that depends upon this. Know that the <term>Middot: (Divine Attributes)</term> are associated with the limbs of the body. For example: the attribute of the eye is sight; the attribute of the ear is hearing; the attribute of the hand is action; the attribute of the foot is walking. Behold, these attributes follow the limbs. Even though our Sages of blessed memory used the language of "Attributes" in reference to the Realms Above, we must judge the matter of these Attributes just as you would judge the matter of the "Ear," "Hand," or "Foot" mentioned before. Just as there is no comparison between us and the Divine regarding physical limbs, so too there is no comparison between us and the Divine regarding these Attributes. Because we must use the language of "Attributes" throughout this book, watch yourself and guard your soul very carefully lest you stumble and say that the Lord, may He be blessed, has a limited or measurable attribute. This is not the case! Rather, just as the concepts of "Eye" and "Ear" have no physical measure, limit, or likeness in the Divine, so is the rule for the Attributes.

Behold, our Sages of blessed memory called His Holy Names "Attributes," as we learn in the first chapter of the tractate Rosh Hashanah: *“Rabbi Yehuda said: A covenant is made regarding the Thirteen Attributes, that they shall not return empty-handed, as it is said: 'Behold, I make a covenant...'”* <note>Exodus 34:10</note> These Thirteen Attributes are: *“The Lord, the Lord, God, merciful and gracious, slow to anger...”* <note>Exodus 34:6. These are the qualities of Divine Mercy revealed to Moses.</note> The general rule you must believe is that there is no likeness between the Attributes of the Lord, may He be blessed, and our own attributes, except by way of using the same name as a signifier. Regarding this, our Sages said in every place: *“Come and see: the attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not like the attribute of flesh and blood.”* Now that we have placed the key to this introduction in your hand, we may enter into the explanation of each of the Holy Names written in the Torah. We shall enlighten your eyes in every place you find one of them written, so that you may understand and contemplate the "Source of Living Water" that flows from all His Names. When you grasp this, you will make your path successful and gain true wisdom.

## Gate 1

Danger. Every prayer a person offers passes through various "bands" <note>Groups of spiritual forces or angels.</note> and ascends to the heavens. If a person possesses merit, <term>bandits<note>original: "lestim" (from the Greek leistēs). In this context, these are destructive spiritual forces that "hijack" or block prayers that lack the proper spiritual weight or merit.</note></term> will not strike at their prayer. But if they lack merit, many spiritual afflictions and destroyers strike at the prayer along the way. Because of this path, King David—may peace be upon him—established the <term>Songs of Praise<note>original: "Zemirot." David is traditionally credited with the Book of Psalms, parts of which are recited as "Zemirot" or "Pseukei D'Zimra" in the morning service.</note></term> to clear a path for the prayer to pass. This is because those bands of forces are like a cloud that hinders the prayer from ascending, as the scripture says: *“You have screened Yourself off with a cloud, so that no prayer may pass through.”* <note>Lamentations 3:44</note>

When David, may peace be upon him, came and established these Songs of Praise, he intended that while a person is reciting them, those destroyers, spoilers, and obstructers should depart and go their way. They are called *Zemirot* from the root meaning <term>to prune<note>The Hebrew root Z-M-R means both "to sing" and "to prune" or "cut away." The author is explaining that the songs "prune" away the spiritual obstacles.</note></term>. As it says, *“He shall cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks.”* <note>Isaiah 18:5</note> Concerning this, the scripture says: *“Your statutes have been songs to me in the house of my pilgrimage,”* <note>Psalm 119:54</note> meaning that in those places where I was afraid on the path—where I felt dread and fear—I used those Songs to "prune" and "cut away" the obstacles. 

This is also the meaning of the verse: *“When the morning stars sang together...”* <note>Job 38:7</note> The concept of "singing" refers to the Songs of Praise said in the morning. Then, all the agents of "Harsh Judgment"—called the "Sons of God"—hurry away and shout in alarm. The word for "shout" <note>original: "yari'u"</note> is related to the word for "broken," as in *“The earth is utterly broken.”* <note>Isaiah 24:19</note> Therefore, a person must focus themselves during prayer and direct their thoughts properly so that their prayer is not hindered and their request does not return empty. Concerning this, our sages said: *“A person should always assess themselves: if they can focus their heart, they should pray; if not, they should not pray.”* <note>Talmud, Berakhot 30b</note> This means: if one can focus their prayer toward whichever "Gate" (or medicine, or Divine Name) is required for their specific prayer, they should pray; otherwise, they should not.

**And after** I have informed you of this, know that the essence of faith and the foundation of Unity <note>original: "Yichud" – the mystical practice of unifying the aspects of the Divine.</note> is to understand the applications of the Names. <margin>It is explained here as follows, written on ancient parchment: We must return and inform you that the essence of faith and the foundation of foundations is to understand and know all His Holy Names.</margin> For all the Holy Names mentioned in the Torah are included within the <term>Four-Letter Name<note>The Tetragrammaton, YHVH.</note></term>, the Blessed Lord. He is called the "Trunk of the Tree," while the other Names are like roots, branches, or hidden treasuries. 

Each Name has a specific function, distinct from the others. This is like a treasury house that has many rooms. Each room is designated for a specific thing: one room for precious stones and pearls, one for silver, one for gold, one for food, one for drink, and one for clothing. If a person needs food but does not know which room holds the food, they might die of hunger even though the house is full of goodness. It is not because the Master denied their request, but because they did not know which room held what they needed.

In this exact way, one must attain knowledge of the Holy Names. Certain Names are appointed over prayer, mercy, and forgiveness; others over tears; others over afflictions and troubles; others over sustenance and livelihood; and others over Strength/Might.

It is not merely that I [God] give you permission to take for yourself, but you may grant favor according to your will to all people of the world. This is the meaning of *“And all the families of the earth shall be blessed through you.”* That is to say, anyone who wishes to take anything from this blessing can only take it through you, for it is delivered into your hand and belongs to you.
