<meta>This page continues the discussion of Gate 2, focusing on the Sefirah (Divine emanation) of Yesod (Foundation), which is associated with the Divine Name "El Chai" (The Living God). It explores the concept of "Signs" (Otot) and "Covenants" (Britot), linking the Sabbath, circumcision, and the rainbow to this specific spiritual level.</meta>

# Gate 2

Through prayer during the Exodus from Egypt, several signs and many miracles and wonders were renewed, according to the secret of the verse: **"And God saw the children of Israel, and God knew"** <note>Exodus 2:25</note> and the secret of **"And I remembered my covenant"** <note>Exodus 6:5</note>. And now, we must inform you that the **Sabbath**, which is the attribute of **El Chai** <note>literally "The Living God," the Divine Name associated with the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, is called a **sign**, as it is said: **"Between Me and the children of Israel, it is a sign forever"** <note>Exodus 31:17</note>.

The **Covenant of Circumcision** is also called a **sign**, as it is said: **"And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between Me and you"** <note>Genesis 17:11</note>. This secret is hinted at in the blessing for circumcision: 

> Blessed are You, Lord... who sanctified the beloved from the womb, placed the statute in his flesh, and sealed his offspring with the **sign** of the holy covenant. Therefore, as a reward for this, O **Living God** <term>El Chai: The Living God</term>, our Portion and our Rock, command the rescue of the beloved of our holy seed from the pit <note>referring to Gehenna or spiritual destruction</note>, for the sake of His covenant which He placed in our flesh. Blessed are You, Lord, who makes the covenant.

The **Rainbow** is also called a **sign**, as it is said: **"I have set My rainbow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between Me and the earth"** <note>Genesis 9:13</note>. We have already informed you that the "Covenant of the Rainbow" is the covenant of **El Chai**. Therefore, know that wherever you find the word **Sign** <note>original: "Ot"</note> in the Torah, it is the secret of **El Chai**, which is the secret of **Remembrance** <note>original: "Zichron"</note> that reminds **Adonai** <note>The Name associated with the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> of all the inhabitants of the world. The sign of the covenant of the Sabbath and the covenant of circumcision is specifically between Him and all flesh upon the earth.

Know that sometimes the Name **Adonai** is included within the word "Sign." You already know that the Sabbath day is called a sign, and the Sabbath is included in the commands to **"Remember"** and **"Observe"**. Similarly, circumcision is called a sign, and it is included in the acts of **circumcision** and **uncovering** <note>referring to the two stages of the ritual, Milah and Pri’ah</note>. The secret of the word **Sign** <note>Ot (אות)</note>, according to the path of plain meaning, is that the letter *Aleph* (א) is the secret of the "Small Yod" known to the masters of wisdom, which is the lower tip of the letter *Vav* (ו). It is called the **Small Sign** and the **Sign of the Holy Covenant**. 

Now, know and understand all these things; write them upon the tablet of your heart and let them not depart from your eyes. Know that upon the foundation of this Sefirah, the language of the **Oath** <note>original: "Shevuah"</note> was established in the Torah. I shall now explain: know that every oath a person swears depends upon this attribute called **El Chai**. The reason is that every expression of **Oath** <note>Shevuah</note> is derived from the word for **Seven** <note>Sheva</note>. 

The secret of this matter is found in what our father Abraham said to Abimelech: **"For these seven ewes you shall take from my hand, that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well."** Therefore, he called that place **Beersheba**, because there they both **swore** <note>Genesis 21:30-31</note>. Do you not see three expressions mentioned in this place, each corresponding to the other? He said first: **"seven ewes"**; as a **"witness"** over the well; then he said: **"Therefore he called that place Beersheba"**; and what is written after that? **"Because there they both swore."** The explanation is that these three expressions—"seven ewes," "Beersheba" <note>Well of Seven</note>, and "they swore"—are all unified in that oath. Therefore it says, "Therefore he called the place Beersheba." What is the meaning of "Therefore"? It means because of the "seven ewes" and the "oath." He called it Beersheba for two reasons: the seven ewes and the oath.

In another place it is written: **"And he called it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba"** <note>Genesis 26:33</note>. Do you not see that he called the city Beersheba after the name "Seven" <note>Shibah</note>, without mentioning an oath there? This is because the essential foundation depends on the secret of **Seven**. The place of the "Well" depends on the "Oath." Now we must clarify: know that anyone who swears is swearing by the secret of the **Seven Sefirot**, which are the secret of the **Seven Days of the World** <note>the seven lower emanations through which the world was created</note>. Everything depends on the attribute of **El Chai**, which is the Sabbath, which is—

# Gate 2

And the sign for this is **"My statutes you shall keep"** <note>Leviticus 19:19</note>. The secret of **"My statutes"** <note>Hebrew: *Chukotai*</note> refers to the Divine names **El Chai** <term>El Chai: The Living God, associated with the Sefirah of Yesod</term> and **Adonai** <term>Adonai: The Lord, associated with the Sefirah of Malchut</term>. Know that the "Covenant" which is called **"day and night"** <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note> is the secret of **circumcision** <note>Hebrew: *Milah*</note> and the **uncovering** <note>Hebrew: *Pri'ah*, a specific stage of the circumcision ritual</note>. These correspond to the Sabbath commands of **"Remember"** <note>Exodus 20:8</note> and **"Observe"** <note>Deuteronomy 5:12</note>, and to the names **El Chai** and **Adonai**. They also represent the **Written Torah** and the **Oral Torah**, which are the secret of the "statutes of heaven and earth" placed one against the other. This is the secret of the verse: **"And in His Torah he meditates day and night"** <note>Psalm 1:2</note>. **"Day"** refers to the Written Torah, the secret of El Chai, the secret of "Remember," and the secret of circumcision (*Milah*). **"Night"** refers to the secret of the Oral Torah, the secret of Adonai, the secret of "Observe," and the secret of uncovering (*Pri'ah*).

Therefore, the Torah is only handed over to one who has received the **covenant of the flesh** <note>circumcision</note>. From the covenant of the flesh, a person enters into the **covenant of the tongue**, which is the reading of the Torah. I must enlighten your eyes as to how the Blessed Name, **YHVH**, signed His great Name into our father Abraham and his descendants who received the Torah. How so? The **Book of Creation** <term>Sefer Yetzirah: An ancient and foundational Jewish mystical text</term> says: "He carved a covenant for him between the ten fingers of his hands," and this is the **covenant of the tongue**, the seal of the name **Yah** <note>the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>. This is found in the secret of the **Yud** (=10) representing the ten fingers, and the **Heh** (=5) representing the five phonetic sources in the tongue of the Torah. These sources follow the secret of the letter groupings: 

1. **Gutturals** <note>Aleph, Chet, Hey, Ayin</note> from the throat. 
2. **Labials** <note>Bet, Vav, Mem, Peh</note> from the lips. 
3. **Palatals** <note>Gimel, Yud, Kaph, Qoph</note> from the palate. 
4. **Linguals** <note>Dalet, Tet, Lamed, Nun, Tav</note> from the tongue. 
5. **Dentals** <note>Zayin, Samekh, Tzadi, Resh, Shin</note> from the teeth. 

Thus, the seal of the name **Yah** <note>YH</note> is found in the covenant of the tongue, which is the covenant of the mouth.

He also carved a covenant for him between the ten toes of his feet; this is the **covenant of circumcision** and the seal of **Yah**. This is half of the Great Name, according to the secret of the ten toes plus the one circumcision, which equals eleven <note>11 is the numerical value of the Hebrew letters Vav and Heh, the final two letters of the Divine Name YHVH</note>. This calculation of eleven corresponds to the letters **Vav** and **Heh**. Furthermore, the secret of **Vav-Heh** represents the Written Torah (Vav) and the Oral Torah (Heh). Everything depends on the covenant of circumcision, which is the lower root of the letter **Vav**. The **Heh** is the secret of the Oral Torah and the secret of the *Pri'ah* (uncovering).

Because of this, the Torah is not handed over to a Gentile, as he is uncircumcised. This is why our sages said regarding the **Blessing After Meals** that one must mention the "Covenant" before the "Torah." We say: "For the heritage You gave our ancestors... for Your **covenant** which You sealed in our flesh, and for Your **Torah** which You taught us." This is also why it is said: **"He tells His words to Jacob"** <note>Psalm 147:19</note>—specifically to one who is circumcised like Jacob (may peace be upon him). A Gentile who is uncircumcised and engages in Torah study is liable for death <note>a traditional legal hyperbole emphasizing the exclusivity of the covenantal relationship</note>. 

Because the covenant of circumcision and uncovering are the secret of the Sabbath (in "Remember" and "Observe"), circumcision overrides the Sabbath <note>meaning the ritual is performed even on the Sabbath if it is the eighth day</note>. It takes place on the **eighth day**, which is the secret of the name **Adonai**, and the secret of the *Pri'ah* performed after the circumcision. The secret name is **Adonai YHVH**. Thus you learn that the covenant of circumcision overrides the Sabbath because it is the very same spiritual attribute. 

Now, contemplate: whenever you find the word **"Covenant"** in the text, look to see which side it refers to—the covenant of the tongue, the covenant of the flesh, or the uncovering (*Pri'ah*). Now that we have awakened you to these principles, you must guard yourself and be very careful not to be among those who defile the **sign of the holy covenant**. For all the portions written regarding **forbidden sexual relations** <term>Arayot: The biblical prohibitions against incest, adultery, etc.</term> throughout the Torah are dependent on these two Sefirot: **El Chai** and **Adonai**. Some are also tied to the two Sefirot attached to them, called **Elohim Tzvaot** and **YHVH Tzvaot**. 

With God's help, a path remains open for you to understand how many good virtues and how many awesome matters are bound to the circumcision of the covenant. Similarly, you will understand the judgment for one who uncovers nakedness <note>commits sexual sin</note>, or one who intentionally arouses himself, or one who holds his organ while urinating. Many hidden and sealed matters you will understand, with God's help, from these things we have hinted at here. Sometimes this is called in the Torah by the term **"Sign"** <note>Hebrew: *Ot*</note>, because signs and wonders depend on this attribute. # Gate 2

The days are for him like sorrow, and every single day curses this denier **A** <note>A reference to a specific category of person who denies the Divine or perhaps a section marker in the text</note>. And for this reason, "whoever swears in the land shall swear by the God of truth" <note>Isaiah 65:16; the Hebrew word for "truth" here is *Amen*</note>. One must be careful regarding the faith in the **God of Truth** (*Elohei Amen*). The punishment for a false oath has already been revealed in the Talmudic tractate of *Shevuot* <note>Tractate Oaths 39a</note>, where the Sages of blessed memory said: "There are things that fire does not consume, but a false oath consumes them." 

**B** The reason for their "seal" is clear in the context of the *Book of Creation* <term>Sefer Yetzirah: An ancient Jewish mystical text describing the formation of the universe through Hebrew letters and numbers</term>. How so? In the nature of fire, it burns all types of wood, clothing, and other similar materials until they are gone. However, fire does not consume stones or dust; even if stones are burnt, they turn into dust and are not truly destroyed. But a **false oath** <term>Hebrew: *Shevuat Sheker*</term> consumes even stones and dust. 

The reason for this is that all created beings were not created, nor do they have any existence, except through the **seven Sefirot** <term>Sefirot: The ten divine emanations in Kabbalah; here referring to the lower seven that govern the natural world</term> which are called the "Seven Days." Upon those Sefirot depend the heavens, the earth, all their hosts, and even the basic elements: fire, water, wind, and dust, as well as mountains, hills, seas, rivers, all types of plants, all living creatures, and all human beings. 

Therefore, when a person denies the truth in an oath, he is effectively denying the seven Sefirot upon which his life, existence, wife, children, wealth, and everything he owns depend. When he denies these seven Sefirot—which are the "secret" or spiritual essence of the **Oath** <note>The Hebrew word for "oath," *Shevuah*, shares a root with *Sheva*, meaning "seven"</note>—then these seven Sefirot consume the very essence of his life and his property, both land and movable goods. This is because everything depends on them; they created all creatures and acted like the **Artisan** <term>Hebrew: *Uman*</term> who performs a craft. Just as a craftsman can destroy and ruin the work he made, so too the one who denies an oath denies the Artisan who made the world. 

When he denies the Artisan who made the world, that Artisan can destroy his house, himself, and all that belongs to him, even the dust and stones. Since the Artisan who made the stones can erase their memory from the world, and the "secret" of the Artisan (*Uman*) is the "secret" of **Amen**. Therefore, one answers "Amen" when an oath is administered. This is the secret of "swearing by the God of Truth (*Amen*)"—meaning, the one who swears, swears by the Artisan who created the world. This is the secret the Sages expounded on the verse: "**Then I was beside Him, as an artisan** (*Amon*)" <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>. They said: "Do not read it as *Amon* [nursed/growing up], but as **Amen** [or *Uman*, Artisan]." Therefore, the Sages of blessed memory said that the matter of an **Oath** and **Amen** are one and the same at the time the oath is administered.

**C** And with God's help, we will further explain to you the secret of **Salt** (*Melach*) and **Amen** regarding the drawing down of Divine abundance through the spiritual channels. Because the Oath encompasses the seven Sefirot that served as the Artisan for all creatures, the Sages said: "Things that fire does not consume, a false oath consumes them." The reason is that the Oath is the Artisan that created the fire, the stones, the dust, and all creatures. Therefore, fire cannot destroy stones or dust because dust is a primary element just like fire, and both are created things. But the Oath—which is the secret of the Artisan and the Creator—can consume fire and stones and all other creatures, for everything is in the hand of the Artisan who made all creations, may He be blessed and exalted. This is what the verse means: "**Of old You laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands. They will perish, but You will endure; they will all wear out like a garment. You will change them like clothing, and they will pass away**" <note>Psalm 102:25-26</note>. 

This is the secret behind the saying that things fire and water do not consume, a vain oath consumes. For the Oath is the Artisan, and everything depends on the hand of the Artisan, as it says, "shall swear by the God of Truth (*Amen*)" and "I was beside Him as an artisan (*Amon*)." You already know this great secret: that the secret of the Oath is the secret of **El Chai** <term>El Chai: "The Living God," a name associated with the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation)</term> and the secret of **"that it was good"** <note>Hebrew: *Ki Tov*, the phrase used during the days of Creation</note>. Therefore, the Sages said regarding all creatures made during the Acts of Creation: "And God saw that it was good." The sign for this is "I was beside Him as an artisan (*Amon*)." The secret of "And I was" (*V’ehyeh*) is the number seven <note>The letter *Vav* (6) plus the concept of the unity</note> attached to the Name *Ehyeh* ("I Will Be"), which is the secret of the six Sefirot, and the last of the six is the secret of "that it was good." Therefore, all the actions that God—who is *Adonai*—performed during the Acts of Creation...

# Gate 2

->With the Seventh. And every oath is dependent on the Seventh. And the secret is: "And on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed" <note>Exodus 31:17; the Hebrew word for "refreshed," *vayinafash*, shares a root with *nefesh*, or soul</note>.<-

<margin>1</margin> Therefore, one who swears an oath swears by the "Soul" and by "Life," as when he says: "I swear by the name of the Lord" <note>original: *Adonai*</note>. The secret of this is "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives" <note>1 Samuel 20:3</note>. For the secret of "as your soul lives" is the mystery of the **Living God** <term>Hebrew: *El Hai*; a name associated with the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation), which is the source of vital energy</term> from whom life is drawn, as are all the souls that fly forth from the "land of the Lord." This is as it is said: "Let the earth bring forth a living soul according to its kind" <note>Genesis 1:24</note>. This is the secret of the Sabbath, which is the mystery of the **Seventh Day** from which the life of the soul is drawn. As it is said: <margin>2</margin> "And on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed." Thus, the life of the soul is suspended from the "Seventh," which is the secret of the **Oath** <term>The Hebrew words for "Seven" (*Sheva*) and "Oath" (*Shevu'ah*) share the same root, implying that an oath is an invocation of the seven lower Sefirot</term>. 

Anyone who denies their oath is as if they have denied the Living God and the **seven Sefirot** <term>The ten divine emanations; here referring to the lower seven that govern the created world</term> which are the mystery of the "Seven Days of the World." If, in their great transgression and deceit, they deny these "Sevens," from where will they receive life and goodness? For the world was only created through these seven Sefirot, and through them all created beings are sustained for seven days, according to the mystery of the seven Sefirot and the mystery of the Oath. If, God forbid, a person should lie in their oath, they are uprooted from these seven Sefirot which are the secret of their existence; thus, they are uprooted from the world. 

You have therefore learned that an oath is by the **Living God**, which is the mystery of the Seventh, which is the mystery of the Sabbath, which is the mystery of the life of the soul, which is the mystery of "He rested and was refreshed." Because an oath is by the Living God, the verse says: "He held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and swore by Him that lives forever" <note>Daniel 12:7</note>. Do you not see that the oath is by "Him that lives forever," which is the Living God? In other places it says: "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand" <note>1 Kings 17:1</note>; "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you" <note>2 Kings 2:2</note>; and "As your soul lives, my lord" <note>1 Samuel 1:26</note>. 

<margin>3</margin> According to the Sages of blessed memory, an oath is like swearing by the King. Therefore, one does not swear to nullify the Torah or any of its commandments. If one does swear [to break a commandment], they are lashed [for the false oath] but must still fulfill the commandment, <margin>4</margin> because an oath cannot take effect to cancel the words of the Torah. This is because the words of the Torah are the mystery of the **Seven Voices** <note>The voices heard at Mount Sinai</note> that emerged from the seven Sefirot during the giving of the Torah. A person cannot swear to cancel the words of the Torah. 

<margin>5</margin> Every oath is "by the Lord" (*b'Adonai*) and every **vow** is "to the Lord" (*l'Adonai*). The secret of "a vow to the Lord" will still be explained in its place with God's help, for a **vow** <term>Hebrew: *Neder*</term> is the secret of the "Great Sabbath," which is the mystery of the **Higher Seventh** <term>Referring to the Sefirah of Binah (Understanding), which is "above" the lower seven</term>. If you find it written: "who swore *to* the Lord" <note>Psalm 132:2</note> and it does not say "swore *by* the Lord," the explanation of the verse is that King David, peace be upon him, swore to *do* this thing for the Lord—meaning he would not be quiet or rest until he found a resting place for the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) to build the Holy Temple. Thus, you can say that for anyone who denies their oath, the **Seven Days of Creation** (which are the secret of all the days of the world) become like enemies and seekers of their harm. For when they denied the oath, they denied the "Seven," and when they denied the Seven Days of Creation, every single day of the seven days [becomes their adversary].

<note>Commentary in Rashi script</note>

Regarding the writing concerning His name, the Torah is called thus because it is dependent on the "Oath," which is the **Foundation** (*Yesod*), the purpose of the oath and its totality. The power of the **Crown** (*Atarah/Malkhut*) is placed within the totality of the Foundation of the oath, for it is the seventh of the [lower] structure. <margin>1</margin> Therefore, the one who swears, swears by the Soul and by Life, because the Soul is included in the word "Life," as will be explained. <margin>2</margin> "And on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed": for this attachment to this word [Life] is what sustains and elevates his soul to its higher degree, both in life and after death, as was explained above in the explanation of the Sabbath. <margin>3</margin> Therefore the Sages said: "One who swears, swears by the King." For the **Foundation** (*Yesod*) is called "King" after the name of **Beauty** (*Tiferet*), who is the King to the Queen (the Crown), and he is the essence of the oath and the King. You already know that Foundation and Beauty are two that are one, and their names are one. <margin>4</margin> An oath does not take effect to cancel a commandment because all the words of the Torah and its commandments were given in the mystery of the Seven Voices that emerged from the seven Sefirot. Therefore, a man does not swear to cancel the words of Torah because they themselves are within the mystery of the Oath, and a thing cannot cancel itself. A thing can only be canceled by something that precedes it and is higher than it. This is the reason that a **vow** (*Neder*) *can* take effect upon a matter of a commandment, for the vow ascends to a place higher than the oath, as will be explained. <margin>5</margin> "Every oath is *by* the Lord and every vow is *to* the Lord": In this explanation, he wants to clarify the difference between an oath and a vow. He says the oath is "by" the Lord, meaning in the seven Sefirot which are included in the Holy Name. But the vow ascends above the Name to **Understanding** (*Binah*). This is why it says "his soul is still in its place," for the mystery of "a vow to the Lord" is in its place in the form of the Name of the one who swears. The name of *Binah* was explained there, for the vow is dependent on it. So too later in the Third Gate. Therefore the verse says: "If a man makes a vow *to* the Lord" <note>Numbers 30:3</note> and not "*by* the Lord," as it says in every place where an oath by the Name is mentioned. This hint is divided into a thing that is "to" Him (the Lord) and not "in/by" Him. Since all oaths are below *Binah*—which is called "Seven"—and they are a structure included in another, he mentions that which is added below it, and if so, it must be explained by that which is above it.

# Gate 2

God was always consulting and contemplating the Work of Creation <term>Hebrew: *Ma'aseh Bereshit*; the secrets of how the world was made</term> with "it is good." This is why it says regarding every single thing, "And God saw that **it was good**." Based on this principle, you should contemplate the secret of "And I was beside Him as a confidant" <note>Proverbs 8:30; original: *Amun*</note>, which is the mystery of ## **The Nurtured**, ## **The Nurturer**, **and the Truth** <note>The Hebrew root A-M-N is polysemic here: *Amun* (nurtured), *Omen* (architect/nurturer), and *Amen* (truth/faith)</note>. This is the secret of "Good" <note>The Hebrew word for "Good," *Tov*, has a numerical value of 17, often linked to spiritual light</note> and the secret of the **Oath**. Therefore, all "sevenths" are linked to the Seventh, which is the collective of the seven, and this is the mystery of the Oath <note>The Hebrew words for "Seven" (*Sheva*) and "Oath" (*Shevu'ah*) share the same root</note>.

Know and believe that no creature has any existence in the world except through the One, Blessed be He, by means of these seven Sefirot. When a person swears falsely in an oath, they are uprooted from all seven Sefirot, and no root remains for them in either the heavens or the earth. This is what the Sages meant regarding one who swears falsely: "it shall enter into his house... and consume it with its timber and its stones" <note>Zechariah 5:4</note>, for everything is uprooted, root and branch.

<margin>1</margin> Now, my son, hear this and contemplate the gravity of the oath and its punishment. For even uttering the Name of Heaven from one's mouth in vain—even if one does not swear an oath—results in punishment; how much more so for one who swears falsely. May the Lord save us from this punishment and send us forgiveness and atonement for all the ways we have transgressed in this.

Because the matter of the oath is the mystery of the seven Sefirot—out of the ten Sefirot included in His Blessed Name—it is said in the Torah: "And by His name you shall swear," for everything depends upon His Name. <margin>2</margin> "And everyone who swears in the land shall swear by the God of Truth" <note>Isaiah 65:16; original: *Elohei Amen*</note>. Therefore, the Sages of blessed memory said: "An oath is like swearing by the King Himself." The mystery of the oath is comprised of the "Seven," as it is written: "She has hewn out her seven pillars" <note>Proverbs 9:1</note>. And it is written: "And he called it *Shebah* (Seven/Oath); <margin>3</margin> therefore the name of the city is **Beersheba** (Well of the Seven/Oath)." And it is written: "Therefore he called that place Beersheba, because there the two of them swore an oath."

<margin>3</margin> And this attribute is called in the language of the Torah a **Statute** <term>Hebrew: *Chok*; literally something "engraved"</term>. Now I must enlighten your eyes in this matter: <margin>4</margin> Know that the Lord, Blessed be He, engraved all formed things and suspended their boundary and their measure in His Great Name. He gave an end and a boundary to all created things in the world. All creatures, upper and lower, have an end and a limit, but for His Great Name, there is no end or limit. As it says: "He sets an end to darkness, and searches out every limit" <note>Job 28:3</note>. And it says: "I have seen an end to all perfection, but Your commandment is exceedingly broad" <note>Psalm 119:96</note>.

The explanation of this verse is as follows: Every single thing among all created beings has a boundary and an end. However, that attribute called **Commandment** <term>Hebrew: *Mitzvah*</term>—which is the mystery of the Tenth Sefirah <note>Malchut (Kingship/Sovereignty), the final emanation through which the divine reaches our world</note> of His Great Name, being the first from the bottom up and the last from the top down—is called *Mitzvah* and has no boundary, for it is "exceedingly broad." She is the one who oversees all creatures and gives them their measure. The reason she is called *Mitzvah* is that all matters of the Bottom World are carried out through her, and by her command, all creatures in the world are guided. This is the secret of "The Torah and the Commandment": the "Torah" refers to the **Written Torah**, and the "Commandment" refers to the **Oral Torah**. For we must conduct ourselves in the Written Torah according to the command of the Lord <note>original: *Adonai*</note>, who is called *Mitzvah* and is called the Oral Torah. Therefore, the verse says: "I have seen an end to all perfection, but Your commandment is exceedingly broad."

Know and understand that all the "engravings" mentioned in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: *Sefer Yetzirah*; an early and influential mystical text</note> which the Lord, Blessed be He, engraved into the Work of Creation, were all engraved through the **Living God** <note>original: *El Hai*</note> and **Lord** <note>original: *Adonai*</note>. Through these two Names, He gave an end and a boundary to every created thing and a known measure, so that they should not go beyond their boundary or change their function. All of this is included in the word "Statute" <note>original: *Chok*</note> and "Decree" <note>original: *Chukkah*</note> of the Living God and Lord, by which all creatures were engraved and limited so as not to exceed their boundaries. This is the secret hinted at in the Psalm: "Praise the Lord from the heavens," where after mentioning all creatures, upper and lower, it says: "Let them praise the name of the Lord, for He commanded and they were created. He has established them forever and ever; He has given a **statute** which shall not be passed."

# Gate 2

For every single action, let us seek counsel in that which is "good." On the first day of creation, what is written? "And God saw the light, that it was **good**." On the second day, however, "it was good" was not said, because the second day is the mystery of division and separation, as it is said: "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between waters and waters." Wherever there is division and separation, "good" is not found, for "good" only comes to bring peace and to unite all things. Therefore, when "Good"—which is the mystery of the **Living God** <note>Hebrew: *El Chai*, a name associated with the Sefirah of *Yesod* (Foundation)</note> and the attribute of **Adonai** <note>The name for God often associated with the Shekhinah or the physical world</note>—is removed, separated, or distanced, <margin>1</margin> then the entire world is desolate and "good" is not present in the world, as it is said: "The righteous one is gathered away because of evil" <note>Isaiah 57:1</note>. And it is said: "Say of the righteous one, that he is **good**" <note>Isaiah 3:10</note>. Therefore, when the Righteous One <term>Hebrew: *Tzadik*; refers to the Sefirah of *Yesod*, which balances the divine flow</term> is present in the world, he establishes peace between two disputing parties; the Righteous One is found to be the deciding factor.

This is the mystery of the "two verses that contradict one another until a third verse comes and decides between them" <note>A fundamental principle of Rabbinic logic used here to explain divine balance</note>. The secret is that **Endurance** <note>Hebrew: *Netzach*</note> is on the right and **Glory** <note>Hebrew: *Hod*</note> is on the left; the "Good" Righteous One is the third force that decides between them. For this reason, "it was good" was not said on the second day, but on the third day it was said twice: "it was **good**" <margin>2</margin>. The reason is that the first "good" corresponds to the Living God <note>*El Chai* / *Yesod*</note>, and the second "good" corresponds to **Adonai**, which is the mystery of the "Lord of the Earth" <note>The Shekhinah</note>. The sign of this is the verse "Say of the Righteous One, that he is good." Furthermore, we say in the Blessing After Meals: "A land that is desirable and **good**."

This secret is that God is included in every act of creation, and "good" is in every single thing, for it is the secret of the **Craftsman** <term>Hebrew: *Uman*; the divine architect</term>. In the separation of things, "good" is not found except at the moment of their union. Do you not see that when the first man, Adam, was alone and separated without the union of his partner, what was written of him? "It is **not good** for man to be alone." But when he was united with his wife, what was written? "He who finds a wife finds **good**"—meaning he found that "good" which had been lost to him. If this is true of a man and a woman, how much more so regarding the other supernal levels? For in the moment of union, "it was good" is found, but in the moment of separation, "it was good" is not found.

In this way, know that the three Sefirot—**Endurance** (*Netzach*), **Glory** (*Hod*), and **Good** (*Tov*)—are always united. Endurance and Glory stand over against one another, and "Good" is the third "verse" that decides between them. According to this secret, you will find that "Good" is the lower root of the letter *Vav* <note>The letter *Vav* has the numerical value of 6 and represents the central pillar of the Sefirot</note>, which is the middle line and the third element. <margin>3</margin> How so? The *Vav* is the secret of the six Sefirot: three above and three below. The three above follow this path: **Greatness** <note>Hebrew: *Gedulah* or *Chesed* (Kindness)</note> is on the right side and **Strength** <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note> is on the left side, and **Beauty** <note>Hebrew: *Tiferet*</note> is the third that decides between them. The three below follow this path: **Endurance** (*Netzach*) is on the right side, **Glory** (*Hod*) is on the left side, and **Good** (*Tov*) is the third that decides between them.

Therefore, you will find the concept of "Good" dwelling upon **Adonai**, which is the final Sefirah of the ten Sefirot, <margin>4</margin> and she is called **The Good Mountain**. When "Good" dwells within *Adonai*, she is called **The Good Land**, named after the "Good" that dwells within her. This is the secret of "And you shall bless the Lord your God for the **good land** which He has given you," and the secret of "you shall lack nothing in it," and it is written: "those who seek the Lord shall lack no **good**." Because the Lord is clothed in the garment of Strength in the attribute of *Elohim* <note>The name of God associated with Justice and Law</note> and performed all the work of creation...

<margin>1</margin> When the "Living One" is removed, the entire world is desolate and "good" is not found in the world. Since the second day was for the repair of the world and its surrounding, "it was good" is not written there, for the collective state—being in a state of the world's mixing—certainly does not have "good" present in it.

<margin>2</margin> The reason is that the first "good" corresponds to the Living God (*El Chai*), and the second "good" corresponds to the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*), which is the secret of the Earth. For on that third day, the dry land was revealed and called by the name "Earth," as it is written: "Let the waters be gathered... and let the dry land appear," and He called the dry land "Earth." Therefore, it is also called the "Good Land."

<margin>3</margin> How so? The *Vav* is the secret of the six Sefirot, three above and three below, for it spreads to every side... as will be explained later in Gate 5. We will yet explain, with God's help, the "Gift of the Manna" <note>Hebrew: *Matan la-Man*</note> by way of the abundance of the Altar. This means that the "Manna" is the secret of the Altar's abundance from all the Sefirot, as explained later in Gate 3.

<margin>4</margin> And it is called **The Good Mountain** because it was always high and exalted above the level of *Adonai*. Based on this principle, contemplate the secret of "And I was beside Him as a confidant" <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>. This refers to the **Nurturer**, the **Nurtured**, and the **Truth** <note>Hebrew: *Omen*, *Amun*, *Emun*</note>, for the six Sefirot are attached to the *Shekhinah*... they are the craftsmen/nurturers of the world, its life, and its greatness as it is revealed to us.

Regarding every single action of creation, we find consultation with "it was good." On the first day, what is written? "And God saw the light, that it was good" <note>Genesis 1:4</note>. There are things that the Tempter <note>original: *Yetzer*; the internal impulse toward doubt or evil</note> challenges and the nations of the world mock. This is the secret of the verse: "My judgments you shall do and my statutes <note>original: *chukotai*</note> you shall keep to walk in them, I am the Lord" <note>Leviticus 18:4</note>. Therefore, wherever you find in the Torah the term "Statute" <note>original: *Chok* or *Chukah*</note>, it refers to a mystery that you are worthy to receive and fulfill, but you have no right to question that commandment or step outside the boundary of divine perception. 

Because the meaning of what is called "Statutes" lies in "Engraving" <note>original: *chakikah*; a play on the word *Chok*</note>, and this is the secret of "My statutes you shall keep." You find this regarding the Passover in Egypt: "And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel," and it says of this: "And you shall observe this thing for a statute <note>original: *chok*</note> to you and to your sons" <note>Exodus 12:22-24</note>. So too with the Scapegoat: "And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you," and with the Red Heifer: "This is the statute of the Torah."

He told us to fulfill them and not to question them, nor to go outside the boundary of perception. He said: "Thus far shall you come to contemplate, and no further," just as He said to the waves of the sea: "Thus far shall you come, and no further" <note>Job 38:11</note>. <meta>This page continues the exploration of the term "Statute" (Chok) and its relationship to divine boundaries. While the previous page established that "Statutes" are commandments beyond human questioning, this page delves into the linguistic and kabbalistic roots of the word, linking it to specific Divine Names—specifically El Chai (the Living God) and Adonai (The Lord)—and the structural balance of the Sefirot.</meta>

### Gate 2
<meta>catchword: things</meta>

"He gave a law that shall not pass" <note>Psalm 148:6</note>. And it says, "The statutes of heaven and earth" <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note>. Regarding the blessing of the New Moon, our Sages of blessed memory said: "By His word, He created the heavens, and by the breath of His mouth, all their host; He gave them a statute and a time so that they should not change their duty." It also says, "Who gives the sun for light by day, and the statutes of the moon and stars for light by night" <note>Jeremiah 31:34</note>. This means the boundary of the day and the boundary of the night are within the mystery of the "Attribute of Day" and the "Attribute of Night." 

It is also said: "Do you not fear Me? says the Lord. Will you not tremble before Me? For I have placed the sand as a bound for the sea, an eternal statute that it cannot pass" <note>Jeremiah 5:22</note>. And it says, "You set a boundary they may not pass, so they do not return to cover the earth" <note>Psalm 104:9</note>. Behold, in every place where you find the language of "Statute" <note>original: *Chok*</note>, it refers to the concept of the boundary and the measure of all things. 

Similarly, it says: "And they ate their portion <note>original: *chukam*</note> which Pharaoh gave them" <note>Genesis 47:22</note>, and "Feed me with my allotted bread <note>original: *lechem chuki*</note>" <note>Proverbs 30:8</note>. Because all created things were engraved <note>original: *nitkakku*</note> into their various kinds and boundaries through these two *Sefirot* <note>divine emanations</note>, the Holy One, blessed be He, found it necessary to place them in the Torah with specific signs: sometimes using the masculine term *Chok* (Statute) and sometimes the feminine term *Chukah* (Decree).

Wherever you find the term *Chok*, it refers to the attribute of **El Chai** <note>The Living God; associated with the Sefirah of Yesod, the "Foundation"</note>. Therefore, it is the "deciding factor in the middle," acting as a third biblical principle. This is what is meant in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an ancient mystical text</note>: "The tongue of the statute decides in the middle." Just as the tongue is in the center of all the body’s limbs, it is called *Chok*, and the attribute of *El Chai* is called *Chok*. 

This is the secret of the verse: "Blow the horn at the new moon, at the concealed time for our feast day. For it is a statute <note>original: *Chok*</note> for Israel, a judgment <note>original: *Mishpat*</note> for the God of Jacob" <note>Psalm 81:4-5</note>. I have already informed you that this refers to the Day of Remembrance <note>Rosh Hashanah</note>, within the mystery of "Remember us for life." Know that "Judgment" <note>*Mishpat*</note> is the mystery of **Tiferet** <note>the Sefirah of "Beauty" or "Harmony"</note>, the mystery of Jacob, and the mystery of the letter *Vav* in the Divine Name <note>the Y-H-V-H</note>. *Chok* is the lower tip of that *Vav*, which is the mystery of Judgment and Jacob. As we mentioned earlier, the tip of that *Vav* is called a "small *Yud*." 

Therefore, it says "a statute for Israel is a judgment for the God of Jacob," and it is written elsewhere, "There He set for them a statute and a judgment" <note>Exodus 15:25</note>. From within the *Chok*—which is *El Chai*, the Day of Remembrance—man enters into judgment on this day. 

Furthermore, you will find many commandments in the Torah marked as *Chok* and many marked as *Chukah*. The explanation is this: wherever you find the term *Chok*, it is a sign that the commandment is attached to *El Chai*. For example, regarding the Passover in Egypt: "And you shall observe this thing as a statute <note>original: *le-chok*</note> for you and your children" <note>Exodus 12:24</note>. This applies wherever *Chok* emerges from the attribute of *El Chai*. In the blessing for Circumcision <note>Brit Milah</note>, which is also the mystery of *El Chai*, we say: "Blessed are You... who sanctified the beloved from the womb and placed a statute <note>original: *v'chok*</note> in his flesh, and sealed his offspring with the sign of the holy covenant."

Wherever the term *Chukah* is found, it is a sign that the commandment is attached to the name **Adonai** <note>The Lord; associated with the Sefirah of Malchut, "Sovereignty"</note>, such as: "And you shall keep this decree <note>original: *ha-chukah*</note> in its season from year to year" <note>Exodus 13:10</note>, or "This is the decree of the Torah" <note>Numbers 19:2</note>, and all similar cases.

Thus, you have learned that the terms *Chok* and *Chukah* are signs for **El Chai** and **Adonai**. They represent the "Attribute of Day" and the "Attribute of Night," as well as "Remember" and "Observe" <note>the two aspects of the Sabbath</note>. 

Now, you should know that wherever the Torah says "Statutes" <note>plural: *Chukim*</note>, it is a sign of *Chok*, as in: "Righteous statutes <note>original: *chukim*</note> and judgments." Wherever it says "Decrees" <note>plural: *Chukot*</note>, it is a sign of *Chukah*, as in: "If you walk in My decrees <note>original: *chukotai*</note>." However, when it mentions *Chukim* in the plural, both *El Chai* and *Adonai* are included within them. The same is true for *Chukot*. 

What then is the difference between *Chukim* and *Chukot*? Know that *Chukim* refers to the mystery of *El Chai* first, including *Adonai* within it from above to below. *Chukot* refers to the mystery of *Adonai* first, including *El Chai* within it from below to above. Meditate on this great principle.

Having informed you of this, we must now explain why some commandments are called *Chukim* or *Chukot*. We have already noted that the term *Chok* refers to the mystery of "investigating" <note>original: *chakirah*</note> things, their measures, and their boundaries, and the fact that they cannot exceed their limits. Likewise, all commandments called *Chukim* or *Chukot* are very hidden and sealed. The Torah expressed them using the language of "Statute" to tell us that we must fulfill them without wondering about their reasons. We must keep the "statute" of the boundary of our wondering and our thought, and not step outside the limits of human contemplation. This is why they are called *Chukim* and *Chukot*. Our Sages of blessed memory already revealed this in the Talmud, saying: "My decrees <note>original: *chukotai*</note> you shall keep..."

It emphasizes that these "irrational" laws are designed to keep human inquiry within its proper limits.</summary>

As written in Gate 9, the name is **The Lord God of Hosts**, for there the **Might** <note>Gevurah</note> and **Vengeance** are clothed, as will be integrated further in Gate 30. **E** "Stretched forth his hand against his covenant of peace"—this refers to how he wanted to reveal his hand to snatch and rob the flow descending from the **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note> to the **Kingdom** <note>Malchut</note>... as it says in the Midrash, they were "cutting off" the sign of the covenant <note>circumcision</note> and throwing it upward. Regarding this, it is said "his covenant of peace" according to everything I have written. **F** And they are the carriers of the **Throne of the Chariot**. The **Throne of ADNY** consists of the **Four Living Creatures** that Ezekiel saw: the face of a Lion on the right, the face of an Ox on the left, etc. This is the **Chariot of the Kingdom**... which will appear in the "Book of the System" in the "Gate of the Kingdom." In the explanation of the Kingdom, it is written that these four camps, these four Living Creatures, stand at the four corners of the Divine Presence...

# Gate 2

The Name designated as **ADNY** <note>original: "Adonai," the Name associated with the Sefirah of Malkhut</note>. Because everything depends upon this divine attribute, it is called **Kol** <note>meaning "All" or "Everything"</note>. Sometimes the Tenth Attribute, which is my Lord (**ADNY**), is called by the term "All" in honor of this quality. Regarding this mystery, it is said: "I am the Lord, Maker of **all**, who stretched out the heavens alone..." <note>Isaiah 44:24</note>. For by the power of this attribute, heaven, earth, and all the hosts above and below were created. The mystery of the phrase "And the heavens were finished" <note>original: "Vayechulu," Genesis 2:1</note> is that "finished" shares the root of "All" (*Kol*). The great mystery of the **Sabbath** is that it is the secret of "All," and it includes two divine attributes within the mystery of **Remember** and **Observe** <note>original: "Zachor ve-Shamor," the two commands regarding Sabbath which represent the union of male and female divine aspects</note>. This is the secret of "And the heavens and the earth were finished" and "God finished on the seventh day."

The three Patriarchs inherited this attribute of **All** (*Kol*) through the mystery of "Remember" and "Observe." Regarding **Abraham**, it is written: "And the Lord blessed Abraham in **all** things" <note>Genesis 24:1</note>. Regarding **Isaac**, it is written: "And I have eaten of **all**" <note>Genesis 27:33</note>. Regarding **Jacob**, it is written: "Because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have **all**" <note>Genesis 33:11</note>. Concerning this, David, peace be upon him, said: "Therefore I esteem **all** Your precepts concerning **all** things to be right" <note>Psalm 119:128</note>.

Because this attribute is the seventh <margin>A</margin> relative to the Sefirah of **Binah** <note>Understanding; Malkhut is the seventh emanation if counting from Chesed downwards</note>, as we have said—and since the Sefirah of **Binah** possesses **fifty gates**—from those fifty gates of **Binah**, the **Living God** <note>original: "El Chai," often associated with the Sefirah of Yesod</note> is nourished. Therefore, it is called by the term "All" (*Kol*), because everything is drawn from there. Thus, the numerical value (**Gematria**) of **Kol** (כ"ל) is **fifty** <note>Kaph = 20, Lamed = 30</note>, for all things found among the created beings emerged from the fifty gates of **Binah**. The sign for all created things is "All" (*Kol*). This is the great mystery: "And God saw **all** that He had made, and behold, it was very **good**" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>.

We have already informed you that this attribute is called **All**. I must awaken you to a subtle, inner mystery: Know that when the attributes of **Remember** and **Observe** are united, the whole world is in a state of fullness and perfection. This is the mystery of "He has made **everything** (*et ha-kol*) beautiful in its **time** (*be-ito*)" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:11</note>. For the attribute of "Remember" is called "All" (*Kol*) and the attribute of "Observe" is called "**Time**" (*Et*). When "Remember" and "Observe" are unified as one in the mystery of "All" and "Time," then one says "He has made the **All** beautiful," and the mystery of "In its time" <note>Hebrew: "be-et"</note> ends with the letter **Vav** <note>original: "be-et v'" - referencing the divine Name</note.

Know that there are times for good and times for evil. Solomon, peace be upon him, already revealed this mystery when he said: "A **time** to give birth..." <note>Ecclesiastes 3:2</note>. There is likewise a "**Time of Favor**" and a "**Time of Evil**," as <term>our Sages of blessed memory</term> taught in the chapter *Chelek*. I shall now reveal the mystery to you: Know that the attribute of **ADNY** is called "**Time**" (*Et*). When it is connected to the **Righteous One** <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> who is called "**Good**" (*Tov*), then it is a **Good Time** (*Et Tovah*), for "Good" is joined with "Time." But if, God forbid, "Good" is separated from "Time," then it joins with "Time" in another matter that sits outside the Sefirot and is called "**Evil**" (*Ra*). This is the mystery of the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil**. We have already explained this regarding the Tree of Knowledge: it is the attribute of **ADNY** as perceived through this quality, and everything is according to Law, Straightness, and the Judgment of Truth. Solomon revealed this at the end of Ecclesiastes: "For God shall bring **every** deed into judgment, with **every** secret thing, whether it be **good** or whether it be **evil**."

Following this path, <term>our Sages of blessed memory</term> said: "A person is obligated to bless God for the evil just as he blesses Him for the good." This is the mystery of what was said: "Speak to Aaron your brother, that he come not at **all times** (*be-khol et*) into the holy place" <note>Leviticus 16:2</note>. What is meant by "at all times"? It means: do not enter during any "time" that is a **Time of Evil**, when the things called "evil" are attached to the "Time," or perhaps that "time" belongs to those external times called "Times of Impurity." For there are several "external times" outside the **Pargod** <note>the Celestial Curtain/Veil</note>, and each of them is prepared for punishment. These too are included in "he shall not come at all times into the holy place." And at what "Time" is it proper for him to enter? With "**This**" (*Zot*). <meta>The catchword at the bottom is "Yavo" (He shall come).</meta>

***

...the attribute of **Justice** (*Tzedek*) as is proper. For the Heavenly Jerusalem has... for the good ones in the earthly Jerusalem, etc. This is the reason it is written: "Jerusalem that is built..." As long as the exile continues, the "Remembrance" is the Tenth... until the inner part of the Moon is renewed speedily in our days, Amen. <insert>Note:</insert> Up to the Sefirah of **Binah**, as we explained above in the explanation of the Sabbath. The doubling of **Binah** contains 50 gates. These are the **Fifty Gates of Binah** that are included in everything. This is the study found in the tradition of the Kabbalists: a gate for each... a gate for the offspring... a gate for the birds... a gate for the fish... This rises until the inclusion of the "Crowning" (*Kippah*), from which the words of the Kippah and from there to the Prophets... for in each of them is a gate of Wisdom and Understanding in their essence. The power of his wisdom is like the wisdom of his companion. Their number is traditionally received... our teacher (Moses), peace be upon him, except for one. It is possible that this gate remains in the knowledge of the Creator alone, as the commentator explained. If you look at these inclusions, they are for the most part... that is, the last gate was not mentioned. From the commentary of <term>Nachmanides</term> <note>original: "Ha-Ramban," 13th-century sage and mystic</note>. # Gate 2

<margin>The author says</margin> Saviors—who are the Lord God of Hosts—shall be upon Mount Zion, which is the mystery of the Living God <note>Hebrew: *El Chai*, a Name associated with the emanation of Yesod</note>, to judge the Mount of Esau, which is Mount Seir. "And the Lord will punish the host of the high heaven on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth" <note>Isaiah 24:21</note>. And then, "For my sword shall be bathed in heaven," and afterward, "behold, it shall come down upon Edom" <note>Isaiah 34:5</note>. When this occurs, what is written? "Who is this that comes from Edom, with crimsoned garments from Bozrah? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save" <note>Isaiah 63:1</note>, following the mystery of "And saviors shall come up on Mount Zion" <note>Obadiah 1:21</note>. In this way, he said that Mount Zion is called "The Mountain of the Lord" when Mount Zion and Mount Moriah are joined **[Annotation Ayin]** in the mystery of "And Abraham called the name of that place 'The-Lord-Will-See,' as it is said to this day, 'In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen'" <note>Genesis 22:14</note>. The standing of Mount Moriah was established through the emanation <term>Atzilut<gloss>The process by which divine light flows from the Source into specific attributes</gloss></term> of Mount Zion **[Annotation Aleph]** in the abundance of blessing. Therefore He said, "By myself have I sworn, says the Lord, for because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son... that in blessing I will bless you, and in multiplying I will multiply your seed" <note>Genesis 22:16–17</note>.

Therefore, wherever you find "Who **[Annotation Bet]** shall ascend the mountain of the Lord" <note>Psalm 24:3</note>, it refers to the mystery of Zion in its union with Jerusalem. "The mountain of the Lord’s house" is the mystery of Mount Moriah and Jerusalem in union. Sometimes this divine attribute is called **Zion** **[Annotation Gimel]**. The matter of Zion and Jerusalem represents the mystery of the Living God (*El Chai*) and my Lord (*Adonai*), the mystery of "Remember" and "Observe" <note>The dual aspects of the Sabbath, representing the male and female divine principles</note>. From within Zion—which represents the [first] nine emanations <term>Sefirot<gloss>The ten creative powers or attributes of God in Kabbalah</gloss></term>—the Name **[Annotation Ayin]** dwells in Jerusalem, which is the mystery of the tenth emanation below. As it is said: "Blessed be the Lord out of Zion, who dwells at Jerusalem" <note>Psalm 135:21</note>. And it says: "As the dew of Hermon that descended upon the mountains of Zion," for from there the blessing is drawn down to Jerusalem and to all the worl**d**.

We have already informed you that "Living God" (*El Chai*) is the conclusion of the nine emanations from top to bottom <note>Referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, and it is that which pours blessing into the Name *Adonai* <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut</note>. Likewise, when the righteous ones (*Tzadikim*) are found in the world **[Annotation Dalet]**, the Lord (may He be blessed) joins together and emanates His blessings below. And through whom? Through Zion. As it says: "Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God has shined" <note>Psalm 50:2</note>.

But if, God forbid, Israel acts improperly, what is written? "The righteous man is gathered [perishes] because of the evil" <note>Isaiah 57:1</note>. And the "Righteous" (*Tzadik*) is the Attribute of Judgment <note>Here, the author suggests the channel of blessing becomes a channel of strict accountability</note>. And it says: "The righteous is the foundation (*Yesod*) of the world" <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. When the attribute of the "Righteous One" is withdrawn, then Mount Zion is destroyed. What is written regarding the departure of the "Living God" from Mount Zion? "Because of the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, the foxes walk upon it" <note>Lamentations 5:18</note>. Who are the "foxes" that walk upon it? They are the other forces of impurity, called "the little foxes that spoil the vineyards" <note>Song of Songs 2:15</note>. Who are the "vineyards"? They are the "Vineyards of Hosts."

However, in the future to come, what is written? "And saviors shall come up on Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s" <note>Obadiah 1:21</note>. Then Jerusalem and Zion will be joined as one, for Jerusalem is the City of the Kingdom—and this is the meaning of "and the kingdom shall be the Lord's." This is the mystery of "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem" <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>. When the emanations return to their proper repair <term>Tikkun<gloss>Restoration or rectification of the divine order</gloss></term>, what is written? "And they shall come who were lost in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem" <note>Isaiah 27:13</note>. "In the holy mount"—this is Mount Zion. "At Jerusalem"—this is the City of the Kingdom.

The mystery <note>original: *Remez*, a hint or allegorical secret</note> of who these "lost ones" are is found in the verse: "The righteous man is lost (*avad*)." And what did he lose? He lost "Justice" (*Tzedek*), and therefore "the lost ones shall come." The "Righteous" (*Tzadik*) is lost to "Justice" (**Annotation Ayin**), and the "Righteous" is lost to the "Righteous." This is why it says "those who were lost (*obadim*)" and not "those who were destroyed." These are called the Holy Mountain in Jerusalem. Based on this essential principle, the Sages established in the prayer: "Who restores His Presence (*Shekhinah*) to Zion," based on the secret of "Blessed is He who restores a lost item to its owner."

Now that we have awakened you to these essential principles, know that this attribute—since it is an attribute belonging to the Patriarchs, and through it they entered the "Table" to each receive their portion in the Divine Chariot—contains all types of flow and emanation coming from all nine Sefirot. Therefore, it is also called by the term **All** (*Kol*). This is because this attribute draws from all the higher emanations every kind of flow and brings them into

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the divine emanations (Sefirot), transitioning from the discussion of Mount Zion to the lower triad of the spiritual structure—Netzach (Victory), Hod (Splendor), and Yesod (Foundation). It explains the title "Mighty One of Israel" and categorizes the different levels of Divine Kindness (Chesed).</meta>

# Gate 2

->In the secret of the Lord of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel.<-

You already know that the three lower <term>Sefirot<gloss>the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Divine is revealed</gloss></term> **[Aleph]** are rooted in the lower foundation: **Victory** <note>Hebrew: Netzach</note>, **Splendor** <note>Hebrew: Hod</note>, and **Foundation** <note>Hebrew: Yesod</note>. Collectively, these three are called "Hosts" <note>Hebrew: Tzeva'ot</note>. When you find Victory on the right, Splendor on the left, and Foundation in the middle—at the level of the "Living God" <note>Hebrew: El Chai</note>, who is the Mighty One of Israel—you will find that the **Mighty One of Israel** mediates between Victory and Splendor. Thus it says: "Behold, the Ark of the Covenant, the Lord of all the earth" <note>Joshua 3:11</note>. The Ark **[Bet]** is called the "Temple" <note>Hebrew: Heikhal</note> because the Name "Lord" <note>Hebrew: Y-H-V-H</note> dwells within it. For this reason, the text says "Mighty One of Jacob" and "Mighty One of Israel," <margin>61 Light</margin> but not "Mighty One of Abraham" or "Mighty One of Isaac." **[Gimel]** This is the "Shield of David" who wages the Great War, and He is the "Lord of all the earth."

Know that from the power of the "Mighty One of Jacob," the "wing of the eagle" is renewed, known through the secret of the verse: "the wing of the stork and the plumage" <note>Job 39:13. The author is connecting the Hebrew word for stork, *Chasida*, to the word for kindness, *Chesed*</note>. The secret of "Does the hawk fly by your wisdom, and spread his wings toward the south?" <note>Job 39:26</note> refers to the secret of the attribute of **Kindness** <note>Hebrew: Chesed</note>. The "stork" <note>Chasida</note> represents the "faithful kindnesses of David." When **Understanding** <note>Hebrew: Binah</note> connects to the "Mighty One of Jacob," then "the hawk flies" **[Dalet]** and spreads its wings toward the south. This is because Understanding is the "seventh attribute" relative to the Mighty One of Jacob. **[He]** "He shall spread his roots by the river" <note>Jeremiah 17:8</note>; when the Mighty One of Jacob connects to the attribute called "Eagle," it is then renewed and filled with all goodness. Regarding this, it is said: "The wing of the stork and the plumage," and "Who satisfies your mouth with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's" <note>Psalm 103:5</note>.

This attribute is called the "Lower Kindness," and you must understand how. Know that there are three types of Kindness:
1. **Supreme Kindness** <note>Chesed Elyon</note>: This comes from the highest source, where there is no mixture of Judgment <note>Din</note>, but only Kindness and Mercy. These are called "Good Kindnesses." The secret is: "My kindness shall not depart from you" <note>Isaiah 54:10</note>. Regarding this, it is said: "For the king trusts in the Lord, and through the kindness of the Most High he shall not be moved" <note>Psalm 21:8</note>.
2. **Worldly Kindness** <note>Chesed Olam</note>: This is the "Kindness of Abraham," as it says: "You give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham" <note>Micah 7:20</note>. However, because the "Fear of Isaac"—which is the secret of the attribute of **Judgment**—is mixed with the Kindness of Abraham, it sometimes withholds the kindness from the side of Judgment. As it says **[Zayin]** "And there was the hiding of His power" <note>Habakkuk 3:4</note>, and it says **[Chet]** "Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy" <note>Exodus 15:6</note>. The Kindness of Abraham is not a "simple" or pure kindness, but is mixed with Judgment. Sometimes the attribute of **Might** <note>Gevurah</note> prevails, and the Kindness of Abraham is hidden within it. Therefore, the Kindness of Abraham is called "Worldly Kindness" because it is sometimes hidden <note>The Hebrew word for world, *Olam*, shares a root with the word for hidden, *Ne'elam*</note> in the secret of the two attributes that govern the world in the secret of "Revealed and Hidden." **[Tet]** This is the secret of "Above and Below," "Right and Left," "Front and Back." Therefore, Worldly Kindness contains both Judgment and Mercy.
3. **The Sure Mercies of David** <note>Chasdei David HaNe’emanim</note>: These are the kindnesses of the "Living God" which come from the power of the "Good Kindnesses" and the "Kindness of Abraham." They are called the "Kindnesses of David" when they reach his attribute, and these kindnesses flow through the "City of David," which is Zion. They are called the "Kindnesses of David" when they reach the Name **Adonai** <note>Lord</note>. This Name is called *Chasida* <note>Stork/Kindness</note> in this context. The sign for this is: "The wing of the stork <note>Chasida</note> and the plumage." Because King David, peace be upon him, would draw the Supreme Kindnesses from above—the "Good Kindnesses" and "Ancient Kindnesses"—the scripture says: "Where are Your ancient kindnesses, O Lord, which You swore to David in Your faithfulness?" <note>Psalm 89:50</note>.

->To Your faithfulness<-

**[Annotations at bottom of page]**

**[Aleph]** He means "Adon" (Lord) in the sense of being close to the Name of God at the completion—meaning **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>. Or perhaps he means **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>, for usually wherever Beauty is mentioned, it is mentioned alongside Foundation, as they are joined.
**[Bet]** The expression "Lord of all the earth" indicates this, for the Sages explained that "Lord of all the earth" refers to the Temple in the Name of God.
**[Gimel]** "Shield of David": This means the protection of David which comes from the attribute called "Kindness of David," and his kindness was also from their influence upon him.
**[Dalet]** "Spreads his wings toward the south": This means that the **Kingship** <note>Malkhut</note> rises and spreads her wings toward the south, which is the attribute of Abraham, and spreads her wings toward him from the hand of the "Mighty One of Jacob."
**[He]** "He shall spread his roots by the river": This refers to the "Living God" reaching the Temple to receive and return from there, for the roots are in the seventh [Sefirah].
**[Vav]** "Then she is changed": Meaning her influence is renewed like the "well-known eagle" which flies and ascends.
**[Zayin]** "And there was the hiding of His power": This is explained later in the gate.
**[Chet]** "Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy": Meaning the enemy shatters those who withhold the Kindness.
**[Tet]** "In the secret of above and below...": All this is explained well later in Gate 5. The cause of the mixture of Judgment is what is below or what is on the side of "The Rivers." Look there and you will understand that the Kindness is always more hidden, and Judgment is revealed.

# Gate 2

<margin>37</margin>
In the secret of the Lord of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel <note>Hebrew: *Abir Yisrael*</note>. You already know that the three lower Sefirot **A** are attached to their root and the lower realm; these are Victory <term>Netzach<gloss>The Sefirah representing endurance and victory</gloss></term>, Splendor <term>Hod<gloss>The Sefirah representing empathy and aesthetic beauty</gloss></term>, and Foundation <term>Yesod<gloss>The Sefirah that funnels divine light into the world</gloss></term>. When
Understanding <term>Binah<gloss>The Sefirah of divine intuition and processing</gloss></term> connects to the Mighty One of Jacob, then the "hawk flies" **D** and "spreads his wings toward the south." For Understanding is the seventh attribute relative to the Mighty One of Isaac.
**E** "He shall spread his roots by the river" <note>Jeremiah 17:8; 'river' here is *Yoval*, associated with the Jubilee</note>. When the Mighty One of Jacob connects to the attribute called "Eagle," it is then renewed and filled
with all goodness. Of this it is said, "the wing of the stork and its feathers," and "Who satisfies your mouth with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's." This attribute is called "Lower Kindness," and you must know why. Know that there are three
types of Kindness. The first is Supreme Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed Elyon*</note>, which comes from the Supernal Source; it contains no mixture of Judgment <term>Din<gloss>The Sefirah of limit, justice, and severity</gloss></term>, but only kindness and mercy. These are called "Good Kindnesses," and the secret is: "My kindness shall not depart from you." Of this it is said, "For the king trusts in the Lord, and through the kindness of the Supreme He shall not be moved." The second is Worldly Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed Olam*</note>, which is the kindness of Abraham, as it is said: "You give truth to Jacob, and kindness to Abraham."
<margin><unclear>Marked</unclear></margin> However, because the "Fear of Isaac"—which is the secret of the attribute of Judgment—is mixed with the Kindness of Abraham, it sometimes hinders the kindness from the side of Judgment, as it says: **G** "And there was the hiding of His power." **H** It also says: "Your right hand, O Lord, dashes the enemy in pieces." The Kindness of Abraham is not a "simple" kindness, but is mixed with Judgment; for sometimes the attribute of Might <term>Gevurah<gloss>The Sefirah of strength and restriction</gloss></term> prevails, and the Kindness of Abraham is hidden within it. Therefore, the Kindness of Abraham is called "Worldly Kindness" <note>or "Hidden Kindness," playing on the Hebrew root *O-L-M*</note>, because it is sometimes hidden within the secret of the two attributes by which the world is led—
in the secret of the revealed and the hidden. **I** In the secret of above and below, right and left, front and back. Therefore, Worldly Kindness contains both Judgment and Mercy. The third type is called "The Sure Mercies of David." These are the kindnesses of the Living God, which come from the power of the "Good Kindnesses" and the "Kindness of Abraham." They are called "Mercies of David" when they reach his attribute, and these kindnesses are drawn down through the City of David, which is Zion. They are called "Mercies of David" when they reach the place of *Adonai* <note>The Name of God associated with the lowest Sefirah, Kingship</term>. *Adonai* is called by the term "Stork" <note>Hebrew: *Chasidah*</note>. The sign is: "The wing of the stork and its feathers." And because King David, peace be upon him, would draw the Supreme Kindnesses from above—which are called "Good Kindnesses" and "Ancient Kindnesses"—the Scripture says: "Lord, where are Your ancient kindnesses, which You swore to David?"

# Gate 2

<meta>catchword: who is called</meta>

"And Aaron shall come into the holy place" <note>Leviticus 16:3</note> through the attribute called "This" <note>original: *Zat* (זאת), a feminine form of "this" often associated with the Sefirah of Malkhut</note>, because the attribute of "This is my God" <note>original: *Zeh Eli* (זה אלי), Exodus 15:2</note>, which is Good, is connected to it. Because it is Good and named after Him, it is called "This." We have already informed you that through the Name <term>Adonai<gloss>The Divine Name associated with the Sefirah of Kingdom/Malkhut, often translated as 'Lord'</gloss></term> it is called a "Time of Favor" <note>original: *Et Ratzon*</note>, for it is the "Time" of Adonai. This is "Justice" <note>original: *Tzedek*</note>, which is the Good that flows from "The Righteous One" <note>original: *Tzaddik*, referring to the Sefirah of Yesod/Foundation</note>. Since all forms of life receive their sustenance and food through her, it is said: "The eyes of all look expectantly to You <gloss>1</gloss> and You give them their food in its time" <note>Psalm 145:15</note>, following the secret of "He has made everything beautiful in its time" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:11</note>.

One who knows how to join the attribute of "Remember" <note>original: *Zakhor*, representing the masculine principle or Tiferet</note> to the attribute of "Observe" <note>original: *Shamor*, representing the feminine principle or Malkhut</note>, regarding him it is said: "Happy are those who maintain justice, who do righteousness at all times" <note>Psalm 106:3</note>. This means that whoever brings the attribute of "Observe" close to "Justice" <note>original: *Mishpat*</note> causes blessings to flow into all things in the world, both within the internal <term>Sefirot<gloss>the ten divine emanations</gloss></term> and the external things that are outside the Sefirot. For when the internal Sefirot are filled with flow and ordered, then all things in the world receive the power of emanation and nobility. This is the secret of "doing righteousness at all times." For how is it possible for a person to literally perform acts of charity/righteousness at every single moment of the day? Rather, the secret of the matter is this: when a person connects the attribute of "Observe" to "Justice," he is "doing righteousness" for all things in the world, even for external matters, and certainly for the internal ones. This totality is called "Every Time" <note>original: *Kol Et*</note>.

One who understands the secret of the verse that says, "I form light and create darkness, I make peace and create evil" <note>Isaiah 45:7</note>, will understand the secret of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, and the secret of a "Good Time" and an "Evil Time." What is the connection between "Peace" and "Evil"? The verse says "making peace and creating evil" because peace is the opposite of war, and good is the opposite of evil. However, the matter of "Peace" being mentioned alongside "Evil" is known to those who perceive the truth: the attribute called "Peace" is Good. Therefore it says "making peace and creating evil," for "Evil" is outside the boundary of the Place called "Good," which is the secret of "All" <note>original: *Kol*</note>. Therefore, they sealed the Works of Creation with the seal called "Good," as it is written: "And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>.

This attribute is sometimes called the ### Mighty One of Jacob <gloss>2</gloss>. The reason is that "from Understanding <note>original: *Binah*</note>, the hawk <note>original: *Netz*</note> spreads its wings" <note>Job 39:26</note>—this is the secret of Wisdom <gloss>3</gloss>, the "Small Sabbath" and the "Great Sabbath." The reason it is called:

->the Mighty One of Jacob, and not the Mighty One of Abraham or the Mighty One of Isaac, is because this attribute is dependent upon the attribute of Jacob<-

For Jacob is the Middle Pillar, chosen as the letter *Vav* of the Holy Name <note>The 'Vav' in the Tetragrammaton Y-H-V-H</note>. The secret of the *Vav* is uniquely assigned to Jacob in the secret of "Beauty" <note>original: *Tiferet*</note>. Within it, the attributes of Abraham <gloss>4</gloss> and Isaac are held—Abraham on the right and Isaac on the left, with Jacob as the Middle Pillar. The sign for this is "Jacob was a simple man, dwelling in tents" <gloss>5</gloss> <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. The secret of the "simple man" <note>original: *Ish Tam*</note> relates to the "completeness" <note>original: *Timat*</note> of the *Lulav* <note>the palm branch used on Sukkot</note>, which is the secret of the middle line of the palm branch. "Dwelling in tents" refers to two tents: the tent of Abraham and the tent of Isaac, for they are the two sides of the *Lulav*. Because the secret of Jacob is the Middle Pillar and the secret of the letter *Vav*, we say "God of Abraham, God of Isaac, **and** God of Jacob," with the additional "and" <note>the letter *Vav* in Hebrew means 'and'</note> for Jacob. So too: "The great, the mighty, and the awesome God." This is the great secret of "I will remember My covenant with Jacob" <note>Leviticus 26:42</note>, where the name Jacob is written in full with a *Vav*.

The "Covenant of Jacob" is the secret of the "Mighty One of Jacob." Sometimes <gloss>6</gloss> it is called the "Mighty One of Israel" in the secret of the "Closed and Sealed." Therefore the Ark says: "The Lord of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel." You must also know who is called "Master—"

Look there. # Gate 2

"And Aaron shall come into the holy place with the measure called **'This'** <gloss>Aleph</gloss>." <note>original: "Be-zot yavo Aharon el ha-kodesh" (Leviticus 16:3). It is called by the name "This" because it is "Good." We have already informed you that according to the Name *Adonai* <note>The Name of God traditionally associated with the Sefirah of Malchut</note>, it is called the "Time of Favor," and it is the "Time of *Adonai*." This time is "Justice" <note>Hebrew: Tzedek</note>, which is the "Good" that flows from "The Righteous One" <note>Hebrew: Tzaddik, referring to the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation)</note>. Because all creatures receive their sustenance and food through this attribute <gloss>Aleph</gloss>, it is said: **"The eyes of all look to You"** <gloss>Aleph</gloss> **"and You give them their food in its season"** <note>Psalm 145:15</note>. This is the secret of: "He has made everything beautiful in its time" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:11</note>.

One who knows how to join the attribute of "Remember" <note>Zachor, representing the masculine principle or Tiferet</note> with the attribute of "Observe" <note>Shamor, representing the feminine principle or Malchut</note>, concerning him it is said: **"Happy are those who keep justice, who do righteousness at all times"** <note>Psalm 106:3</note>. This means that one who brings the attribute of "Observe" close to "Justice" <note>Mishpat</note> causes blessings to flow into all things in the world, whether into the internal <term>Sefirot<gloss>the ten divine attributes or emanations</gloss></term> or into external things that exist outside the Sefirot. For when the internal Sefirot receive the flow and are ordered, then everything in the world receives the power of abundance and emanation. This is the secret of "doing righteousness at all times." How is it possible for a person to do righteousness at every single moment of the day? Rather, the secret of the matter is this: when a person joins the attribute of "Observe" to "Justice," he performs "Righteousness" <note>Tzedakah</note> throughout all things in the world, even in external matters—how much more so in the internal matters, where the collective whole is called "All" <note>Hebrew: Kol</note>.

One who understands the secret of the verse: **"Former of peace and Creator of evil"** <note>Isaiah 45:7</note> will understand the secret of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, and the secret of a "Good Time" and an "Evil Time." For what does "Peace" have to do with "Evil"? The verse says "Former of peace and Creator of evil" because peace is the opposite of war, just as good is the opposite of evil. However, the connection of "Peace" to "Evil" here is known to those who perceive the Truth: the attribute called "Peace" is "Good," and therefore it says "Former of peace and Creator of evil," for evil exists outside the boundary of the Place called "Good," which is the secret of "All." Therefore, the works of creation were sealed with the seal called "Good," as it is written: "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>.
