# Gate 3, [Part] 4

...of the world. (א) And the **Book of the Generations of Adam** <note>Genesis 5:1</note> is suspended in this place, and from them is drawn the Great Power into all great things in the world among all living creatures. All of this occurs when **Netzach** <term>Victory/Endurance</term> and **Hod** <term>Splendor/Majesty</term> join with **Yesod** <term>Foundation</term>. It was at this attribute <note>Sefira</note> that all those who came to ask for children before the Lord, may He be blessed, would prepare themselves. Their prayer would first enter the "Palace of the Lord of Hosts" <note>original: *Heichal YHVH Tzevaot*</note> to ascend higher until reaching **Binah** <term>Understanding</term>. Thus, when **Hannah** prayed <note>1 Samuel 1</note>, she only entered that palace because of what she needed. What is written? "And she vowed a vow and said..." What does a "vow" <note>original: *neder*</note> have to do with this place? Her prayer ascended to the place of **Binah**, which is called *G.D.* <note>possibly a shorthand for a divine name or numerical value related to Binah</note>, which is the power that draws children from **Keter** <term>The Crown</term>, from the place called "Ayin" <note>Nothingness/Source</note>. And into which palace did she enter to produce children from it? Into the palace called **Hosts** <note>original: *Tzevaot*</note>. This is the secret of her saying, "O Lord of Hosts, if You will indeed look on the affliction of Your maidservant." In her prayer, she mentioned the source of all those who are born. From there, she ascended to **Binah**, which draws children from the *Mazal* <term>celestial flow or destiny</term> of **Keter**, which is the "Supreme Flow" in the secret of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy established in **Keter**. For from that flow, "children, life, and sustenance" <note>a famous Talmudic dictum</note> depend, and even the Torah scroll depends on it. This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, meant by: "Everything depends on *Mazal*, even the Torah scroll in the Temple." Do not let it enter your mind that this refers to the constellations of the stars of the heavens.

The Wise One <note>likely referring to a specific commentator like Abraham ibn Ezra or a similar figure</note> also spoke in this manner, and it was accepted by the **Kabbalists** <term>mystical tradition</term>, regarding the one who clothes the Ten Sefirot of **Malchut** <term>Kingdom</term>, which is called "Malchut" according to the appearance of the *Face* <note>original: *Pe'ah*</note> called by the name **Adam** <term>Man</term>. Their beginning is in **Keter**. **Malchut** is called by this name because the intention is for the created glory in **Malchut**; in this secret, **Malchut** is prepared for the eyes of the body to see the entities that are the souls of the pious and the "children of the pious." When they are called "Angels," they are clothed for a time without a permanent garment and are revealed only to the eye of the soul and its imagination, appearing to it according to the power of its imagination. This is what the Sages meant by "Everything was said concerning children, and here it was said concerning angels." "Everything was said concerning children" when the **Shekhinah** <term>Divine Presence</term> was upon them; and further on, it was said "Angels" when the **Shekhinah** departed from there and they donned the form of angels. For there was a Voice before him, and they went... and it is written in the [Book of] Twelve, "And the two angels came to Sodom" <note>Genesis 19:1</note>, even though there they were also called "men," as it is written, "the men seized his hand" and "the angels seized." This is as the author of *Ha-Penini* explained: things that are "clothed" can be seen even by eyes of flesh. For the **Shekhinah**—which separates from the second soul, the **Malchut**—can take the form of hearts and even "wings of thread" and "enlighteners of heaven." But this is not by the eye of its kingdom... and do not be surprised by any of this and do not err. The "wing" is visible in a vision... which others are not worthy of. Some of these actions and matters are from this impurity, certainly the messengers of the Holy One, blessed be He, who are the attributes of purity and holiness... for his messengers are for them. We have already seen and heard examples of this, where the messengers stand near their death, and they recognize the deceased who come to receive them, as in the case of "clear the vessels for Hezekiah, King of Judah" <note>Talmud, Berakhot 28b</note>. And there is no... in all this, and he dons the appearance of a message, and they are not messengers or those who speak with them generally among the prophets like the case of Daniel, but rather a vision called "the opening of eyes," as in "And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw the angel of the Lord." Similarly, "And Elisha prayed and said: Lord, open his eyes." All prophetic visions and power come only from **Netzach** and **Hod**, and from them they issue. In the place of **Binah**, through the angels... and the **Shekhinah** in a form, as the Rabbi, the author, explained. Through this, many of his secrets and hints are clarified... I have already elaborated on these matters in the chapter of *Likutei* on the portions *Vayeira* and *Vayishlach*; you will find there a broad explanation of the nature of prophecy among the prophets.

(א) **And the Book of the Generations of Adam is suspended in this place.** The explanation is that **Yesod** is like a body in which all the generations of man are depicted and inscribed, in the likeness of a book in which they write. These are the secrets of the seed, and the meaning of what is said in the *Bahir* <note>The Sefer Ha-Bahir, an early Kabbalistic work</note>, explaining the verse "from your seed," that through this, I will make... And know these things. Therefore, when joining **Netzach** and **Hod**, the secret of the *Teli* <note>The "Celestial Dragon" or axis</note> is sent between them, the "clothing of the glory" of the inner matters by their power for us above. In the author's introduction, he included these attributes which were intended for the "vessels" before the Lord, may He be blessed, to give birth to children, and to raise my thought from below to above to remember **Chesed** <term>Loving-kindness</term> which is **Malchut** <note>This likely refers to the flow into Malchut</note>, to **Yesod** which is the secret of the **Covenant of Circumcision** <note>original: *Brit Milah*</note>, in the secret of "Remember" and "Observe" <note>the two aspects of the Sabbath</note> and in the "one between two" that I mentioned. The strength of the three is the "Middle Line" of the world above in the union of the "Hearers of the World." From there [comes] the secret of **Chokhmah** <term>Wisdom</term> and **Binah** <term>Understanding</term> in the union of the **Will** which is **Keter** <term>The Crown</term>, the secret of the Source and the Supreme *Mazal* from which everything issues. And through it, everything is born. Afterwards, he returns and gives birth in my thought... the secret of the Infinite <note>original: *Ein Sof*</note> which includes all three matters in the details of the arrangement in the "four arms" until the "two between" descends to the "speech of H" <note>likely the letter Hey, representing Malchut</note> and from there to Abraham, the secret of the "female quantity," the "crown of her husband." The power of the "Table" is the secret of the drawing down of children and life, which are included in the 70 supreme... to the Eye of Life, and from it to all... and from there to the "Land of the Living," and sustenance follows this same path.

# Gate 3, [Part] 4

...of the world. (A) And the **Book of the Generations of Adam** <note>original: *Sefer Toldot Adam*; referring to the mystical record of all human souls</note> is suspended in this place. From these Sefirot, the great power is drawn into all great things in the world, including all living creatures. All of this occurs through the union of **Netzach** <term>Victory/Endurance</term> and **Hod** <term>Splendor/Majesty</term> at the point of **Yesod** <term>Foundation/the Procreative force</term>. It was toward this specific attribute that all those who came to ask for children before the Blessed Lord would direct their intention. 

One’s prayer first enters the "Hall of the Lord of Hosts" <note>original: *Heikhal Tzevaot*</note> to ascend further up to **Binah** <term>Understanding/the Divine Mother</term>. This is why Hannah, in her prayer, only entered that specific Hall that she required. For what is written? "And she vowed a vow" <note>1 Samuel 1:11; original: *va-tiddor neder*</note>. What does a "vow" have to do with this context? Rather, through her prayer, she ascended to the place of **Binah**, which is called **N'der** <note>A wordplay on *Neder* (vow) and the number 50 (*Nun*) plus *Dar* (to dwell), representing the 50 Gates of Understanding</note>. It is she <note>Binah</note> who draws down children from **Keter** <term>Crown/the highest Sefirah</term>, from the place called "Ayin" <note>Nothingness/Infinity</note>. 

Into which Hall did she enter to produce children from it? Into the Hall called **Tzevaot** <note>Hosts</note>. This is the secret of her saying, "O Lord of Hosts (*YHVH Tzevaot*), if You will indeed look on the affliction of Your handmaid." In her prayer, she mentioned the source-place of all those who are born. From there, she ascended to **Binah**, which draws children from the "Fortune" (*Mazal*) of **Keter**. This is the "Supernal Fortune" within the secret of the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy** established in the Crown. For from that "Fortune," children, life, and sustenance are suspended—and even a Torah scroll depends upon it. This is what the Sages, of blessed memory, meant when they said: "Everything depends on **Mazal** <term>Fortune/Source-flow</term>, even the Torah scroll in the Temple." And do not let it enter your mind that this refers to the constellations of the stars in the heavens...

<margin>
(A) **The Book of the Generations of Adam is suspended in this place.** This means **Yesod**, which is called a "Sign" (*Ot*), wherein all the generations of man are etched and hinted at, like a book in which things are written. This is the secret of the "covenant" (*karet*). Regarding this, they said in the *Bahir*: "What is a house? To your seed I have given this land." Know that when these two—**Netzach** and **Hod**—unite, they are the secret of the "two testicles" <note>original Aramaic: *trei beia d'dikura*; a bold anatomical metaphor for the Sefirot Netzach and Hod as the sources of "seed" or divine flow</note> in the secret of the internal matters written for us above in the introduction, which bring children. Therefore, these attributes were the focus for those asking for children before the Blessed Lord. One must elevate their thought from below to above: from the **Malchut** <term>Kingdom</term> to **Yesod** (the secret of the Covenant of Circumcision), then to **Binah**... up to the first union in **Keter**, which is the Source and the Supernal Fortune from which the power of everything is drawn. Then, one leads the flow (*shefa*) back down through their thought... to the "two sources" and from there to the Crown of the Bridegroom... this is the secret of drawing down children and life included in the three Upper Sefirot...
</margin>

...[The commentary continues regarding the nature of vision] And the building likewise follows this path. It has been explained by the Kabbalists that **Malchut**, which is called *Elohim*, serves as the garment for the attributes above it, which are called "Adam." This *Malchut* clothes itself in the "Throne," and on the Throne, there is a likeness of the "Glory of the Great King." These are appointed over the eyes of the body... while souls, the pious, and the sons of prophets [perceive differently]. When angels were created, they were actual angels without "garments," and they could not be perceived except by the eye of the soul. A person's imagination forms an image of them according to the power of their imagination. This is what the Sages meant: "The Lord appeared to Abraham as a traveler, and to Jacob as a shepherd." The Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) was upon them. Sometimes they are called "men," as it is written, "And the men turned their faces from there," and yet they are angels. As the author of *Ha-Penini* explained: things that are "clothed" can sometimes be seen even by the eyes of flesh... but this is not through physical garments, but through a spiritual reality. 

Do not wonder at this. The spirit of a person can see... while those coming from the side of impurity cannot. Certainly, the spirits of the Blessed Name, coming from the attributes of purity and holiness, appear according to their mission. We have seen and heard examples of this: where the sick, standing near death, mention the deceased who come to meet them—as in the case of Hezekiah, King of Judah. There is no doubt in this, and the Sages did not withhold this from the public. However, those who see spirits or speak with them are not necessarily "prophets" like Daniel; rather, it is another type of angel called "Sight of the Eyes," as in "The Lord opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the Lord," or Elisha’s prayer: "Lord, please open his eyes." But the "Vision of Prophecy" and "Divine Speech" come only from the power of **Netzach** and **Hod**... as the Master [Maimonides] explained. I have already elaborated on these matters in the commentary on the portions *Vayerach* and *Vayishlach*, where you will find a broad explanation of the difference between the prophecy of Moses and that of other prophets.

# Gate 3, [Part] 4

<image-desc>A decorative scribal flourish appears in the right margin next to the first five lines of text.</image-desc>

An angel calls and the Word speaks, but here the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "I am the One who calls and I am the One who speaks." <note>original: *ani hu ha-kore ve-ani hu ha-medaber*</note> The explanation of the matter is that all the prophets must prepare themselves and focus their intent toward prophecy before the prophetic spirit rests upon them—whether through their own efforts or through an angel. However, Moses our Teacher <note>original: *MaRa"H*, abbreviation for *Moshe Rabbeinu Alav HaShalom*</note> does not need to prepare himself for prophecy, for he is always prepared and ready, as it is said: "Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you" <note>Numbers 9:8</note>. It also says: "And when Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with Him, then he heard the voice speaking unto him" <note>Numbers 7:89</note>. If so, contemplate, know, and believe that the prophecy of all other prophets comes from **Netzach** <term>Victory/Endurance</term> and **Hod** <term>Splendor/Majesty</term>; from these they draw their sustenance. And if you see in the Torah an angel speaking with a prophet in a prophetic vision, or with another person, you must understand and know that there is another matter here that requires explanation. For you should know that an angel spoke with **Hagar**, the handmaid of Sarai, as it is said: "And the angel of the Lord found her by a fountain of water..." and "the angel of the Lord said to her..." <note>Genesis 16:7-9</note> and the entire account of Hagar. You should know that Hagar was not a prophetess. Similarly, in the matter of **Manoah**, it says: "And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah: 'Though you detain me, I will not eat of your bread'" <note>Judges 13:16</note>. Do you not see that even Manoah did not understand that an angel was speaking with him, for he was an unlearned man? <note>original: *am ha-aretz*</note> The proof is that when Manoah saw the angel of the Lord ascending in the flame of the altar, he was terrified and said to his wife: "We shall surely die, because we have seen God" <note>Judges 13:22</note>. Let it not enter your mind that Manoah or his wife were prophets, for they are not included in the category of prophecy. <gloss>(a)</gloss> However, regarding the seeing of angels by those with "pure eyes," there is a wondrous secret in it. For three angels appeared to our father **Abraham** in the likeness of men, as it is said: "And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood by him" <note>Genesis 18:2</note>. But when the two remaining ones came to **Lot**, they appeared to him in the likeness of angels, as it is said: "And the two angels came to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom; and Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them" <note>Genesis 19:1</note>. Do not let it enter your mind that Lot was a prophet; rather, in these matters there are several aspects and hidden secrets that require great understanding. And regarding **Daniel**, who was not a prophet, <note>In Jewish tradition, Daniel is considered to have perceived the Holy Spirit but is not ranked among the Prophets (Nevi'im)</note> he would speak with the angel as it is said of him: "the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly" <note>Daniel 9:21</note>. You will yet hear clear and living words regarding these matters, with the help of God.

By this path, contemplate how the prophets draw from **Netzach** and **Hod**, which are the "Secret of the Lord of Hosts" <note>original: *Sod YHVH Tzevaot*</note> as we have already informed you. Therefore, know that because these are the "mirrors" through which the prophets looked, you will find that at the time of prophecy, the bodies of the prophets would recoil, tremble, and shake. Their bones would be terrified until they were transformed from their original state, so that their souls were purified; only then would they see what they saw in the prophetic vision. Regarding this, it is said: "In a vision I make Myself known to him" <note>Numbers 12:6</note>, and sometimes through a dream. According to the number of "partitions" <note>metaphorical veils between the human and the Divine</note>, parables and riddles would increase within them. <margin>25</margin> This is the meaning of: "In a dream I speak with him." And the prophet says: "The prophet who has a dream, let him tell a dream; and he who has My word, let him speak My word faithfully" <note>Jeremiah 23:28</note>. But Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, prophesied without the mediation of **Netzach** and **Hod**, for he would enter the innermost sanctum. Therefore: "Mouth to mouth I speak with him, manifestly, and not in riddles" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. Because of this, Moses did not mention the name "Lord of Hosts" <note>original: *YHVH Tzevaot*</note> in the Torah, because his prophecy was through the name **YHVH** <term>The Tetragrammaton/Infinite Name</term> alone. He reached the very source of the spring, and all the "hosts" of above and below would go out and come in by his word.

Know that all those who come to pray according to the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy** <note>original: *Yod-Gimmel Middot Ha-Rachamim*</note> and ask for children from the Lord, may He be blessed, would direct their intent toward **Netzach** and **Hod** in order to draw the power down to the name **Adonai** <term>Lord/Sovereignty</term>. From these [Sefirot], all the "hosts" of heaven and earth are drawn forth according to their kinds. The abundance <note>original: *shefa*</note> comes to all species to make every kind sprout and grow according to its nature. From them is drawn the power of growth in plants, trees, and every fruit-bearing tree. From them is drawn the power of procreation, and from them, all the generations

# Gate 4

The angel calls and the speech speaks, but here the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "I am the one who calls and I am the one who speaks." <note>This refers to the unique level of Moses’s prophecy where God spoke directly to him without an angelic intermediary.</note> The explanation of this matter is that all other prophets must prepare themselves and direct their intentions toward their prophecy before the spirit of prophecy rests upon them—whether through their own efforts or through an angel. However, Moses our Teacher (peace be upon him) did not need to prepare himself for prophecy, for he was always prepared and ready, as it is said: "Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you" <note>Numbers 9:8</note>. It also says: "And when Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with Him, then he heard the voice speaking unto him" <note>Numbers 7:89</note>.

If so, contemplate, know, and believe that the prophecy of all [other] prophets is rooted in **Netzach** <term>Victory/Endurance</term> and **Hod** <term>Splendor/Majesty</term>; it is from them that they draw their sustenance. And if you see in the Torah an angel speaking with a prophet in a prophetic vision, or with any other person, you must understand and know that there is a different matter here requiring explanation. For you should know that the angel spoke with **Hagar**, the handmaid of **Sarah**, as it is said: "And the angel of the Lord found her by a fountain of water..." and "the angel of the Lord said to her," and that entire passage concerning Hagar <note>Genesis 16:7-11</note>. Yet you know that Hagar was not a prophetess!

Similarly, in the matter of **Manoah** <note>The father of Samson</note>: "And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah: 'Though you detain me, I will not eat of your bread'" <note>Judges 13:16</note>. Do you not see that even Manoah did not understand that an angel was speaking with him?

But when the remaining two of them came to **Lot**, they appeared to him in the likeness of angels, as it is said: "And the two angels came to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom; and Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them" <note>Genesis 19:1</note>. Let it not enter your mind that Lot was a prophet; rather, in these matters, there are several levels and several hidden secrets that require great understanding.

Even the matter of **Daniel**, who was not a prophet <note>The Jewish tradition categorizes Daniel’s book in the "Writings" rather than "Prophets" because his revelations were through the Holy Spirit/angels rather than direct prophecy</note>, yet he spoke with the angel, as it is said: "even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly" <note>Daniel 9:21</note>. Regarding these matters, you will yet hear words that are clear and living, God willing.

Therefore, know that because these are the "mirrors" through which the prophets would look, you will find that at the time of prophecy, the bodies of the prophets would tremble, fear, and shake. Concerning this, it is said: "I will make Myself known to him in a vision" <note>Numbers 12:6</note>, and sometimes through a dream. According to the number of "partitions" <note>spiritual veils</note>, the parables and riddles within them would multiply.

But Moses our Teacher (peace be upon him) prophesied without the mediation of **Netzach** and **Hod**, for he would enter the innermost of the innermost [realms]. Therefore: "With him I speak mouth to mouth, even manifestly, and not in dark speeches" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. For this reason, Moses did not mention the name "Lord of Hosts" <note>original: *YHVH Tzevaot*</note> in the Torah, because his prophecy was through the [essential] Name **YHVH**. He reached the very source of the spring, and all the "hosts" above and below would go out and come in at his word.

The abundance (*shefa*) then comes to all species to make them sprout and grow, each according to its matter. From these [Netzach and Hod] is drawn the power of growth in plants, in groves, and in every tree yielding fruit. # Gate 4

A person who seeks to obtain favor from before the Lord, may He be blessed, should contemplate the ten **Sefirot** <term>the ten divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the world</term> and draw the desire and the will from above to below, down to the end of the Will, which is the name **Adonai** <note>original: *ADNY*, the name associated with the lowest Sefira, Kingship</note>. Thus, the Sefirot are found to be blessed by him <gloss>meaning: we make it known that there is a Lord, for the divine flow moves and spreads to every "foundation and arm" and to the world; this secret is for the sake of the collective whole, and everything depends on the deeds of those below. This is his intention here</gloss>. Consequently, the person themselves is blessed by the Sefirot. This is the secret of what is written: 
<margin>The secret of Amen and the Mouth</margin>
"He who blesses himself in the earth shall bless himself by the God of **Amen**" <note>Isaiah 65:16</note>. The secret of **Amen** is the secret of drawing down blessings from the name **Ehyeh** <note>original: *AHeYeH*, meaning "I Will Be," the name associated with the highest Sefira</note> to the name **Yahweh**, and from the name **Yahweh** to the name **Adonai**. 

Thus you have learned that every person who prays and directs their heart in this way—unifying the Sefirot and bringing them close to one another—is acting correctly. Therefore, contemplate what the Lord said to Abraham: "**So** [Koh] shall your seed be" <note>Genesis 15:5</note>. This means: you must rise from the attribute of **Koh** <note>The Hebrew word "So" (*Koh*) has a numerical value of 25, often associated with the Shekhinah or the lowest Sefira</note>, which is the lowest, up to the level of **Ehyeh**, which is the highest, and then you will merit children. 

Because a person must focus in their prayer and ascend from Sefira to Sefira and from "will to will" until they reach the source of the Supreme Will in their heart, which is called **Ein Sof** <term>the Infinite; God as He exists beyond all human comprehension</term>, King David said: "A song of ascents. Out of the **depths** I have called You, O Lord" <note>Psalm 130:1</note>. The meaning of "out of the depths" is from the Supreme Source called **Ein Sof**, which is "deep." This is the secret of the **tip of the letter Yod** in the name **Yahweh** <note>The small stroke at the top of the Hebrew letter Yod represents the highest point of emanation, the Sefira of Keter (Crown)</note>. This is the meaning of "out of the depths I have called You, O Lord." 

How does one direct their heart in the way of the "ascents" from bottom to top? By including the final **Koh** of the Name to rise from attribute to attribute and from Sefira to Sefira, until their thought is elevated to the "tip of the Yod" in the **Crown** <note>original: *Keter*</note>, which is called **Ein Sof**. This is the secret of "the depths." Therefore it says: "A song of ascents; out of the depths I have called You, O Lord." 

Do not think that the word "depth" refers only to something lowly or deep at the bottom; rather, anything that is hidden, concealed, and difficult to grasp is called "deep." As it is said: "That which is far off and exceeding deep, who can find it out?" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>. And the great secret that includes everything: "How deep are Your thoughts" <note>Psalm 92:6</note>. See how the term "depth" is linked here to the place of **Thought** <note>original: *Machshavah*, the Sefira of Wisdom or Chokhmah</note>. You already know that the secret of Thought is the letter **Yod** of the Name. In the *Book of Formation* <note>original: *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note> it says: "The depth of height and the depth of bottom, the depth of beginning and the depth of end, the depth of east and the depth of west." 

As for what you find in the scriptures—"The heaven for height, and the earth for depth" <note>Proverbs 25:3</note>—this does not contradict our words. In truth, all things remain within their natural character. It is known that the heavens are high above the earth. Because the heavens are high and surround the earth, you might say that the heavens surrounding the earth from below are "deeper" or "lower" than the earth. This is not true; there is nothing in the world lower than the earth and its offspring. For the heavens that are below the earth are still "high" relative to the earth. 

If you understand the secret of the earth’s position in the center of the heavens, you will know that the earth inside the heavens is like a point in the center of a circle. When you understand the **science of astronomy** <term>original: *Tichunah*, the study of the structure of the celestial spheres</term>, you will find that the entire circle in its rotation is "high" from every side, and the center point is "low" from every side. Because the earth is in the center of the heavens—like a point within a circle—and the heavens are high above it from every side, and it is lower than all the celestial spheres that surround it, it is said: "The heaven for height, and the earth for depth." 

This matter requires great understanding for those not accustomed to the science of astronomy, but for an astronomer, it is a simple thing to understand. 

**After** having informed you of this, let us return to our subject: the one who prays must focus their thought until they reach, with perfect intention, the source of the Will. This is the "tip of the Yod," which is the "depth of thought." Concerning this it is said: "Out of the depths I have called You," and "How deep are Your thoughts." 

Now, contemplate and know how deep the power of prayer is! From what place does it begin, and to what place does it chain down and flow? Through prayer performed properly, all the Sefirot are unified and the divine flow is drawn from above to below. Thus, those in the upper and lower worlds are found to be blessed by the one who prays. Their prayer is accepted, and they become beloved above and cherished below. They obtain their needs and all the requests of their heart are fulfilled, for they are beloved by all the Sefirot. Of such a person it is said: "The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth" <note>Psalm 145:18</note>.

It uses an astronomical analogy to explain "depth" as the center of a sphere, representing the most hidden point of divine thought.</summary>

# Gate 54 <note>The Hebrew letters "Nun Dalet" signify 54, though this page continues the themes of Gate 4 discussed previously.</note>

"Everything depends on **Mazal** <term>literally 'luck' or 'zodiac,' but here referring to the supreme divine influence flowing from the highest Sefira</term>, even the Torah scroll in the Sanctuary." Do not let it enter your mind that the Torah scroll depends on the literal constellations of the heavenly stars! For the entire world was created through the Torah; how then could the Torah be dependent on a "mazal" that was itself created by the Torah? Rather, the secret of the saying "Everything depends on **Mazal**, even the Torah scroll in the Sanctuary" refers to the **Supreme Mazal** known within the **Keter** <term>the Crown, the highest of the ten Sefirot</term>. All the **Sefirot** and all created beings hang from this level, and even the Torah is dependent upon it.

It is called **Mazal** <note>original: *mazal*</note> because from it the divine powers "flow" <note>original: *nozelim*, a wordplay on *mazal*</note> into all the Sefirot and to all the inhabitants of the world. Even the Torah scroll draws power from this **Mazal** and receives from it. 

Consider how Hannah, in her prayer, ascended higher and higher until she reached the place called **Mazal**. This is the secret of what is written: "And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed **on** the Lord" <note>1 Samuel 1:10</note>. The verse does not say she prayed "**to** [el] the Lord," but "**on** [al] the Lord." I have already informed you that there are three primary names: Below is **Adonai**, in the middle is **Yahweh**, and above is **Ehyeh**, which is the **Keter**. Within **Ehyeh** hangs the **Mazal** from which "children" <note>referring to new souls or outcomes</note> are drawn. This is the secret of "praying **on** the Lord"—meaning literally "above" the name **Yahweh**, reaching the name **Ehyeh**. From that place, she secured her desire in this matter.

This is what our sages meant when they said: "Children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit, but rather depend on **Mazal**" <note>original: *Banei, Chayei, u-Mezonei la'u bi-zechuta talya milta ela be-mazala talya milta*</note>. The place of "merit" <note>original: *zechuta*</note> is the site of the Great Heavenly Court, called the "Court of Seventy," which is the place called **Elohim** <term>the name of God associated with Justice and the Sefira of Gevurah/Strength</term>, as we will explain in its proper place, God willing. 

However, these things depend on **Mazal**, which is the place of the known **Mazal** that gives out of grace and mercy to whoever finds favor in its eyes, according to the secret of the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy** <term>the list of God's merciful qualities revealed to Moses</term> within the Sefira of **Ehyeh** (the Crown). One who wishes to give birth to children through a miracle must ascend to this place. Similarly, one who wishes to attain more years of life than were allotted to them, or one who wishes to attain more sustenance than is naturally due to them based on their birth. 

These three things—Children, Life, and Sustenance—are explained in the Torah as being above the "Great Court" (which is called "Merit"). This Court is the "Left Side" of the Sefira **Tiferet**, which is called **Yahweh**. How do you know that these three things depend on levels higher than the name **Yahweh**?

1. **Life:** Regarding Hezekiah, King of Judah, it is written: "I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, **He shall add** [yosif] to your days" <note>Isaiah 38:5</note>. It does not say "I am adding" [mosif], but "He shall add"—meaning, "I, the Great Court, have judged the case; if the Supreme Light so wills, **He** shall add to your days."
2. **Children:** As written regarding Hannah's prayer when she asked for "human seed" and "prayed **on** the Lord"—literally reaching the level of **Ehyeh** where the **Mazal** is fixed. Therefore the verse says "on [al] the Lord."
3. **Sustenance:** As written: "Cast your burden **on** the Lord, and He shall sustain you" <note>Psalm 55:23</note>. It says "**on** the Lord" and not "**to** the Lord." 

The reason for this is that whoever wishes to attain these three things cannot always obtain them in this world according to the law of "Merit" (the Great Heavenly Court). In such a case, where should they direct their intention? They must raise their focus higher and higher, inward from this world, to the place of the **Keter** (**Ehyeh**), which is the **Infinite** [Ein Sof], the place of the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy**. One of those thirteen attributes is called **Mazal**. 

This is what the sages meant: "Children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit, but on **Mazal**." Based on these words, know and understand that although we say one who wishes to receive their request from the Lord should contemplate the specific Divine Name associated with that need, we do not mean they should focus on that name alone and stop there. Rather, the intention should be to focus on that name through which the need is channeled, and then draw the focus of that name up through the ten Sefirot to the **Supreme Source**, called the **Source of Will**. When one reaches the Source of Will, they will secure their desire and the requests of their heart. This is the meaning of: "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing" <note>Psalm 145:16</note>. Do not read it as "Your hand" [yadecha] but "Your hands" [yadeicha], meaning you open the secret of the letter *Yod* of the name **Yahweh**, which is the Source of Will. Then you fulfill the desire of every seeker. Thus you have learned that when a person...

# Gate 3 & 4 <note>The header indicates a transition or combined discussion of these Gates, though the themes involve the higher Sefirot.</note>

Certainly, He can turn back His outstretched hand. The reason is that [the Divine Name] receives flow and power from the attribute called **Mi** <note>original: *Mi* ("Who"), a mystical designation for the Sefira of *Binah* (Understanding)</note>. 

And the secret is: "Lift up your eyes on high and see: **Who** [Mi] created **these** [Ele]?" <note>Isaiah 40:26. In Kabbalah, "Mi" (Who) is the hidden upper world of *Binah*, while "Ele" (These) refers to the revealed lower seven Sefirot.</note>. **Mi** certainly created **these**, for the lower God called **L"S** <note>original: *L"S*, likely an abbreviation for the name *Elohim* as it manifests in the lower realms or *Malchut*</note> created the world through the power of the upper God, which is (A) the secret of **Binah** and is called **Mi**. Concerning this, it is said: "Mi created these." 

Since the righteous know the secret of **Mi**, they can nullify a decree. Understand this great matter and see the secret stated: "Turn from Your fierce anger," for the place of **Repentance** <term>Hebrew: *Teshuvah*</term> is **Mi**, and it (B) rules over wrath and anger. Thus it says: "In this jubilee year (C) you shall return every man unto his possession" <note>Leviticus 25:13. The Jubilee year is associated with *Binah*, where all things return to their source.</note>. 

Therefore, contemplate the wonders alluded to in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <term>The Book of Formation, an early Jewish mystical text</term>, that counsel (D) is finalized in the kidneys. As it says: "Against counsel he shall remove it," and our Sages, of blessed memory, said: [The kidneys are] the place where counsel is finalized. Therefore, understand that every decree decreed in the Heavenly Court begins by consulting **Binah** and finishes the counsel in **Netzach** and **Hod**, which are the secret of "Lord of Hosts" <note>Hebrew: *YHWH Tzevaot*</note>. 

Even though a decree has been made, the attribute <margin>And for</margin> called **Mi**, which is called **Repentance**, can break and nullify that decree. Thus it is written: "The Lord of hosts has purposed, and **Who** [Mi] shall annul it?" <note>Isaiah 14:27. A mystical wordplay: the name "Mi" has the power to annul the purposes of the "Lord of Hosts."</note>. Those who knew these secrets would focus their intent in their prayers and nullify all harsh and evil decrees, for they held the keys of **reception** <term>Hebrew: *Kabbalah*</term> and would enter until the necessary place. 

After we have informed you of this, know (E) that in the Palaces <term>Hebrew: *Heikhalot*</term> of **Netzach** and **Hod**, called "Lord of Hosts," there is an angel appointed over all the legal verdicts that emerge from the Great Court upon all people of the world, by the hands of two scribes. Before those verdicts go out into the world, that appointee has the power to tear them up or amend them, all according to the power of the repentance of the one against whom the verdict was decreed. Just as mercy comes from the place of **Mi**, who annuls and is called **Repentance**, so this appointee completes the verdict, whether to tear it up or to amend something in it. 

Know that in these Palaces there is another appointee under the hand of the Name, may He be blessed, who has under his hand treasuries and storehouses and appointees to receive all the souls of all those who were executed by the court, as well as those executed by the government <term>Hebrew: *harugei malchut*, often referring to martyrs</term>, and other those killed by the nations; in these places they are hidden and guarded. 

In the places of these Palaces, there are hidden things called the **Cup of Consolations**, from which the Lord sends comfort to all mourners and those in pain, and to all those worthy of comfort. And there are treasuries in them called the **Cup of Reeling** <note>original: *kos ha-tar'elah*, a cup of judgment or staggering</note>, with which the Lord, may He be blessed, takes vengeance on those who are fitting and deserving before Him. 

In the places of these Palaces, there are hidden things in which there are several kinds of precious garments, in which the pure souls are clothed when they enter to appear before the Lord, may He be blessed. Each and every soul (F) is clothed in these Palaces according to the garment worthy of it, to appear...

# Gate 4

And it says: "Then you shall call, and the Lord will answer" <note>Isaiah 58:9</note>; and it says: "May He grant you according to your heart’s desire and fulfill all your counsel" <note>Psalms 20:5</note>. Know that these two attributes, which are **Counsel** <term>Hebrew: *Etzah*, associated with the Sefirah of *Netzach*</term> and **Splendor** <term>Hebrew: *Hod*</term>, are 

## The Place of Counsel
in the Heavenly Court. The secret is: "For the Lord of Hosts has counseled, and who shall annul it?" <note>Isaiah 14:27</note>.

When the Name, may He be blessed and exalted, decrees a matter in the Heavenly Court through these two attributes of counsel—this is what is written: "This is the counsel that is purposed upon the whole earth" <note>Isaiah 14:26</note>. And it says: "For the Lord of Hosts has counseled, and who shall annul it?" Even though the beginning of counsel <margin>A</margin> comes from the place of **Understanding** <term>Hebrew: *Binah*</term>, the end of counsel is in **Victory** <term>Hebrew: *Netzach*</term> and **Splendor** <term>Hebrew: *Hod*</term>. (A) And the great secret is: "With whom [Mi] did He take counsel, and who instructed Him [Binah], and taught Him the path of justice?" <note>Isaiah 40:14. The author reads the Hebrew word *Mi* ("Who") as a reference to the Sefirah of *Binah*.</note> And it says: "Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am Understanding, I have strength" <note>Proverbs 8:14</note>. The great secret according to the way of the Sefirot is: "And his name shall be called **Wonderful**, **Counselor**, **Mighty God**, **Everlasting Father**, **Prince of Peace**" <note>Isaiah 9:5</note>. 

"And his name shall be called **Wonderful**" — this is **Wisdom** <term>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</term>. In the beginning of the *Sefer Yetzirah* <term>The Book of Formation</term> it says "Wonderful" refers to Wisdom. "**Counselor**" — this is **Understanding** <term>Hebrew: *Binah*</term>. "**God**" — this is **Greatness/Kindness** <term>Hebrew: *Gedulah/Chesed*</term>. "**Mighty**" — this is **Strength** <term>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</term>. (B) "**Everlasting Father**" — this is **Beauty** <term>Hebrew: *Tiferet*</term>. "**Prince of Peace**" — this is **Foundation** <term>Hebrew: *Yesod*</term>, which includes **Victory** and **Splendor**. As the scripture said: "Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am (C) Understanding, I have strength." This explains the matter: know that the Great Sanhedrin of Above, called the "Great Court," is the place of **Strength** <term>*Gevurah*</term>. When they come to decree judgment upon all creatures, they consult and take counsel with **Understanding** <term>*Binah*</term>, which is above Strength, and with **Victory** and **Splendor**, which are below. This is the secret of "Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am Understanding, I have strength." 

The great secret is: "For the Lord of Hosts has counseled, and who [Mi] shall annul?" <note>Isaiah 14:27</note>. And the secret of "Who [Mi] shall annul" (E) is the secret of "With whom [Mi] did He take counsel, and who instructed Him?" For the **annulment of vows** is the secret of **Understanding**, and therefore it said "Who [Mi] shall annul." "**Who**" [Mi] is certainly the one who annuls, as it is the secret of the "Place of the Vow," and everything depends on Understanding (F). Since the prophets knew this great secret, they would nullify all decrees that were decreed in the Heavenly Court. This is the secret of: "A righteous man rules by the fear of God." <note>2 Samuel 23:3</note>.

The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "I rule over man, but who rules over Me? The **Righteous** <term>Hebrew: *Tzaddik*</term>, for I decree a decree and he nullifies it." This is the secret of: "And Moses besought [*Vayechal*] the face of the Lord his God" <note>Exodus 32:11</note>, for he raised his thought to the place where the decree is nullified. This is what our Sages of blessed memory meant when they said he implored Him (G) until He released Him from His vow. For **Understanding** is the place of the vow; it is the secret of the beginning of the seven Sefirot, and this is the secret of "And he besought" [*Vayechal*]. This is why the Sages of blessed memory said: "How do we know that a final decree can be torn up? As it is said: 'For the Lord our God is near whenever we call to Him'" <note>Deuteronomy 4:7</note>. 

This is the secret of: "For the Lord of Hosts has counseled, and who [Mi] shall annul, and His hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?" The explanation of the verse is thus: The Lord of Hosts counseled with the Great Sanhedrin of Above to decree judgment and to seal it. However, **Understanding**, which is the secret of **Repentance** <term>*Teshuvah*</term>, can annul it. This is "And **Who** [Mi] shall annul?" "And His hand is stretched out"—which is the secret of Strength—"**Who** [Mi] shall turn it back?" This means Understanding, which stands above it, can return it. Certainly, "The Lord of Hosts has counseled and **Who** [Mi] shall annul," for it is called the "Place of Releasing Vows," because the vow depends on the place of "**Who**" [Mi].

This is the secret of: "With **Whom** [Mi] did He take counsel and who **instructed** [Vayivinehu] him?" <note>Isaiah 40:14</note>. Certainly with "**Who**" [Mi] the Holy One took counsel and emanated Understanding and created the world; this is the secret of "And instructed him." This is the secret of the Place of Repentance. Therefore, even if a judgment is sealed above, Israel can nullify it through the power of Repentance, which is called "**Who**" [Mi]. This is "And Who shall annul" and "Who shall turn it back," for certainly "**Who**" [Mi] can annul <margin>PAI 3</margin> certainly.

<meta>This page continues from the previous discussion on the Sefirah of Victory (Netzach) and its role in divine decrees. The previous page established that while counsel begins in Understanding (Binah), it manifests through Victory (Netzach) and Splendor (Hod). Page 43 (labeled 47 in the margin) explores why the decrees of Victory are irrevocable and how this attribute relates to the architecture of Solomon's Temple.</meta>

The reason for this is that this attribute stands in a place that is not included in the category of "man," and therefore: "He is not a man" <note>1 Samuel 15:29: "The Glory of Israel [Netzach Yisrael] will not lie nor repent; for He is not a man, that He should repent."</note>.
But if the attribute of Victory stands below in the "heels of desire," it is possible to "repent" <note>In this context, "repentance" refers to God changing a divine decree or "changing His mind."</note>, for there the matter stands in the place called "Likeness" (A), as in: "the appearance of a man was upon it from above" <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>. But in the place where it is written, "He is not a man," there is no "repenting" <note>This suggests that at the higher level of the Sefirah Netzach, the divine will is absolute and unchanging.</note>. 

And by this path, contemplate how **Victory** <term>Hebrew: *Netzach*</term> stands to do good and perform kindness for Israel. By this path, contemplate every place where you find the language of "Victory," as it is written of Him that He is the one who grants victory over the enemies of Israel, and He stands at the right hand to do good for Israel. Thus it says: "Pleasures are at Your right hand forever [*Netzach*]" <note>Psalms 16:11</note>, and it says: "And also the Glory [*Netzach*] of Israel" <note>1 Samuel 15:29</note>. 

Know that there are twenty-four Heavenly Courts in the secret of the Name called **Victory**, and all of them are called **Victors** <term>Hebrew: *Netzachim*</term>. They are the ones who turn the scales toward the merit of Israel and overcome all those who stand on the "Left Side" <note>The "Left Side" (*Sitra Achra*) represents the forces of judgment and accusation.</note> and all the accusers. Therefore, the Scripture said regarding the accusing side of Babylon: "From generation to generation it shall lie waste; forever and ever [*Netzach Netzachim*] none shall pass through it" <note>Isaiah 34:10</note>. This means that as long as the Courts of "Victory of Victories" are in their permanence and high standing, the accusing side of the wasteland has no existence on any side, only destruction.

Know that corresponding to this attribute called Victory, which is also called **The Lord of Hosts** <term>Hebrew: *YHVH Tzevaot*</term>, King Solomon (B) made the right-hand pillar and called its name **Jachin** <term>Hebrew: *Yakin*, meaning "He shall establish"</term>. He who knows the secret of the two pillars, which are **Jachin** and **Boaz**, will know how the souls, spirits, and vital breaths fly (C) by means of the **Living God** <term>Hebrew: *El Chai*</term> and **The Lord** <term>Hebrew: *Adonai*</term> through the overflow of these two pillars. Thus it says: "The two pillars, and the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals which were on the top of the pillars" <note>1 Kings 7:41</note>. 

Behold, I am hinting: these "two pillars" are **Victory** <term>Netzach</term> and **Splendor** <term>Hod</term>. The "two bowls of the capitals on the top of the pillars" are **Greatness** <term>Gedulah/Chesed</term> and **Might** <term>Gevurah</term>. The "two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals" are **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term> and **Understanding** <term>Binah</term>. 

Know that by means of these two pillars and by means of the **Living God** <term>The Sefirah *Yesod*</term>, the souls, spirits, and vital breaths fly in the secret of the Tabernacle and through the "channels." And through this pillar called **Jachin**, the City of Zion—Jerusalem—was built and established. A sign for this is: "You have prepared [*Hakhin*] in Your goodness for the poor, O God" <note>Psalms 68:11</note>. If you understand these three words—"Prepared in Your goodness for the poor"—you will know how the **Lord of Hosts** prepares and sends goodness through the attribute of the **Living God** to pour out all the overflow and blessing into the attribute of **The Lord** <term>Adonai/Malkhut</term>, which is "empty" like a poor person who has nothing of their own. A sign for this (D) is: "Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together into one place, and let the dry land appear" <note>Genesis 1:9</note>.

# Gate 2

<meta>catchword: the one called</meta>

To receive the presence of the Lord, blessed be He, every single soul is clothed in these **Palaces** <term>Hebrew: *Heichalot*; the spiritual structures or "halls" through which divine light descends</term> according to the garment appropriate for it, and thus it clothes itself in these Palaces to receive the presence of the Lord, blessed be He. Within the places of these Palaces are hidden treasures from which all "masters of wisdom" draw sustenance, allowing them to enter and perceive the inner dimensions, the supernal secrets, visions, sights, and dreams. **Daniel**, the "man of delights" <note>original: *ish chamudot*; a biblical title for Daniel signifying his high spiritual standing</note>, was bound to those hidden treasures, and regarding this it is said: "And Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams" <note>Daniel 1:17</note>. In these Palaces, he would gaze through visions and "looking glasses" <note>original: *ispaklariyot*; a term for prophetic lenses or mirrors of perception</note>, and from them, he attained and understood all those great matters and interpretations, and all those visions he achieved (A) which are explained in the Book of Daniel. Many great and awesome matters exist within the treasures of the Palaces of **Victory** and **Splendor** <term>Hebrew: *Netzach* and *Hod*; the seventh and eighth Sefirot</term> which we shall yet awaken you to, with the help of God.

Know that the name "Lord of Hosts" <note>original: *YHVH Tzevaot*</note>, which is the "Pillar of the Right," is the one called **Victory** <term>Netzach</term>, as in the verse: "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory [*Netzach*], and the splendor [*Hod*]" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>. It is this Victory that sustains His kindness for Israel, as it says: "Has His kindness ceased forever [*la-netzach*]?" <note>Psalms 77:9</note>. This is the place from which good decrees are issued for Israel when it is attached to the **Supreme Crown** <term>Hebrew: *Keter*; the highest Sefirah</term>, and such a decree never returns [is never revoked]. This is the secret of what is said: "And also the Strength [*Netzach*] of Israel will not lie nor repent" <note>1 Samuel 15:29</note>. Because Israel always needs to attach themselves and strengthen themselves in the attribute of Victory—which is the secret of the Right Side that stands to overcome the Left—it is called **Victory** because it conquers the wars of Israel. Therefore, King David, peace be upon him, found it necessary to say in the Book of Psalms: "To the Chief Musician [*La-Menatzeach*] (B), a Psalm of David." Wherever he mentions "To the Chief Musician," it corresponds to the attribute of Victory [*Netzach*]. And wherever he mentions "Give thanks to the Lord for He is good," it corresponds to the attribute of **Splendor** [*Hod*]. The mnemonic for them is **Victory** and **Splendor**.

I must awaken you to a great and deep matter. Know that three lights shine from the "Whiteness of Providence," which is called (C) the **Eye of Mercy**; they are called **Kindness** [*Chesed*], **Victory** [*Netzach*], and **Beauty** [*Tiferet*]. When these three lamps shine and gaze into the **Sefirot** <term>Divine emanations</term>, then the whole world is in joy, gladness, and perfection. No trouble or evil occurrence happens, for the "Good Eye" watches over all creatures, and all the worlds stand in fullness and perfection. Sometimes the attribute called Victory (also called the Lord of Hosts), when it stands in its lower place, may decree a judgment for good; but sometimes it turns toward punishment, all according to one's deeds. However, if the attribute of Victory ascends through the "channels" and attaches to the **Supernal Victory** which is within the Eye of Mercy (meaning: every language is included in all that is good) and to the "Victory of Will" at the head of the Crown [*Keter*], it issues good decrees for Israel. Even if they later sin and become impoverished and unworthy of that good, it is not revoked. The reason is that the attribute of Victory has already ascended to the place that is "not called man," which is the place called the Crown. This is the secret of: "And also the Strength [*Netzach*] of Israel will not lie nor repent, for He is not a man, that He should repent" <note>1 Samuel 15:29</note>.

Perhaps this is why the early pious ones were meticulous in what they wrote [or did] regarding their graves; they intended to stand in the "Inner Garment," similar to the one who is "established," who said: "Do not bury me in white..." <note>A reference to the Talmudic story of Rabbi Yannai or similar sages giving instructions for their burial garments to avoid shame if they are resurrected among the righteous or wicked</note>. For others who will be in garments, even their deeds will look at them; it is necessary to repair the body in the likeness of the soul, and a physical action makes an impression above. Perhaps they intended to clothe them in the likeness of their garment which stands before them and has the power to receive them. For the soul that wrote [on] its body and overcame it, so the soul that desired to be clothed could look at those standing before it in sapphire-like garments according to its merit and preparation. # The Fifth Name of the Holy Names.

Following the order of the rungs <term>Hebrew: *Ma'alot*; the hierarchical levels of divine emanation</term>, this is the Name called **YHVH**, blessed be He. Know and believe that the name **YHVH**, blessed be He, is the **Pillar** in which all the Sefirot <term>the ten creative attributes or emanations of God</term>—both upper and lower—are unified. They are united in it from behind, from bottom to top, and they lean upon it from top to bottom. This Name stands like the **trunk of the tree**, while all the other holy names are like the branches of the tree; they all unite in it above and below and on all other sides. It is the one that unifies all the Sefirot through its letters, etc. Through them, all were created and sustained, and all the "Chariots" <term>Hebrew: *Merkavot*; the structures of the spiritual realms</term> in the world, upper and lower, are supported by it and look toward it. All the orders of the world, its foundations, and its buildings hang upon it, and there is nothing in all the worlds that is not dependent on and included within the name **YHVH**, blessed be He.

Before we enter into its explanation, we must inform you of a fundamental principle in which you will find rest and ease for many matters. Know that you will find this honored and awesome Name, which is **YHVH**, blessed be He, in the Torah in several contexts and several uses. Know that sometimes you will find it by itself in most of the Torah, as in "And the Lord spoke" <note>original: *Vayedaber YHVH*</note> or "And the Lord said" <note>original: *Vayomer YHVH*</note> and many other such instances. Sometimes you will find another of the holy names joined to it, as it says after the story of Creation: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day that the **Lord God** <note>original: *YHVH Elohim*</note> made earth and heaven" <note>Genesis 2:4</note>. You will not find in the entire account of the six days of Creation anything but the name **Elohim** <note>God, specifically as the attribute of Justice or Law</note> alone. But when the Torah began to speak of the perfection of creation in the section of "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth," it began to mention **YHVH Elohim**.

We must inform you of the reason for this. Know that since **YHVH**, blessed be He, is perfect and crowned and "full of all attributes," and within it all the Sefirot are unified, and through it all things and all creatures are completed and finished—as we have informed you—there was no need to mention it during the Work of Creation. This is because the world and its inhabitants were not yet in a state of perfection or completed action, nor was the world at its "fullness"; rather, all things were being made and coming into being. But when the creation of the world was finished and all things were perfected and completed in total repair <term>Hebrew: *Tikkun*; the state of spiritual harmony and completion</term>, then it mentioned **YHVH Elohim**, which are two names unifying with one another. This is because the name **Elohim** often "clothes" itself in the name **Adonai** <note>My Lord</note>, and then it is called **Adonai Elohim**, as we have informed you. When **YHVH** and **Adonai** are unified—which is the secret of **YHVH Elohim**—then all things are in complete perfection. And even though the name **Elohim** represents the secret of the attribute of **Strength** <term>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</term> and **Judgment** <term>Hebrew: *Din*</note>, as...

<margin>As will be explained later and as we informed you in Gate 5. Therefore the name **Elohim** is in all of them, as it is written there to speak and to learn these 20 names. According to this, the book of **Elohim** mentioned them all, which indicates that all things were completely finished. Therefore, now that the world was full, it mentioned **YHVH**. And the reason it mentioned **Elohim** and did not mention **Adonai** was to show the opposite: that the name **Elohim** indicates a greater unity, for the name **Elohim** points to **Strength** and to the "Dome" <note>the overarching divine influence</note> that flows into all of them and is included in the name as a memorial. Because of this, they are all called **Elohim**, a name that indicates a "Full World." For at a time like this, the attribute of **Mercy** <term>Hebrew: *Rachamim*</term> is clothed with the "What" <note>the numerical value of the name YHVH when spelled out as 45</note>, and every aspect performs its action in perfection. In this way, the entire matter proceeds in the explanation of why this name is called a "Full Name." You will already see the time when it is called a "Full Name" when it comes to the writing of **YHVH Elohim of Hosts**; that is the Full Name of the **Ancient of All** <note>original: *Atik de-Kola*; the highest, most ancient level of the Divine</note>, and more will follow.</margin>

And its structure is formed by the attachment of the Emanation <term>Hebrew: *Atzilut*; the process by which divine light flows into the world</term> to the Name **Adonai** <note>original: "אדנ'י"; traditionally translated as "Lord," here representing the tenth Sefirah, Malchut (Sovereignty)</note>. All the limbs of a human being receive their form and arrangement from this place. The secret of this is found in the verse: "He made you and established you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:6</note>. Now that we have informed you of this regarding the Name called **the Lord of Hosts** <note>original: "יי' צבאות"; YHVH Tzva'ot</note>, look into its other matters, secrets, and mysteries which we have already hinted at in this gate. Ponder how many keys and how many inner, celestial matters exist which are not appropriate to be spoken of explicitly, but only through hints, for "It is the glory of God to conceal a matter" <note>Proverbs 25:2</note>. And it is said: "The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him, and His covenant is to make them know" <note>Psalm 25:14</note>.

**And after we have informed you** of these general principles regarding the word "Lord of Hosts," it is proper for us now to explain the secret of the Seal according to the way of holiness, through the secret of: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory" <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>. Behold, the prophet, peace be upon him, said: "I saw the Lord sitting on a high and lofty throne" <note>Isaiah 6:1</note>. From the power of the *Vav* <note>The numerical value of the Hebrew letter Vav is 6</note>, they receive six wings. 

"And one called to the other and said: Holy, holy, holy." 
The **first "Holy"** is the secret of the drawing down of the holy emanation from the **Keter** <term>Crown; the highest Sefirah</term> until the Sefirah of **Gedulah** <term>Greatness, also known as Chesed or Lovingkindness</term>. 
The **second "Holy"** is the secret of the drawing down of the holy emanation from **Chokhmah** <term>Wisdom</term> until the Sefirah of **Gevurah** <term>Strength or Judgment</term>. 
The **third "Holy"** is the secret of the drawing down of the holy emanation from **Binah** <term>Understanding</term> until the Sefirah of **Tiferet** <term>Beauty</term>. 

Thus you have six Sefirot mentioned: three corresponding to three, where the [upper] three influence holiness upon the [middle] three. What is written after this? "**The Lord of Hosts**" <note>YHVH Tzva'ot</note>. This refers to the three Sefirot below them: **Netzach** <term>Victory</term>, **Hod** <term>Splendor</term>, and **Yesod** <term>Foundation</term>. The flow of abundance comes to them from **Gedulah**, **Gevurah**, and **Tiferet**, who in turn receive from **Keter**, **Chokhmah**, and **Binah**. Thus, nine Sefirot are accounted for. 

And into what do they pour their blessings and influence their powers? Into the tenth Sefirah, called **Adonai**, which is also called **Earth** <term>Hebrew: *Eretz*</term>. This is the secret of the end of the verse: "The whole earth is full of His glory." Behold, we have informed you of the secret of this verse regarding holiness and unity, the ten Sefirot, and the path of the emanation of abundance from the upper three (**Keter**, **Chokhmah**, **Binah**) to the middle three (**Gedulah**, **Gevurah**, **Tiferet**) and to the lower three (**Netzach**, **Hod**, **Yesod**). All the abundance of these nine Sefirot is poured into the tenth Sefirah, which is **Adonai**, called **Earth**. This is why it says, "The whole earth is full of His glory." 

Know and believe that one who answers "Holy" <note>during the Kedushah prayer</note> and focuses his intent on this blessing, specifically on the unification of the ten Sefirot, his portion is for life, the words of his mouth are accepted, and he is a son of the World to Come. 

The matter of how holiness is unified in this verse according to this order is as follows: 
**Holy** (first) is **Keter**. 
**Holy** (second) is **Chokhmah**. 
**Holy** (third) is **Binah**. 
What is written after? "**Hosts**" <note>Tzva'ot</note>. The secret of **Hosts** includes **Netzach**, **Hod**, and **Yesod**. 
What is written after? "**The whole earth is full of His glory**," which is the secret of the tenth Sefirah called **Adonai**, which is the "Land of the Living" and the "Light of Life."

<meta>This page continues the exploration of divine Names, moving from the Name of Hosts (Tzva’ot) to the combined Name "YHVH Elohim." It focuses on how the divine attributes of Judgment and Mercy balance one another through the Sefirah of "Justice" (Mishpat), associated with the patriarch Jacob.</meta>

# What is Gate 5
### M
<warning>Horizontal strip of semi-transparent tape across the middle of the page, partially obscuring lines 17-20.</warning>

A section in which the Name **YHVH Elohim** <note>original: "יה'וה אלהים"; this combination represents the unification of the attributes of Mercy (YHVH) and Judgment (Elohim)</note> is mentioned refers to actions performed through all the attributes that are completed by both the **Attribute of Judgment** <term>Hebrew: *Middat HaDin*; the divine quality of strict law and justice</term> and the **Attribute of Mercy** <term>Hebrew: *Middat HaRachamim*; the divine quality of compassion and grace</term>. You find this, for example, in the creation of the first man (Adam), in his judgment, and in his exile. In all those matters, you will find that they occurred through both Judgment and Mercy, all in perfect completion, with Mercy and Judgment applied exactly as is fitting in a **True Judgment** <note>original: "דין אמת"</note>. 

According to this principle, the Torah states: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is as follows: **The Rock** <note>original: "הצור"; a title for God as a firm foundation</note> who decrees judgment with strength does not act with cruelty. He does not decree judgment until **His work is perfect**, meaning the judgment He decreed was first deliberated upon by the two attributes: **Kindness** <term>Hebrew: *Chesed*</term> and **Judgment**. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect" <note>Hebrew: *Tamim*</note>. For the word *Tamim* <note>meaning perfect or complete</note> contains the secret of two things. It is as if one said **twins** <note>original: "תאומים"; *Te’omim*</note>, but the Torah uses the dignified term "perfect" (*Tamim*) when referring to the two celestial things above, and the term "twins" (*Te’omim*) for things below. 

Thus it says: "And they shall be doubled [twins] below... they shall be complete [perfect] at the top" <note>Exodus 26:24; referring to the construction of the Tabernacle</note>. Below they are called "twins," and above they are called "perfect." This is because below they appear as two separate things—opposites, like an advocate and an accuser—but above, everything is a single intention. Between the advocate and the accuser, both have one purpose; there is no hatred or love there, nor is there any favoritism, but only a **Judgment of Truth**. Therefore it says, "His work is perfect," meaning He deliberated with both Judgment and Mercy and then decreed the law. This is the secret of "True Judgment."

And regarding what is said, "For all His ways are justice" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, the explanation is that everything is visible to every seeing eye, as it says, "For all His ways are justice." You already know that **Justice** <term>Hebrew: *Mishpat*; representing the middle path or balance</term> is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy. For Justice corresponds to the patriarch **Jacob**, who is the "middle line" that balances between the "two tents" of **Abraham** and **Isaac**. 
*   **Abraham** corresponds to **Kindness** (*Chesed*).
*   **Isaac** corresponds to **Judgment** (*Din*).
*   **Jacob** mediates between them, as he is called "a perfect [simple] man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. 

Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Kindness on Abraham’s side and from Judgment on Isaac’s side. Thus it says: "**Justice** and **Righteousness** in Jacob You have made" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>. And the prophet said: "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation of the verse "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice" uses the word "but" <note>original: "אך"; *ach*</note> to imply a division—meaning, use only half of the attribute of Justice, which is the Kindness within it. Since Justice is half Judgment and half Kindness, he said "but with justice" <unclear>and afterward said "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing."</unclear> He revealed the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger. 

For this reason, Justice depends on Jacob, who is the <insert>Father</insert> of the tribes. He knew the great pain of children when the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees against them, so he seeks Mercy and Righteousness for them. The secret of "And the Lord of Hosts is exalted through **Justice**" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note> is followed by "and the holy God is sanctified through **Righteousness**." This means when Justice is exalted, the harsh Judgment is eased and makes way for the attribute of **El** <note>original: "אל"; a Name associated with kindness</note>. This is the secret of what is said: "And the holy God is sanctified through **Righteousness**" <term>Hebrew: *Tzedakah*; often used in Kabbalah to mean the softening of judgment through benevolence</term>. In general, when the Lord of Hosts is exalted through Justice, the attribute of *El*, which is higher, arrives and performs Righteousness, and the strict Judgment passes. This is the secret behind the saying that **Justice is included within Kindness and Judgment**, as it says, "Justice and Righteousness in Jacob You have made." 

The great secret is: "Righteousness and Justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. For "Righteousness" <note>Hebrew: *Tzedek*</note> can sometimes act as Judgment when it receives a certain flow, as I explained that *Tzedek* can be a very strong judgment. But when **Justice** (*Mishpat*) is joined with it, then the Throne is established in Mercy. And if it is exalted through Justice and reaches as far as Kindness and Truth together, they are called the **Shining Face**; then everything becomes great Mercy. This is the secret of "they shall come before...

This hints at "The Lord our God, the Lord is One." They have a single intention, for the ultimate purpose and essence is the distribution of Judgment and Kindness according to the recipients who are prepared for them through spiritual arousal. In the **Zohar** <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> on the portion of Balak, it says that the "Ancient of Ancients" <note>original: "עתיקא דעתיקין"; the most hidden, merciful aspect of God</note> looks upon all, and all is life, and everything becomes like the Sabbath and rest. When the light is rectified on the right, all Judgment is seen in the balance. Before anything was separated into the paths of the right or the support of the left, these were secrets given only to the holy head. And it is written, "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters..." <note>Psalm 29:3</note>. This is to say that "all His ways are justice." Justice is a revealed path, visible to all below, and not just hidden above. As it says, "For all His ways are justice," meaning it is a path revealed to the eyes of all who can recount it. Therefore, this is not written in secret. This is similar to what was said to Job... <unclear>regarding the concealment of counsel</unclear>. ### Gate 5 45
<meta>Handwritten "49" in top left corner of the page. Marginal note "10 f 107" in pencil on the right side of the text block.</meta>

A section which mentions **YHVH Elohim** <note>original: "יה'וה אלהים"; the combination of the Four-Letter Name of Mercy and the Name of Judgment</note>: these actions are performed through all the attributes that conclude in both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy. You find this, for instance, in the creation of the first man <note>Adam</note>, in his judgment, and in his expulsion—all these matters occurred through both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy. Everything was done in total perfection, with mercy and judgment each applied as was fitting for a true judgment. Based on this principle, the Torah states: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is as follows: "**The Rock**" <note>original: "הצור"; Ha-Tzur</note> refers to the One who decrees the sentence with strength, yet He does not act with cruelty. He does not decree the sentence harshly; rather, "**His work is perfect**." This means the judgment He decreed was first deliberated upon by the two attributes: Kindness <term>Hebrew: *Chesed*; the expansive force of giving</term> and Judgment <term>Hebrew: *Din*; the restrictive force of law</term>. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect" <note>original: "תמים"; Tamim</note>.

The word "**perfect**" <note>Tamim</note> contains the secret of two things. It is as if the text said "**twins**" <note>original: "תאומים"; Te'omim</note>, but the Torah uses an honorable term, "perfect," when referring to two celestial things, while using the term "twins" for things below. Indeed, the verse says: "And they shall be **twins** <note>Te'omim</note> from below... they shall be **perfect** <note>Tamim</note> at its head" <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below, they are called "twins"; above, they are called "perfect." This is because below, they appear as two separate things—opposites, like an advocate and an accuser. But above, they share a single intent. Whether it is the advocate or the accuser, both have one purpose. There is no "hatred" or "love" there, nor is there "favoritism," but only a judgment of truth. Therefore, it says "His work is perfect"—He deliberated with Mercy and Judgment and then decreed the sentence. This is the secret of a **true judgment**.

When it says, "For all His ways are justice" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, it means that everything is visible to the eye of any observer. You already know that **Justice** <term>Hebrew: *Mishpat*; the balance between kindness and severity</term> includes both Judgment and Mercy. Justice corresponds to the patriarch **Jacob**, who is the "middle line" that balances between the "two tents" of **Abraham** and **Isaac**. Abraham corresponds to Kindness (*Chesed*), and Isaac corresponds to Judgment (*Din*). Jacob decides between them, as it says: "A **perfect** <note>original: "תם"; Tam, related to Tamim</note> man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Kindness on Abraham’s side and from Judgment on Isaac’s side. Thus it says: "You have executed **justice and righteousness** in Jacob" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>.

The prophet also said: "Correct me, O Lord, but with **justice**; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation of this verse is: "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice"—the word "but" <note>original: "אך"; Ach</note> suggests a division, meaning: use only half of the attribute of Justice, which is the side of Kindness. Since Justice is half Judgment and half Kindness, he says "but with justice," and then adds "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing."
<margin>10 f 107</margin>
He revealed the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger. Because Justice is associated with Jacob—who is the "Chosen of the Patriarchs"—Jacob knew the great pain of children. When the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees a sentence upon them, Jacob seeks mercy and righteousness for them.

The secret of the verse "And the Lord of Hosts is exalted through **justice**" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note> is revealed in what follows: "And the holy God is sanctified through **righteousness**." This means that when the "Lord of Hosts" is exalted through justice, the severity of the judgment rests, making way for the attribute of **El** <note>original: "אל"; a Name associated with Chesed/Kindness</note>. This is the secret of: "And the holy God <note>El</note> is sanctified through righteousness." When the Name YHVH of Hosts is exalted through Justice, the attribute of El—which is higher—arrives and performs an act of righteousness, and the harsh judgment passes. This is the secret of what they said: Justice is included in Kindness and Judgment. And it says: "You have executed **justice and righteousness** in Jacob."

There is a great secret in the verse: "**Righteousness and justice** are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. For "Righteousness" <note>original: "צדק"; Tzedek</note> sometimes acts as Judgment according to how it receives its flow; it can be a judgment of great strength. But when "Justice" <note>Mishpat</note> is joined with it, then the Throne is established with Mercy. If it is exalted through Justice and reaches as far as Kindness and Truth together, they are called "The Shining Countenance," and then everything becomes great mercy.
