# Gate 6 Page 74

A place where you find the name **Elohim** <note>original: אלה"ים; often translated as "God," but in Kabbalah represents the attribute of Justice</note> so that you may know toward which side it leans. (A) I have already informed you, beloved of my soul, that the Great Name called **Y-H-W-H** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter Name associated with Mercy</note> (blessed be He) is alone the essence; He is the **trunk of the tree** that extends upward, downward, and to the sides. He clothes Himself in all other holy Names and other titles as I have informed you. According to the action that He (blessed be He) renews in His world, so He is called by that specific Name, changing according to that action. Therefore, He is sometimes called **Ehyeh** <note>"I Will Be"</note>, and called **Yah**, and called **Adonai**. He is called **Adonai of Hosts** (*Adonai Tzevaot*) and called **Elohim of Hosts** (*Elohim Tzevaot*). **Living God** (*El Chai*) or **God of Life** (*Elohim Chayim*). It is all according to the action He renews in the world; thus He wears the garment of the Name designated for that action. 

And behold, this Name called **Elohim** is the Name appointed over **Judgment** (*Din*). The sign (B) is that "Judgment belongs to **Elohim**" <note>Deuteronomy 1:17</note>. When He (blessed be He) performs an action from the side of Judgment, He is called by that action: **Elohim**. Now know and see that the side <gloss>(Meaning: for in the Attribute of Judgment there is right and left; above is a section to explain the matter, see the *Pardes* <note>Referring to the *Pardes Rimonim*, a foundational Kabbalistic text by Moshe Cordovero</note>)</gloss> designated before us as the **Left Side** is the essence of the "Law of God" (*Torat Elohim*). This is because that side is the place of Judgment, and in it all who enter the world are judged with all the appropriate decrees—whether for good or for evil, for life or for death. Within it are several established courts of law, and each completes its work and its judgments in truth and faithfulness, all with righteous judgment. This is what is called the **Heavenly Court** (*Beit Din shel Ma'alah*). There, creatures are judged for peace or for the sword, for famine or for plenty, for life or for death. This is the Name called **Elohim**, and everything is by law in His court. 

Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "A person is obligated to bless for the evil just as he blesses for the good" <note>Mishnah Berakhot 9:5</note>. And we seek proof for this matter—from where do we know it? Rabbah bar Hana said in the name of Rabbi Yohanan: The verse says, "In the **Lord** (*Y-H-W-H*) I will praise the word; in **God** (*Elohim*) I will praise the word" <note>Psalm 56:11</note>. "In the **Lord** I will praise the word"—this refers to the attribute of Goodness <term>The Attribute of Mercy</term>. "In **God** I will praise the word"—this refers to the attribute of Punishment <term>The Attribute of Judgment</term>. 

And now we must tell you that everything is judged in the Court called **Elohim**. If the judgment goes forth for good, the name **Ehyeh** or **El** is invoked. But if the judgment goes forth for punishment, it is called **Elohim**. Guard this well. You must contemplate that every place you find **Elohim** in the Torah, it is the attribute prepared to judge and decree upon all the world. 

We have already informed you in the gate preceding this how the **Great Sanhedrin** <term>The supreme celestial council of seventy-one elders</term> of on high stands between the Name called **Y-H-W-H** and the Name called **Elohim**. And how the **Attribute of Mercy** (*Midat HaRachamim*) mingles with the **Attribute of Judgment** (*Midat HaDin*) so as not to destroy the creatures at the time of judgment. Therefore, the Great Sanhedrin of on high is fixed to the left side between **Y-H-W-H** and **Elohim**, and it leans toward the left. Regarding this it is said: "Your navel is like a moon-shaped bowl, let it not lack mixed wine" <note>Song of Solomon 7:3</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "This is the Great Sanhedrin." Because it is written "The face of the **Ox** is on the left" <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>, the Great Sanhedrin is called by the language of *Sarakh* <note>A term implying a connection, attachment, or the umbilical cord/navel</note>. 

And the Torah of the Lord prepares a remedy for the sinner at the hour they judge him for his sins, so that he may have a connection (*Sarakh*) when he returns in repentance, as it is said: "It shall be a healing to your navel (*Sarkhekha*)" <note>Proverbs 3:8</note>. And the prophet proclaims and says that the most important thing is the healing, as it is said: "And he shall return and be healed" <note>Isaiah 6:10</note>. 

Now open your eyes and see that in the Great Court called **Elohim**, all the inhabitants of the world are judged, both the upper and the lower. We must inform you of the great principles upon which the world stands, which is the secret of the **Work of Creation** (*Ma'aseh Bereshit*). We shall enlighten your eyes regarding the secret of why the Name **Elohim** is mentioned throughout the entire Work of Creation. The secret is that all created beings, both upper and lower, were all created with the **Line of Law** and Justice. There is no creature among all creatures upon whom the Court called **Elohim** did not agree before it was created. This creature emerged from the judgment as it was fit to be: established in its height, the form of its limbs, its vitality, and its sustenance. And from the judgment it emerged that this creature would be subservient to a certain other creature, whether in the subservience of the body or the subservience of wealth. Thus was the law in all the Work of Creation and in every creature.

# Gate 6

“For all His ways are justice” <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, meaning the world was created with justice. For this reason, the Blessed Name is called **Elohim** <note>The Divine Name associated with the attribute of Justice</note> during the creation of the world. At the end of the Work of Creation, what does it say? “And **Elohim** saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good” <note>Genesis 1:31</note>. (2) Our Sages of blessed memory taught: even “death” is considered “good,” for the Attribute of Justice required it as a matter of upright law.

Behold, I am opening a great key for you: Why did the Blessed Lord see fit to command in the Torah to slaughter animals for human consumption, when it is written, “The Lord is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works” <note>Psalm 145:9</note>? If He is merciful, how could He command the slaughter of this beast for human consumption? Is this not a lack of mercy? Rather, the secret lies in the beginning of that verse: “The Lord is good to all.” He is certainly good. Therefore, “His mercies are over all His works.”

This is the explanation: During the Work of Creation, He consulted with this beast regarding its slaughter, and the beast said, “It is good.” What is the reason? Because a beast does not possess a higher soul to perceive the acts of God and His mighty deeds. The Blessed Lord, during the creation of the world, stood before the animals and said to them: “Is it your will to be slaughtered so that man may eat you? You shall then rise from the level of a beast—which knows nothing—to the level of a man, who knows and recognizes the Blessed Lord.” The animals replied: “It is good, and it is a mercy upon us.” For when a human eats a part of the animal, that part becomes a part of the human. Thus, the beast has been transformed into a human. Ritual slaughter (*shechitah*) <term>shechitah: the Jewish religious method of animal slaughter intended to be swift and humane</term> is a mercy for the animal, as it leaves the status of "beast" and enters the status of "human."

In this same way, the death of a human is actually “life” for them, as they rise to the level of the angels. This is the secret of the verse: “Lord, You preserve man and beast” <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. If so, contemplate and understand the secret of ritual slaughter—the killing of living creatures—and see that it is all a result of His mercies and His great kindness toward His creations.

What is the reason for this? Consider what our Sages of blessed memory said in Tractate Pesachim: “An *Am Ha’aretz* <term>Am Ha'aretz: literally 'person of the land,' referring here to one who is unlearned in Torah</term> is forbidden from eating meat.” This is because the Torah only commanded the slaughter of cattle, wild beasts, and fowl for one who knows the Torah. Anyone who occupies themselves with Torah is permitted to eat meat, but one who does not is forbidden. Therefore, an unlearned person does not eat meat because they are like a beast themselves, lacking a [higher] soul. The Torah did not command the slaughter of a beast just so another "beast" could eat it, unless the animal was already dying or torn.

Now that I have informed you of this, know that the Kabbalists—those who enter the secrets of the Torah’s mysteries—say that the beginning of creation and the "First Will" were drawn from the **Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom** (3). These are the secret of the beginning of creation included in the name **Elohim**. The *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an early and influential mystical text</note> opened its book by stating: "With thirty-two hidden paths of wisdom, Yah, the Lord of Hosts, engraved His world." Because these thirty-two paths were aligned with the line of Justice and Truth, you will find the seal of **Elohim** corresponding to each and every one of these thirty-two paths.

According to this secret, you will find that in the entire Work of Creation, no name is mentioned except **Elohim**. You will find the name **Elohim** written thirty-two times in the story of creation, corresponding to the thirty-two wonders of Wisdom. These are they, according to the order in which they are written:
1. "In the beginning **Elohim** created..." 
2. "...and the Spirit of **Elohim**..."
3. "And **Elohim** said, 'Let there be light'..."

5. "And **Elohim** divided..."
6. "And **Elohim** called the light..."
7. "And **Elohim** said, 'Let there be a firmament'..."
8. "And **Elohim** made..."
9. "And **Elohim** called..."
10. "And **Elohim** said, 'Let the waters be gathered'..."

This is according to its strength, for each exists within its Creator to be identified as its end, to be formed into another material after it was formed from it. # Gate 6

The **Heavenly Court** <note>Hebrew: Beis Din—a panel of judges</note> reached a consensus regarding the measurements of the body, the lifespan, the sustenance, the servitude, and the dominion of every single creature. Each and every being stood before the **Heavenly Court**, which is called **Elohim** <note>The Name of God associated with Law and Judgment</note>. They were cautioned and informed: “Know that the measure of your body shall be such; your limbs, your food, your life, your servitude, and your dominion shall be thus.” Every creature replied and said: “Behold, I accept all of this with joy and a good heart.”

This is what our Sages of blessed memory meant when they said: *“All the works of the Beginning were created with their own knowledge, they were created in their full stature, and they were created by their own desire.”* <note>A famous teaching from the Talmud, Tractate Chullin 60a</note> This means:
*   **With their own knowledge:** to understand everything that would befall them.
*   **In their full stature:** to understand the proportions of their bodies and the form of their limbs.
*   **By their own desire:** that they wanted and willed to accept everything upon themselves.

The reason for this great secret is that *“one cannot impose a liability upon a person except in their presence.”* <note>A legal principle: an obligation cannot be placed on someone without their consent or awareness</note> This means that one cannot be held to an agreement if they do not understand the essence and the reason behind it. Therefore, a creature might have complained, “I was too small to understand,” or “I did not yet exist, and one cannot be liable in one's absence.” Because of this, the Sages had to say that they were created with knowledge, stature, and desire—so that nothing exists in them that was not agreed upon by their own mind, form, and will.

After we have informed you of this great principle, we must return and inform you of the reason why **Elohim** is written throughout the entire account of the Work of Creation. It is to let you know that all **Created Beings** were created according to the "Line of Judgment" and integrity; there is nothing crooked or perverse in them. 

Now, since you find many creatures that differ from one another—some beautiful and some ugly—you might say that it was not through justice that this creature came out ugly and this one beautiful. You might ask: Who caused this one to be beautiful and that one to be ugly? What did the Blessed Lord see that led Him to create this one ugly and that one beautiful? Or, what sin did the ugly one commit against Him?

To this we respond: Know that the Blessed Lord created all beings with knowledge, stature, and will. He placed every single creature He created before Him and said to it: “Know that you shall have this form and these limbs, this servitude and this dominion. Now, if you desire this, speak; and if not, it is as if you were never created.” Every single creature replied and said: “I desire this, and I am happy with this great matter.”

This is the secret of what is said in the Work of Creation: *“And Elohim saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good.”* <note>Genesis 1:31</note> Our Sages explained: *“Behold, it was good”* refers to the Good Inclination; *“Very”* <note>Hebrew: Me'od</note> refers to death <note>Hebrew: Mavet—the Sages used a wordplay to suggest death is a necessary part of the "very good" design</note>. When the Blessed Lord created all beings in this form and with this nature, no claim remained in the world for any creature to say, “I was created unfairly.”

Because all the works of the Beginning were created through the "Judgment of Integrity" and Law, the name **Elohim** is mentioned throughout the story of Creation to say that all beings were created through righteous judgment and true law. From this righteous judgment, it emerged that this creature should be large and this one small; this one lives long and this one lives briefly; this one has a large body and this one a small body. This one flies, this one walks, this one leaps with its hands, this one with its feet, and this one swims upon the water. This one is round, this one square, this one long, and this one short.

Lest you say that these creatures suffered an insult or a wrong because they were made different from one another, the Sages established the blessing: *“Blessed be the Lord... who created you in judgment, sustained you in judgment, and will in the future raise you to eternal life in judgment.”* <note>Part of the blessing recited at a cemetery, emphasizing that all stages of life and death are governed by Divine Justice</note> 

Following this path, contemplate how all the works of the Beginning stood in rows upon rows before the **Heavenly Court** and were cautioned as we have said, and they replied, “It is good.” This is the meaning of: *“And Elohim saw all that He had made and behold, it was very good.”* 

After we have informed you of this, you must believe that the **Heavenly Court** called **Elohim** agreed upon every single creature and every single limb, deciding it was fitting to be exactly as it is. They set each on its base and established every creature and every limb of the body in its proper form, such that it is not fitting for it to be any other way, nor could it be better than this. This is the secret of *“In the beginning **Elohim** created.”* **Elohim** is the Creator, for all inhabitants of the world, those above and those below, were created through the line of Judgment and righteous law. No creature has suffered insult or wrong. This is what the Torah proclaims when it says: *“The Rock, His work is perfect...”* <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note> and what...

<summary>This page explains that every creature, regardless of its appearance or status, consciously consented to its physical form and destiny before the Heavenly Court (Elohim). This "pre-creation consent" justifies the diversity of life and the existence of death as parts of a perfectly just Divine plan.</summary>

# Gate 6

...the [limb] that sinned [while another] performed this commandment. If you punish this whole body because of the sin of the hand, then the eye is also stricken, and it is punished unjustly. This is the meaning of "killing the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous is treated like the wicked" <note>original: "le-hamit tzaddik im rasha"; a quote from Genesis 18:25</note>. Following this path, the **Attribute of Lovingkindness** <note>Hebrew: Middat ha-Chesed</note> prevents many calamities from coming upon the world. In this way, because of one righteous person who is in a place, calamity is delayed from coming to that place, so that the righteous person does not experience the pain of the local disaster. Just as we described the limbs in the body, so is the righteous person in a place like a limb in a body; from this perspective, the righteous person protects their location.

How does this protection work? When the people of a place are judged Above and the verdict is issued that they deserve destruction or punishment, the **Attribute of Lovingkindness** approaches and says: "Will You also destroy the righteous with the wicked?" <note>Genesis 18:23</note>. That is to say, the Attribute of Lovingkindness says to the **Attribute of Justice** <note>Hebrew: Middat ha-Din</note>: "If you punish these wicked people of such-and-forth place, the damage will reach the righteous person, who will suffer because of them when they are punished or their land is destroyed—and this righteous person did not sin to deserve such pain or damage." Thus, we find the righteous person protects the people of the place for the sake of ensuring that no damage or pain reaches him. Guard this principle very well. This is the meaning of "If I find in Sodom fifty righteous... I will forgive the whole place for their sake" <note>Genesis 18:26</note>. And so it continued until they reached ten <note><gloss>meaning: for the five cities of the region, according to the decree of the Higher Court</gloss></note>. This is the secret of what was said to Lot: "Behold, I have favored you concerning this thing also, that I will not overthrow the city" <note>Genesis 19:21</note>. However, Lot himself did not have the power to save Sodom through his own merit, even though he lived within it; even Lot was only saved through the merit of Abraham. As our sages interpreted the verse "Do not look behind you" <note>Genesis 19:17</note>: it means "do not look so closely as to suggest the city is worthy of being saved through your merit, for you are not worthy." This was said when they brought them outside. Guard this great principle for the whole Torah, for from it flow the "issues of life."

Likewise, guard another principle, which is the secret of this Torah portion. Although the matter is spoken in the name of Abraham—as it is written there, "And Abraham drew near and said: Will You also destroy the righteous with the wicked?"—it is also the secret of the **Heavenly Attribute of Lovingkindness** that always approaches the **Court of God** <note>original: Beis Din shel Elohim</note> at the hour He judges the creatures. It turns the judgment toward their merit and prevents many calamities in this manner. This portion comes to make known great secrets: how the Attribute of Lovingkindness always turns toward the merit of the creatures, and the **Attribute of Mercy** <note>Hebrew: Middat ha-Rachamim</note> joins with it to prevent many calamities from the world. This is what our Sages of blessed memory meant when they said: *"At first, He thought to create the world with the Attribute of Justice; He saw it could not endure, so He stood and joined the Attribute of Mercy with it."* This is what is written: "In the day that **YHVH Elohim** <note>YHVH represents Mercy; Elohim represents Justice</note> made earth and heaven" <note>Genesis 2:4</note>.

Behold, I am revealing a secret to you in this verse: **YHVH Elohim** corresponds to **earth and heaven**. **YHVH** corresponds to **earth** <note><gloss>the Name YHVH corresponds to earth because earth is mentioned before heaven in this verse</gloss></note>, and **Elohim** corresponds to **heaven**. This is to say that the Name (Blessed be He), which is **YHVH**, conducts Himself with the Attribute of Mercy toward the inhabitants of the earth, who are greater sinners. **Elohim** conducts Himself with Justice toward the heavens and their hosts <note>e.g., the angels</note>, who do not sin. This is why our Sages of blessed memory established the prayer: *"He who illuminates the earth and those who dwell upon it with mercy."*

Now that you know this, we must inform you of great principles: Everywhere you find the name **Elohim** written in the Torah, it is the secret of the **Heavenly Court**, as we will explain. We must inform you that there are two Courts Above <note><gloss>aside from other courts between them, such as the three courts of the High Priest</gloss></note>. The **Higher Court** among these is the Supreme Court, which is the **Attribute of Strength** <note>Hebrew: Middat ha-Gevurah</note> on the **Left Side** <note><gloss>called "True Elohim" everywhere, for it is the court of YHVH</gloss></note>. There sits the Great Sanhedrin <note>Supreme legislative and judicial council</note> of Heaven, and they judge the inhabitants of the world; this is what is called the **Attribute of Severe Judgment**. And the **Lower Court**...

# Gate 6

24: And God made the beast... 25: And God saw that it was good... 26: And God said... 27: And God created... 28: And God blessed them... 30: And God said to them... 31: And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. <margin>And now, my son, open [your eyes]</margin> **And now**, open your eyes and see how every single path of the <term>Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom</term> <note>A foundational concept in the *Sefer Yetzirah*, comprising the ten divine emanations (Sefirot) and the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet</note> is sealed with the seal of **God** <note>original: "Elohim"</note> to make known that everything created in the "Work of Creation" <note>original: "Ma'aseh Bereshit"; refers to the account of the six days of creation in Genesis</note> exists within the secret of each individual path. Everything exists through Law and true Judgment. This is what the Sages meant when they said: "He established it upon its base."

In the Midrash on Ecclesiastes, it teaches that He and His <term>Heavenly Court</term> <note>original: "Beit Dino"; literally, "His House of Law"</note> were consulted regarding every single limb of the body, for they were created according to the line of Justice. Concerning each and every one of them, the Heavenly Sanhedrin—which is called **God** <note>Elohim</note>—reached a consensus; they are all upright and represent true judgment. Behold, there is no path among the thirty-two paths that is not sealed with the seal of **God**. 

King Solomon proclaimed that all the works of creation, which were created through the name **God**, are worthy of existing forever, because they were all created with uprightness, justice, and absolute law. No creature requires any addition or subtraction to make it more perfect than it was made during the Work of Creation. This is what Solomon meant when he said: "Whatever God does, it shall be forever; nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:14</note>. 

If so, open your eyes and see that the Name called **God** <note>Elohim</note> is the Name appointed over Law and Judgment. He is the one who creates everything through judgment, and He is the one who brings all creatures to judgment. Solomon, peace be upon him, cried out and said: "For God will bring every work into judgment, including every hidden thing" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:14</note>. 

**Therefore**, you must understand that when the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create the world with Law, uprightness, and judgment through the name **God**, He arose and partnered with it the **Name of Mercy**, which is **YHVH** <note>The four-letter Name of God, often associated with Compassion</note>, so that creatures would be able to proceed slowly through the judgment of **God**. This is because creatures cannot endure if He does not conduct Himself with them through Mercy, due to the harsh judgment of the Great Sanhedrin called **God**. 

Therefore, He partnered the Name of Mercy with Him. This is the secret of the verse: "These are the products of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day that the **Lord God** <note>original: "YHVH Elohim"</note> made earth and heaven" <note>Genesis 2:4. Note the combination of the two names</note>. The name **God** <note>Elohim</note> is called the "Attribute of Harsh Judgment," meaning that it decrees judgment without any worldly consideration (a), but only according to the strict words of precision and the peak of the Law's sharp edge. 

This is (b) the secret of the <term>Chamber of Hewn Stone</term> <note>original: "Lishkat ha-Gazit"; the room in the Jerusalem Temple where the Great Sanhedrin sat</note>. Therefore, if creatures were judged in the Heavenly Court without the partnership of the Name of Mercy, the world would be destroyed and ruined according to the cutting edge of the Law. However, the Name of Mercy and Kindness intervenes in favor of the creatures' merit. If it finds no merit for them, it extends the time before the judgment is finalized Above. This is the secret of being "Slow to Anger" <note>original: "Erech Apayim"</note>. 

At every moment, the Attribute of Kindness intervenes for the merit of creatures while they stand in judgment before God. This is the secret of the verse: "And Abraham approached" <note>Abraham knew his attribute was Kindness</note> "and said: 'Will You indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Far be it from You to do such a thing!'" <note>Genesis 18:23, 25</note>. I shall now open for you the "Gates of Light" regarding this verse. What was the reason he said, "Far be it from You to do such a thing"? Does the Heavenly Court actually kill the righteous with the wicked? If so, that would not be a just law—yet it is written: "A God of faithfulness and without iniquity" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. 

Rather, the secret of this verse is deep, and I will hint at it. Know that the Attribute of Kindness intervenes for the merit of every single creature. If a person has performed both merits and transgressions, the Attribute of Justice comes to punish the person for the transgression, but the Attribute of Kindness says: "Even if the hand of a man has sinned and deserves to be punished, his eye is righteous and did not sin..."

# Gate 4
-> V <-

The nation and its land: The Holy One, blessed be He, willed that the <term>Prince</term> <note>original: *Sar*; refers to a high-ranking angel or spiritual representative appointed over a specific nation</note> appointed over that nation should judge his people according to the authority granted to him by the Blessed One throughout the year. Because he acts as a judge over that nation, he is also called "Elohim" <note>In Hebrew, the word *Elohim* can mean "God," "divine beings," or "human judges." The author is explaining how this title applies to angelic governors</note>. If that Prince's nation sins, the Blessed Name judges the Prince, strikes him, and punishes him. In this way, understand that the nations and their Princes are judged in the <term>Heavenly Court</term> <note>original: *Beit Din*; literally "House of Law"</note> of YHVH, blessed be He, who is the True God.

This is the secret behind the verse: *For YHVH your God is the God of gods* <note>Deuteronomy 10:17</note>. Know and believe that all the nations and their Princes—who are called "gods"—all come on <term>Rosh Hashanah</term> <note>The Jewish New Year, traditionally viewed as the Day of Judgment for all inhabitants of the world</note> to be judged before the Blessed God. If the nations have not behaved properly, their Princes are struck, and the flow of abundance and goodness that the Blessed God would have given them is diminished. When the Prince of a nation is struck, the nation falls. This is what the Prophet meant when he said: *YHVH will punish the host of the high heaven on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth* <note>Isaiah 24:21</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory also said: "No nation falls unless its Prince falls first." The reason is that whatever judgment is decreed upon the Prince of that nation is exactly what the nation receives, whether for good or for ill.

This explains the saying of our Sages: "The sinners of Israel [are punished] with their bodies, and the sinners of the nations of the world [are punished] with their bodies." The "body" refers to their Prince, for those who know the hidden secrets. Whenever the nations of the world sin, their Princes are struck for their crimes. This is what the Prince of Abimelech, King of the Philistines, meant when he said: *And I also withheld you from sinning against Me* <note>Genesis 20:6</note>. In Hebrew, the word "from sinning" (*me-chato*) is written without the letter *Aleph*, which implies it can be read as "needles" (*mechatim*). It is as if the Prince said to him: "Know that from the moment you sinned by taking Sarah, the wife of Abraham, they judged me in the Heavenly Court and stuck needles and thorns into me, and I am in great pain." For the "God" who spoke with Abimelech was actually the Prince of Abimelech; Abimelech was not worthy of prophecy or the speech of other angels, but only of his own Prince. Understand this well.

As for what they said regarding the "sinners of Israel in their bodies," this is the secret of the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*; often identified in Kabbalah with the *Shekhinah*, the Divine Presence and the spiritual collective of the Jewish people</note> for those who know hidden things. When Israel sins, the Assembly of Israel is punished, as it says: *And for your transgressions was your mother sent away* <note>Isaiah 50:1</note>.

Do not be confused by what we wrote in previous gates—that the Princes of the nations of the world can neither do good nor harm, or what the Sages established for us to say about the nations: *that they bow to vanity and emptiness and pray to a god who cannot save*. The intention there was to say that they have no power or authority of their own to judge for harm or for good. However, if God gives them permission, they carry it out because God placed the execution in their hands. Therefore, the Princes of the nations are called "gods" (*elohim*) over them.

Now, consider that every single nation among the seventy nations is judged throughout the year in its own court, which is the Prince of 그 nation, who is called "Elohim" for this reason. On Rosh Hashanah, all the Princes called "gods" and all their nations are judged in the Court of YHVH, blessed be He, who is the True God. Thus, even the "gods" of the nations are judged, even though they themselves judge the nations. This is the secret of the verse: *For YHVH God is the God of gods*—meaning He is the Judge who judges the gods of the nations. Keep this great principle and be careful with it, and you will understand deep, hidden secrets.

Know that the Blessed God warned Israel and said to them: "My children, I am your God and you are My people. You must not accept any of the gods of the nations as a power, for those gods were given to the nations and not to you; they belong to others and not to you, for I alone am your God." Therefore, God began the Ten Commandments by speaking the first two commandments directly without an intermediary, saying: *I am YHVH your God* <note>Exodus 20:2</note>. "Your God" certainly. If so, *You shall have no other gods*. This is why the Sages said that the commandments "I am" and "You shall not have" were heard directly from the mouth of the Almighty.

# Gate 6

The lower [dimension] is the secret of the Name called **ADonai**, and it is also called the **Lower Court**. It is also referred to as the **Weak Attribute of Judgment**. Within it, everything is brought to completion and finalized regarding all created beings, according to what was decreed in the **Upper Court**. Therefore, **ADonai** is also frequently called by the name **Elohim**. It is called **Elohim** at the moment the judgment is finalized—the same judgment that was decided by the Upper Court, which is called the **True Elohim**. In this way, you will find that the attribute of **Kingship** <note>original: *Malchut*; the final of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</note>, which is **ADonai**, is also called **Elohim** many times when it executes the verdict decided in the **Heavenly Sanhedrin** <note>The supreme celestial council or court</note>. Understand this well. Therefore, there is one principle to contemplate: anyone who acts as a judge—be they an angel or a human—is called **Elohim** during the time of judgment or when they are appointed as a leader over justice. This is why the Torah says: *The matter of both shall come before the judges (Elohim); whom the judges (Elohim) shall condemn, he shall pay...* <note>Exodus 22:8</note>, and it says: *You shall not revile the judges (Elohim)* <note>Exodus 22:27</note>. It also says: *For the judgment is God’s (Elohim)* <note>Deuteronomy 1:17</note>.

We must also reveal to you a hidden and sealed secret. The Torah says: *You shall not revile Elohim*, and although the plain meaning of the verse is not to curse a judge, it hints at another matter: if a person is struck by a blow, a plague, an illness, death, or loss, they should not be brazen toward the Upper Court called **Elohim**—which is the place of true justice—and they should not speak blasphemies or insults, saying: "God <unclear>mentioned above</unclear>, because of Him these troubles came upon me." A person might open his mouth without restraint, as the Sages said regarding Job’s wife: *Do you still hold fast to your integrity? Curse God (Elohim) and die!* <note>Job 2:9</note>. Rather, one should speak as Job did: *Shall we receive good at the hand of God (Elohim), and shall we not receive evil?* <note>Job 2:10</note>. This is why a person is obligated to bless [God] for the bad just as they bless Him for the good. As David said: *In YHVH I will praise His word, in Elohim I will praise His word* <note>Psalm 56:11</note>. This is the faith of Israel: to receive the judgments of God with joy, to rejoice in His discipline, rebukes, and decrees, to give thanks before Him for everything, and to bless His Name, as it is said: *I will sing of mercy and judgment* <note>Psalm 101:1</note>—if it is mercy, I will sing; if it is judgment, I will sing. A person should not rebel against suffering or let harsh words escape their mouth. All of this is hinted at in the verse: *You shall not revile Elohim*. This is the general rule: every judge in the world and all courts, upper and lower, are included in this verse.

Now that we have informed you of this, we must hand over to you a great principle; guard it carefully, for many who consider themselves wise have stumbled and failed to understand it. It is the secret of what is meant by **"Other Gods"** <note>original: *Elohim Acherim*</note>. We must inform you that the Name—may He be blessed—the High and Exalted One, who dwells forever and whose Name is holy, He alone is King over all existence. His Holy Temple is positioned in the center, and surrounding the Holy Temple are seventy **Crowns**. From these proceed seventy **Princes** and seventy **Nations**, as has already been explained. All seventy Princes were divided during the **Generation of Division** <note>The Tower of Babel</note> according to their languages and lands; seventy Princes for seventy nations, so that each Prince would rule over his own nation and land. But YHVH, blessed be He, arose and chose **Abraham** in that generation, and He chose **Israel** after him, who are the seed of Abraham. He gave them His Great Name so that they would be His portion and inheritance. His Great Name—which is **YHVH**, blessed be He—is called upon all of Israel, and no other nation has a portion in it, as it is written: *And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of YHVH is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you* <note>Deuteronomy 28:10</note>. And it says: *For YHVH’s portion is His people* <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. Because YHVH, blessed be He, placed all other nations of the world in the hands of the Princes—each nation to a specific Prince—as the scripture says: *The Prince of the kingdom of Greece... and the Prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me* <note>Daniel 10:20, 13</note>. But **Michael**, the Great Priest, who carries the banner of YHVH, blessed be He, was assigned to Israel. The other seventy Princes are on the "outside" and have no portion in the Inner Temple; each of them is designated to a specific nation and rules over that nation.

# Gate 6

The names of the **Great Heavenly Sanhedrin** <note>The supreme celestial council or court</note> are called **Elohim** in truth. Even human beings are called **Elohim** <note>original: *elohim*; commonly translated as "judges" or "lords" in this context</note> when they judge a true judgment. Now that we have informed you of these principles regarding the Name called **Elohim**, we must return and inform you of the other names by which the Name **Elohim** is sometimes called.

Know that this attribute called **Elohim** is sometimes called **Gevurah** <note>original: *Gevurah*; meaning Might, Strength, or Severity; the fifth of the ten Sefirot</note>. The reason is that it arises from the "strengthening" <note>original: *mit-gavret*</note> to execute judgment upon transgressors and sinners; it is that which rises up against the hands of the wicked and those who rebel against the Blessed Name. Since it is the **Upper Court of Justice** and provides the full recompense to all who deserve it, it is called **Gevurah** due to its power and dominion. It possesses the ability to judge, to exact punishment, and to prevail over all, and nothing can stand before it. This is what the prophet said:

<margin>Isaiah 51:9</margin>
-> Awake, awake, put on **strength**, O arm of the Lord! <-

And he said: *Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab in pieces, and pierced the dragon?* <note>original: *Ha-lo at hi ha-machzevet Rahab...*; Isaiah 51:9. "Rahab" and the "dragon" are symbols of chaotic or oppositional forces</note>. If not for its "Mights" <note>original: *Gevuroteiah*; the plural manifestations of Power</note>, judgments would never be finalized and the powerful would never be punished. But because the **Gevurah** is strong and rules over all, the judgments decided in its Court are brought to completion.

Do you not see that when Israel sinned, the **Gevurah** was weakened by their sins? Thus the prophet said: *Where is thy zeal and thy **Gevurah** (strength)?* <note>Isaiah 63:15</note>. And the **Gevurah** responds, saying: *Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee* <note>Deuteronomy 32:18; the Hebrew word "tashi" (unmindful/weakened) is interpreted here as the weakening of the Divine Power</note>. According to the sins of the sinners, the **Gevurah** is weakened and the "Right Hand" is turned backward. So it says: *He hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy* <note>Lamentations 2:3</note>.

Know that above the side of **Gevurah** is the Source and the Influence from which the **Gevurah** draws. From that Source, which is superior to **Gevurah** and is called **Binah** <note>original: *Binah*; meaning "Understanding," the third Sefirah</note>, many types of "Might-powers" flow, and they are called **Gevurot**. This is what is meant by: *Who can utter the **Gevurot** (mighty acts) of the Lord?* <note>Psalm 106:2</note>. When Israel are righteous, those **Gevurot** influence their powers into the attribute called **Gevurah**, and then Israel prevails over the nations. This is because **Gevurah** is the force that fights against the nations to take Israel’s vengeance from the enemy. But if, Heaven forbid, Israel sins, then the attribute of **Gevurah** remains weakened and does not act to take vengeance on the nations. This is the meaning of: *The Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful* and *Where is thy zeal and thy **Gevurah**?*

Understand this: from this attribute, it is called the **Upper Court of Justice**. Through this attribute, all the inhabitants of the world are judged—as we have said—for good or for evil. This place is also called **Zakhut** <note>original: *Zakhut*; usually translated as "merit," but also related to "clarity" or "purity"</note> because in it all merits and all sins are remembered. Even the "evil" <note>punishment</note> given from there is also called **Zakhut**, because through it, a person is purified from sin.

From the power of this **Great Sanhedrin**, three other courts emerge that judge the inhabitants of the world regarding wealth and poverty, health and sickness. All judgments in the world are decided in the **Great Sanhedrin** and in these three courts of hers—except for three things which are not judged in the Court of **Elohim** at all. Rather, they are drawn from a higher place of **Mercy** <note>original: *Rachamim*</note>. These are: **Life**, **Children**, and **Sustenance**.

Even if they decreed in the Court of the **Great Heavenly Sanhedrin** regarding these three things, if a person stands and focuses his prayer until the "Place of Will" <note>original: *Makom ha-Chefetz*</note>, he may obtain his request. This is what the Sages of blessed memory meant when they said: *Children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit (Zakhut), but rather depend on Mazal* <note>original: *Banee, chayyei, u-mezonee... be-mazla talya milta*; Babylonian Talmud, Moed Katan 28a</note>.

The matter of "Merit" <note>original: *Zakhut*</note> mentioned in this context is the secret of the **Great Sanhedrin**. The matter of **Mazal** <note>original: *Mazal*; literally "constellation," but here referring to the highest flow/drip of divine influence</note> mentioned in this context is the secret of the **Supreme Source**, which is the source of "Will" <note>original: *Chefetz*</note> called **EHYEH ASHER EHYEH** <note>original: *Eh-yeh Asher Eh-yeh*; "I Will Be What I Will Be" or "I Am That I Am," the Name revealed at the Burning Bush</note>. From there, the waters of Will and Desire flow. This is the **Mazal** upon which all things depend—even the Torah Scroll in the Sanctuary. Therefore it says:

-> Everything <-

<gloss>
(א) *Awake, awake:* As mentioned above, and as will be explained in its place at the beginning of Gate 9. *Awake, awake, put on, etc.*: You already know that this verse is taken from the "Arms of the World."
(ב) *Art thou not it that hath cut:* Speaking of the **Gevurah** in the feminine language, for she executes her judgment through the **Kingship** <note>original: *Malchut*</note> of the lower world.
(ג) *And the Gevurah was weakened:* Meaning the Gevurah is weakened by their sins, resembling an afflicted woman at this time.
(ד) *And to say, "The Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful":* This comes to mean that because he sinned, it is as if the power is weakened.
(ה) *As it says, "He hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy":* Meaning that the sin of the generation prevents the finding of merit before the enemy, and she [Gevurah] is not strengthened to take vengeance on the nations.
(ו) *Because in it a person is purified from sin:* And in the **Book of Zohar**, it is explained that it is called **Zakhut** because they always begin there with "merit" (*zakhut*), the opposite of the "Daughter of Iniquity" which is always cursed with "guilt" (*chovah*).
(ז) *Three other courts:* As is their custom.
</gloss>

# Gate 6

<meta>catchword: from the attribute</meta>

...we heard them from the **Might** <note>original: *Gevurah*; referring to the Divine Attribute of Severity/Judgment</note>. These two commandments <note>The first two of the Ten Commandments: "I am the LORD" and "You shall have no other gods."</note> are the essence of the entire Torah, and therefore we heard them from the mouth of the Almighty; whereas the rest of the commandments of the Torah we heard from the mouth of Moses. From where do we know that we heard "Torah" from the mouth of Moses? Because the word *Torah* has the numerical value of 611 commandments <note>In Hebrew Gematria, *Torah* (ת-ו-ר-ה) equals 611. 400+6+200+5 = 611. Adding the two commandments heard directly from God equals 613</note>, and they are the "Secret of the Torah." Regarding this, it is said: *Moses commanded us a law [Torah]*; for through Moses, 611 commandments were given to Israel. However, *I am the Lord* and *You shall have no other gods* were not received through Moses, but rather they heard them from the mouth of the **Might** (a) <note>original: *mi-pi ha-Gevurah*; "from the mouth of the Might" is a traditional idiom for God's direct speech</note>, as it says: *God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this* <note>Psalm 62:11</note>. Thus there are 613 commandments: two were heard from the mouth of the **Might**, and the remaining 611 were the "Secret of the Torah" heard from the mouth of Moses. This is why the scripture was precise in saying *Moses commanded us a Torah*, referring to those 611 commandments.

Based on this principle, the Blessed Lord said to Israel: *My children, you shall have no other gods*, for they have no portion in you, and you have no portion in them, for *the LORD’s portion is His people*. Now that you know this, contemplate what the prophet said: *For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever* <note>Micah 4:5</note>. You must not believe the empty words of certain vain people who say that the "gods" of the nations have no power and are not called "gods" <note>original: *elohim*</note>. Rather, you should know that the Blessed Lord gave power, dominion, and a scepter into the hand of every **Minister** <note>original: *Sar*; a celestial patron or angelic governor</note> among the ministers of the nations to judge and govern his people and his land. That minister is called by the name **Elohim** because he is a prince and a judge over the people of his land. However, in the end, all the ministers and all their nations come to be judged in the Court of the LORD, who is called the **True God** <note>original: *Elohim Emet*</note>. If the nation of a minister sins or goes astray, woe to the minister, for he is stricken on account of the nation in his land.

Know and believe that there is no independent power in "other gods" which are the gods of the nations, except for that specific power given to them by the Lord to judge and sustain their nation. They cannot, however, strike or heal, kill or give life, outside of that known power granted to them over the inhabitants of their land and dominion. This is the meaning of *For all the gods of the nations are idols* <note>Psalm 96:5</note>. The meaning of **idol** <note>original: *elil*</note> is like "dead human flesh." According to the debate of the Sages in the tractate Chullin, the term *elil* always denotes something dead; this is also the meaning of *you are all physicians of no value* <note>original: *rof'ei elil*; Job 13:4</note>, referring to flesh for which there is no cure. Thus, the gods of the nations have no power to do good or evil, except for that allotted power which the Name [God] transmits to them. They cannot deviate from that line; they are like **subjects** <note>original: *kandonin*; likely referring to officials or subjects bound by law</note> just as the people of their land are judged. All their power and dominion is merely the "stipend" they receive from the Name of the Blessed LORD, who is the Master and Judge over them all. 

Now, guard this principle for the entire Torah, and you will be able to know the meaning of the name **Elohim** in every place, or the name "other gods," as in: *your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood... and they served other gods*, or *You shall have no other gods*. Now that we have informed you of these great principles, we must inform you of another great principle: you must know and contemplate that the "Place of Life" called **Eternal Life** is the secret of **Binah** (b) <note>original: *Binah*; Understanding, the third Sefirah and the source from which judgment flows</note>. This is the Name written in the Torah as **YHVH** <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> but pronounced as **Elohim**. The reason is that it is the source from which the attribute of **Gevurah** (Might)—called the "Upper Court" and named **Elohim**—draws its strength. Because it is not absolute judgment, it is written with the letters **YHVH**, but because it is the root from which the attribute of Judgment draws when called **Elohim**, it is read as **Elohim**, even though it is only written with the letters **YHVH**. Guard this great principle for every place you find in the Torah where it is written **YHVH** but read as **Elohim**. 

After you know this, know that the two attributes called **Netzach** <note>Victory/Endurance</note> and **Hod** <note>Splendor/Majesty</note> are as follows: **Netzach** is called **YHVH of Hosts** <note>original: *YHVH Tzevaot*</note> because it is on the Right. **Hod** is called **Elohim of Hosts** <note>original: *Elohim Tzevaot*</note> because it is on the Left. Because it clothes itself in the garment of Judgment from the Court called **Elohim**, it too is called **Elohim of Hosts**. Ultimately, every single attribute is named according to the place from which it draws. In every place in the Torah where a thing in the world is called by the name **Elohim**, know that it is drawing power from the attribute...

# Gate 10

<meta>Catchwords: "from the attribute", "And they were finished". Archival pencil mark "83" at top left.</meta>

...masters of destruction. He commanded in the Torah that every sacrifice brought for a sin must be slaughtered in the **North** <note>original: *tzafon*; in Jewish mysticism, the North is associated with the attribute of Judgment and Severity</note>. As it says: *And he shall kill it on the side of the altar northward* <note>Leviticus 1:11</note>. The sacrifice slaughtered in the North is brought for the sins a person commits, whether by an individual or the community—such as the bull and goat of **Yom Kippur** <note>The Day of Atonement</note>, the burnt offerings that are consumed, the goats that are consumed, communal peace offerings, guilt offerings, and the sin offerings of both the community and the individual. All of these are slaughtered in the North. And if you should ask: "Behold, there are communal peace offerings which are not brought for sin or guilt, [why are they in the North]?" Know that they are compared to the sin offering, as the scripture says: *Then ye shall sacrifice one kid of the goats for a sin offering, and two lambs of the first year for a sacrifice of peace offerings* <note>Numbers 7:16-17; the text links these two types together</note>. However, the peace offerings of an individual, the thanksgiving offering, the ram of the **Nazarite** <note>one who has taken a vow of holiness and abstinence</note>, the firstborn animal, the tithe, and the **Passover** offering—none of these are required to be slaughtered in the North; rather, their slaughtering may take place anywhere in the Temple Courtyard <note>original: *Azarah*</note>, and the reason for all this is explained. Since sacrifices serve as a ransom <note>original: *kofer*</note> for a person to protect them from "striking," as it is written: *and let us sacrifice to the LORD our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword* <note>Exodus 5:3</note>. These types of retribution originate from the North; therefore, the Blessed Lord commanded that every sacrifice brought for a sin should be slaughtered in the North. With God's help, regarding these matters, we shall yet inform you (a) of great principles regarding the reasons for the sacrifices. Since the attribute of the name **Elohim** <note>The Divine Name associated with Justice and Judgment</note> is the secret of Judgment and stands in the North, the sacrifices brought for sin are slaughtered in the North. The secret is: *The sacrifices of God [Elohim] are a broken spirit* <note>Psalm 51:19</note>; understand this well. Now that we have informed you of these great principles, you must know that because the **Supreme Court** <note>original: *Beit Din ha-Elyon*</note> called **Elohim** sits on the Northern side, the sacrifices brought for sin are slaughtered in the North to be an atonement before the Heavenly Court. Know that on the Northern side above, outside the **Curtain** <note>original: *Pargod*; the celestial veil separating the Divine Presence from the lower realms</note>, there is a "Great Slant Serpent" <note>original: *Nachash Akalaton*; a primordial symbol of chaos or the inclination toward evil</note>. He is the one who caused death for **Adam**, the first man, and cast impurity <note>original: *zohama*; a spiritual filth or infection</note> into **Eve**. He is the head of all retribution. Therefore, the Blessed Lord promised Israel to remove him, distance him, and cast him to a place where he can never again act as an accuser <note>original: *le'katerig*; to prosecute or act as a legal adversary in the divine court</note>. The prophet said: *But I will remove far off from you the northern army [the Northerner], and will drive him into a land barren and desolate* <note>Joel 2:20</note>. <margin>Another version: Explanation</margin> (b) This is tied to the matter called the **End of All Flesh** <note>original: *Ketz Kol Basar*; often identified with the Angel of Death</note>, for he consumes from the soul to the flesh. He entered to accuse the **Generation of the Flood**, and they were delivered into his hand. This is what is meant by *The end of all flesh is come before me* <note>Genesis 6:13</note>; that is to say, the attribute of Retribution, which accuses all creatures, came before Me and accused them because *the earth is filled with violence*. The judgment was finalized, and He delivered them into the hand of the **End of All Flesh** to destroy them. Regarding this, it is said: *and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth*. Since this attribute, prepared for retribution, is fixed in the North, the Blessed Lord commanded that sacrifices for sin be slaughtered in the North. But in the time to come, when sacrifices are destined to cease, God will distance the attribute of Retribution from us and lead it away from the Northern side to a place where it can no longer accuse. And just as the action of the service of retribution...

Just as in the times explained by the **Gemara** <note>The part of the Talmud containing rabbinical analysis and commentary</note>, where it describes bringing in people contrary to the law, wild beasts, and from death comes "consuming fire" to test nations and destroy kingdoms—so too, it mentions a spiritual parallel to this in the higher powers: evil spiritual matters and angels of death, may the Merciful One save us. This is to discipline the transgressors and those who inherit [punishment], as I wrote above in **Gate 5** regarding the level of the "husks" <note>original: *Kelipot*; the outer shells of evil that conceal divine light</note> in the order of the *stormy wind and the cloud*, etc. And with God's help, we shall inform you in these words (a) of the great principles regarding the reason for the sacrifices. Also, my heart has followed His paths to investigate further into the matter of the sacrifices and the silencing of the mouths of the accusers. I did not worry [about the difficulty], for my findings are intended for those beginning their contemplation, as these are like books on the Torah. (b) And this is the connection to the matter called the **End of All Flesh**, the **Angel of Death**. Like **Korah** <note>The biblical rebel who was swallowed by the earth</note>, he can also forgive and ascend to offer a burnt offering, yet he also accuses and consumes all flesh to sustain himself. His end is, so to speak, as his name and his power, as explained in Gate 5 in the explanation of the **Unique Name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note>.

# Gate 6

<meta>image quality: good, aged manuscript; catchword: And like</meta>

"Everything depends on **Luck** (A), even the Torah Scroll in the Sanctuary." <note>original: *Mazal*; though usually translated as "luck" or "constellation," in Kabbalah it refers to the supernal flow of divine energy from the highest sources</note> And do not let it enter your mind that the Sages, of blessed memory, spoke of the astrological constellations of the stars in this place; rather, they spoke only of the "Place of Will," and this is sufficient for those who understand. We have already explained these matters in the previous Gates.

Know that this **attribute** <note>a *Sefirah* or divine quality</note> is called **North** (*Tzafon*). You must understand the root principle: we have already informed you that the attribute of **Loving-kindness** (*Chesed*), which is on the Right, is always open and ready to provide for anyone who asks. When a person asks and seeks their desire from God, the attribute of Loving-kindness is awakened and draws from the "Source of Will" all types of wealth and all types of goodness to give the seeker enough for their needs. 

However, when those gifts and benefits arrive from the side of the **Left**, the attribute of **Judgment** (*Din*)—which is the side of the North—stands up and prevents the Right from completing the seeker's desire. It says: "Let us sit in judgment and see if this seeker is worthy of being given what they have asked for or not." Then the seeker is judged in the **Great Sanhedrin** <note>the supreme celestial court</note> that stands in the North. If they are worthy, their request is granted. If they are not worthy, all that wealth and goodness that the attribute of Loving-kindness had drawn down is withheld from them. 

Then that attribute in the North receives all that wealth and goodness and brings it into its treasuries and storehouses in the North. That wealth remains in the treasuries of the North because once the attribute of Loving-kindness has drawn it down, it does not (B) return to its source. Instead, the Great Sanhedrin in the North receives it. Therefore, it is called **North** (*Tzafon*) because all types of wealth, hidden things (*genuzim*), and secrets (*matzpunim*) dwell there, as well as all gold. Thus it says: *Out of the north comes gold* <note>Job 37:22</note>. Because that place is called North, it is the place of hidden and secret things and all types of wealth. 

The Sages, of blessed memory, said: "He who desires to become wealthy should face North" <note>Talmud, Bava Batra 25b</note>—meaning, he should direct his intention toward the attribute of the North to make peace with the attribute of Judgment that stands there, so that it does not hinder his request when he asks God, may He be blessed, for wealth and possessions. It was for this reason that the **Table** <note>the *Shulchan* in the Tabernacle which held the Showbread</note> was placed in the North, for from there wealth and the needs of creatures are drawn. Since the North is on the left, the Scripture says: *Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor* <note>Proverbs 3:16</note>. 

Know that all this wealth and all these secrets in the North are hidden and guarded, prepared for the righteous in the world to come. Thus it says: *How great is Your goodness which You have hidden (tzafanta) for those who fear You...* <note>Psalms 31:20</note> and it says (C) *He stores up (yitzpon) sound wisdom for the upright* <note>Proverbs 2:7</note>.

After we have informed you of this, know that on the side of the North there are <margin>(meaning: **Hell** <note>original: *Gehenna*</note>)</margin> great places and chambers filled with many **angels of destruction** and many types of punishments. There are many wells of murky water, mire, mud, and "miry clay" <note>original: *tit hayon*; see Psalm 40:2</note> that descend to the abyss. There are many types of pits, and many types of snakes and scorpions and all other types of (D) wild beasts. All of these that we have mentioned stand and watch for when the judgment that is in the North will go forth to destroy, or to uproot, or to tear down kingdoms, and to strike human beings with every type of blow and every type of destroyer. Then each of these types of punishment in the North goes out and roams the world, executing judgment on all those who were found guilty in the Court Above. Regarding all of these, it is said: *Out of the north the evil shall break forth* <note>Jeremiah 1:14</note>. 

Know that in this place there are many informers and many accusers who prosecute humanity. Because God, may He be blessed, gave the Torah and commandments out of His great mercy for Israel, He commanded them to offer **sacrifices** (*Korbanot*) before Him to atone for sins, in order to silence these accusers in the North and all the masters of...

---

Three houses of the Sanhedrin—the small ones of twenty-three members—sit before the Great Sanhedrin, for this is the pattern: as the upper things are made, so are the lower. And so it is below in the "cave" at the entrance of the building. 

(A) **Even the Torah Scroll in the Sanctuary:** This refers to the attribute of *Tiferet* <note>Beauty/Harmony</note> within the Holy of Holies. 

(B) **Do not return to their source:** For once it has descended, it is "given" and they do not "return and take" it back. 

(C) **He stores up sound wisdom for the upright:** Meaning, for <unclear>those</unclear> who were found liable by the <unclear>mark</unclear> of their <unclear>birth</unclear> below and were mixed into the North. 

(D) **Other types of beasts:** One must understand that there are literally "wild beasts" and "scorpions" above and things similar to them—but they are all spiritual forces that resemble them, born from the "squads of Judgment" as we have mentioned many times. These are damaging forces and various types of destroyers, such as "snakes" and "scorpions" and "wild beasts." This is <unclear>clear</unclear> because all these things are metaphors, and as is the way below, so His power made the spiritual pattern above.

<meta>Continuity Note: The previous page established that the "North" is associated with the attribute of Divine Judgment (Gevurah) and the celestial court. This page explores how this attribute—specifically called "Fear"—manifested in the life of the patriarch Jacob and how it relates to the afterlife and daily prayer.</meta>

# Gate 6 Page 84

The Torah states: **"An Aramean sought to destroy my father"** <note>original: *Arami oved avi*; Deuteronomy 26:5. While often translated as "A wandering Aramean was my father," the Passover Haggadah and Kabbalistic tradition interpret it as "An Aramean [Laban] sought to destroy my father [Jacob]"</note> because Laban sought (A) to uproot everything—root, branch, and fruit. Jacob (B), however, grew strong through the **attribute of Fear** <note>original: *Middat ha-Pachad*; this refers to the Sefirah of Gevurah/Judgment</note> which came to assist him. He began to demonstrate his might and power against Laban, as the scripture says: **"Jacob became angry and took up his grievance with Laban."** <note>Genesis 31:36</note> Now, if Jacob was physically weak, how could he dare to quarrel with the powerful Laban? Rather, know that the attribute of Divine Fear came to Jacob’s aid. 

What is our proof for this? Jacob said to Laban: **"If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, you would surely have sent me away empty-handed."** <note>Genesis 31:42</note> Indeed, the **"Fear of Isaac"** was with him and came to support him. Following this path of understanding, realize that the attribute of Fear is the location of the **Great Sanhedrin** <note>the supreme celestial court of justice</note> and its subordinate courts. Within it are all types of intense fire and all types of weapons of war and instruments of destruction used to demolish, kill, destroy, and uproot. All these exist to carry out the judgments decreed by the Great Sanhedrin, which is called *Elohim* <note>a name of God associated with Justice</note>. Regarding this place, King Solomon found it necessary to reveal that even the mighty, the pious, and the righteous are afraid of this place. 

As it says (C): **"Behold the bed of Solomon; sixty heroes surround it, of the heroes of Israel. They all handle the sword and are expert in war... because of fear in the night."** <note>Song of Songs 3:7-8</note> Our Sages of blessed memory explained that this refers to the **fear of Gehenna** <note>Hell or the purgatorial afterlife</note>, which is compared to night. Know that even the highest righteous souls are afraid and terrified of the attribute of Fear. Even King David cried out, saying: **"My flesh trembles from fear of You."** <note>Psalm 119:120</note> What is the reason? **"I am afraid of Your judgments."** This means the place of Judgment is the dwelling place of the attribute of Fear. 

After we have explained this to you, know that in the place called "Fear," there are many levels below it consisting of various pits and very deep trenches. These are called the "dwellings of Gehenna." There, one finds many types of destructive forces and punishments. Because of their great depth, they are entirely dark—always murky and gloomy. For this reason, they are called **"Night,"** because no light ever shines there; it is always entirely night in that place. Therefore, both the heavenly beings and the earthly beings fear it greatly. This is the meaning of "fear in the nights," which the Sages interpreted as the fear of Gehenna, which resembles night. Many righteous people prayed for mercy during their lives so they would not have to see that place. The Holy One, blessed be He, promised to fulfill their request, saying: **"You shall not fear the terror of the night."** <note>Psalm 91:5</note>

Now, consider the power of those who perform **repentance** (*teshuvah*), for they are saved from this harsh place. Woe to the wicked who are judged in this place where light never appears! This is what is meant by: **"A land as dark as gloom, as the shadow of death, without any order"** <margin>if so</margin> **"and where the light is as darkness."** <note>Job 10:22</note> Know that any person who does not say the **Order of Sanctity** <note>original: *Seder Kedushah*; specifically the *Uva LeTzion* prayer</note every single day—which includes the "Holy, Holy, Holy" declaration and its proper sequence—is destined to taste the flavor of this place of Fear, which is entirely dark, unless they repair what they have damaged before leaving this world. Thus it says: "A land as dark as gloom... without any order." Why is this associated with the word *Alemit* <note>possibly a scribal shorthand or reference to "silence"</note>? Because the person did not say the "Order of Sanctity," and therefore they find themselves where there is "shadow of death and no order." 

Know that this attribute, called "Fear" and "Consuming Fire," was given by the Holy One to Israel to stand before them to conquer the Land and fight their battles, as it says: **"No man shall be able to stand against you; the LORD your God will lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land."** <note>Deuteronomy 11:25</note> Why does the scripture mention "your fear" as a praise for Israel? It is a wonder! God says that even though the attribute of Fear is Mine, Israel has taken it as an inheritance, for Isaac inherited the attribute of Fear, and thus it became his.

# Gate 6

From the north side (A), the sacrifices that used to be slaughtered in the north will be abolished, because the **attribute of retribution** <note>original: *middat ha-puranut*</note>—the accuser that stood in the north—will have already been nullified. There will be no need to slaughter a sacrifice in the north for sin, as they will no longer (B) sin; understand this well. Know that this attribute called *Elohim* <note>the Divine Name associated with strict justice</note>, which stands to the Left, is sometimes called the **weak hand** <note>original: *yad kehah*</note>. The reason it is called a "weak hand" is that it is the Left, and it restrains (C) and prevents the Right from flowing into the world, except for what is issued by strict Law. This is because it receives all the wealth from the hand of the Right and hides it in its treasuries, as we have said. This is the secret of the verse: **"He has rays flashing from His hand, and there is the hiding-place of His power"** <note>Habakkuk 3:4; the Hebrew *karnayim* can mean "rays" or "horns."</note>; understand this very well.

Now that we have informed you of this, we must inform you that this attribute of **Might** <note>original: *Gevurah*</note> is called **Fear** <note>original: *Pachad*</note>. The reason is that this attribute of Might and Dominion is the place of the **Great Sanhedrin** <note>the supreme celestial court</note>. There, many houses of judgment exist, many chambers of flaming fire, and many <term>gardinim<gloss>celestial bailiffs or officers of the court</gloss></term> who are appointed to strike, punish, and discipline with every type of blow, wound, and illness. All of them are a flaming fire. In this place, there are many types of fire that consume every other type of fire in the world, destroying them just as fire consumes straw. Therefore, it is called the **Great Fire**, because all other types of fire in the world are small compared to this fire. Because this fire burns all other types of fire, those above and those below (E) fear it. Even the high angels are startled, terrified, and "burned" by this fire; they cannot approach it. Rather, "fear and dread" exist there because of its great strength and the power of its dominion. In this way, this attribute is called **Fear**, which the multitudes above and below dread. This is the meaning of the verse: **"Before the terror of the Lord and the glory of His majesty"** <note>Isaiah 2:10</note>. From this fire, which burns and consumes everything, and which is the place of Fear and the **refiner's furnace** for the wicked and the willful sinners—and by the power of whose flame many celestial hosts are burned—the scripture says: **"Sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling grips the godless: 'Who of us can dwell with the consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting burning?'"** <note>Isaiah 33:14</note>.

Know that it is called **consuming fire** <note>original: *esh okhlah*</note> because it "eats" all other types of fire in the world. In this way, the Blessed Lord is called—from the perspective of this attribute—a "consuming fire," as it says: **"For the Lord your God is a consuming fire... He will consume them"** <note>Deuteronomy 4:24 and 9:3</note>. Because He, may He be blessed, is a consuming fire, He can humble, lower, and destroy, for through this attribute, the Blessed Lord wages war. Therefore, this attribute is called **Fear**. Our father Isaac, peace be upon him, held fast to this attribute; it belongs to the Left side and to the side of Great Judgment, and it is called the **Fear of Isaac** <note>original: *Pachad Yitzchak*</note>. Thus it says: **"And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac"** <note>Genesis 31:53</note>.

Know that when Laban the Aramean pursued Jacob and sought to uproot everything, this attribute came to uproot Laban and to fight with him. For Laban the Aramean (F) came with a great and supernal power. Do not let it be a light thing in your eyes that the Torah said—

# Gate 7

## The Attribute Called "El"

Now, know and understand: in times of trouble, the holy and pious ones would hasten to pray and focus their intentions toward the attribute called **"El."** This is why we say in our prayers, <term>God (El), the King who sits on a throne of mercy</term> <note>original: "El Melech yoshev al kisse rachamim"</note>. He is also called **"God (El) Most High."** 

Our father **Abraham** (may he rest in peace) devoted all his days to pursuing this specific attribute, which is entirely comprised of kindness, mercy, and grace. He accepted upon himself various types of suffering and pain in order to merit this attribute. Through his great effort and his love for God, he merited an eternal inheritance. This is the secret behind the verse: **"Blessed be Abram to God (El) Most High"** <note>Genesis 14:19</note>. It is also said: **"And he planted an *eshel* tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God (El)"** <note>Genesis 21:33</note>.

Behold, Abraham inherited this attribute, and therefore he was blessed in everything. He had no <term>accuser</term> <note>a spiritual prosecuting force</note> or challenger from above; rather, all things were ready to fulfill his will because the attribute of **"El"** was constantly revealed upon him. When this happened, all the "Lords of Judgment" <note>the harsh spiritual forces</note> would flee from before him. This is the secret of the phrase **"Kindness to Abraham"** <note>Micah 7:20</note>. Because the attribute of **"El"** is the one prepared for great mercies, our Sages established the prayer: "God (El), the King who sits on a throne of mercy."

Now, we must awaken you to a great principle regarding the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy**. The verse states: **"The Lord, the Lord, God (El), merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth"** <note>Exodus 34:6</note>. Even though this verse was explained to you in the previous Gate, we must still explain it based on the foundation of the attribute **"El."** Indeed, King David (may he rest in peace) took these attributes and included them all within the name **"El,"** saying: **"But you, O Lord, are a God (El) full of compassion, and gracious, long-suffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth"** <note>Psalm 86:15</note>. Now, pay attention and hear the explanation of this verse:

**"El"** is the secret of a supreme attribute that is entirely pure mercy. Before it, all the "camps of Judgment" are humbled, and not one of them can stand in its presence. Because Abraham inherited the attribute of **"El"** and loved it, he merited to possess all the inheritances of the 310 heavenly camps called <term>Yesh</term> <note>In Hebrew, the word for "substance" or "there is" (Yesh) has a numerical value of 310, representing the rewards for the righteous</note>. This is the secret of the verse: **"To cause those who love me to inherit substance (*Yesh*)"** <note>Proverbs 8:21</note>, and it says of him: **"the seed of Abraham my friend"** <note>Isaiah 41:8</note>. Understand this well.

Following this, the verse says **"Merciful"** (*Rachum*). The secret of **"Merciful"** is the function of the attribute **"El"** when it sees that a decree has been issued by the "Great Sanhedrin" <note>the Heavenly Court</note> to destroy or banish a person, a place, or something similar. If such destruction would bring a great loss to the world, the attribute called **"El"** emerges to show mercy to the creatures so that the world is not destroyed. It shows mercy to that specific creature that was sentenced to be annihilated. When the attribute of **"El"** emerges, all the "camps of Judgment" flee and hide, and then that creature is saved from judgment and punishment. This is the secret of the "Mercy" found within the attribute of **"El."**

Following this, it says **"Gracious"** (*Chanun*). The secret of **"Gracious"** is that many times, when the "camps of the Destroyer" go out to destroy the inhabitants of the world according to the law, the attribute of **"El"** emerges and revolves to save them. Even though they are not worthy or deserving, it gives a **"free gift"** <note>a grace that is unearned</note> to save the creatures from great punishment.

Following this, it says **"Long-suffering"** (*Erech Apayim*). Know that among the creatures, there are those who deserve neither mercy nor grace, but rather deserve to be punished according to the judgment <margin>God (El), merciful and gracious, long-suffering</margin> decreed upon them from above. Nevertheless, the attribute of **"El"**—which is entirely mercy—emerges and says: "Wait for this person; do not punish him immediately." Even though he deserves neither mercy nor grace, they wait for him, perhaps he will repent. This is the secret of **"Long-suffering"**—meaning they extend the time for him, perhaps [he will return], and even though the **"Anger"** <note>The Hebrew word for "Nose" (*Af*) also means "Anger"</note> is hanging over him, they lengthen the anger for him.

I must enlighten your eyes in this great secret: what is the secret of **"Long-suffering"**? Know that when the Heavenly Court passes a sentence, they do not wait for a person, except during the hours when the messengers are dispatched from the "Anger." As soon as they leave the "Anger," they strike those deserving of punishment. But this attribute called **"El,"** when it wishes to have mercy on creatures who deserve neither mercy nor grace—what does it do? It "lengthens" the time for the sinners.

<meta>This page continues the exposition of the divine Name **El**, specifically focusing on its role within the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy revealed to Moses.
