# Gate 7

It is deep, and with God’s help, you will yet grasp the matter further. Now that we have informed you of these great principles regarding the **Attribute of El**, we must return and complete the explanation of this verse <note>Exodus 34:6: "The Lord, the Lord, El, compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in kindness and truth."</note>. We have already explained to you the secret of this verse: the Name **El**, "Compassionate," "Gracious," and "Slow to Anger." It remains for us to explain to you what **"Abundant in Kindness"** means in this context.

Know that among created beings, there are those who are worthy of neither compassion, nor grace, nor "slowness of anger," but are instead deserving of immediate punishment. What does the **Attribute of El**—which is the Attribute of Mercy—do? When the iniquities of that creature are weighed during judgment in the **Heavenly Court**, this attribute removes the first and second sins so they do not enter into the count (a), even though they are not erased. The counting begins only from the third sin, as it is said: **"Behold, all these things God (El) works, twice, three times, with a man"** <note>Job 33:29. The author interprets this to mean God overlooks the first two instances of a sin to give the person a chance to tip the scales.</note>. 

And after the iniquities and merits of that creature have been weighed, if the scales stand in perfect balance, the **Attribute of El** tips the scale toward the side of merit, as it is said: **"Abundant in Kindness"**—meaning, He leans toward kindness. Thus, the **Attribute of El** is found performing an act of kindness and mercy for that creature standing in judgment. Even if the person was not inherently worthy of compassion, grace, or patience, God still performs kindness with them during the weighing of sins and merits.

Once you know this, know that the **Attribute of El** continues to perform even more kindness and mercy with creatures through the secret of how this verse concludes: **"and Truth."** What is the meaning of **"and Truth"**? 

Consider a case where a person’s sins and merits were weighed, and it was clear from the <term>abundance of his sins</term><note>The OCR reads "גרוחטאיו," likely a corruption of "רוב חטאיו" (abundance of his sins).</note> that the Attribute of Kindness could not help, because his sins tipped the scales toward the side of liability. Even then, the **Attribute of El**—which is the Attribute of Kindness—performs kindness and mercy with that punished creature in two ways:

The first way: If that creature is sentenced to be <term>excised</term><note>Hebrew: *Karet*; spiritual "cutting off" or total loss of the soul's portion.</note> and perish according to the law, the Attribute of Kindness counts every merit and every good thing that creature ever did—even a <term>pleasant conversation</term>—and lightens the creature's punishment so they do not suffer excessively. 

The second way: If the punished creature is not liable for excision and total loss, then at the end of the punishment, the Attribute of Mercy scrutinizes even a tiny conversation to give them a good reward for what they did after the days of punishment have passed. 

Even though the <term>Attribute of Justice</term><note>Hebrew: *Middat Ha-Din*.</note> also performs this function—scrutinizing to do good just as it scrutinized to punish—it is for this reason that the Attribute of Justice is also called **"Truth."** 

Now that we have informed you of these great principles in this verse regarding the **Attribute of El**, we must return and inform you of a great general rule: Wherever you find the name **El** written in the Torah, you must include within it (b) all those attributes of kindness and mercy contained therein. Furthermore, you must know and contemplate that in every place (c) these two attributes—the Attribute of Kindness and the Attribute of Mercy—are intermingled as one. Likewise, the titles of both are intermingled with one another. Guard this principle <note>original: "עקב זה", literally "this heel," a metaphor for a fundamental point to follow.</note> for every place, and do not forget it.

# Gate 7
->7<-

This is a deep matter, and with God’s help, you will yet grasp it further. After we have informed you of these great principles regarding the attribute of **El** <note>The Hebrew name for God associated with the attribute of Kindness/Chesed</note> in this context, we must return and complete the explanation of this verse. We have already explained the secret of this verse: **"God (El), Merciful and Gracious, Long-suffering..."** <note>Exodus 34:6</note>. It remains for us to explain to you what is meant by **"Abundant in Kindness"** in this context.

Know that among the creatures, there are those who are worthy of neither mercy, nor grace, nor long-suffering, but instead deserve to be punished immediately. What does the attribute of **El**—which is the attribute of Mercy—do? When the iniquities of that creature are weighed during judgment in the Heavenly Court, this attribute removes the first and second iniquity, and they are not included in the count <note>original: (א)</note>, even though they are not erased. The court does not begin its scrutiny until the third iniquity, as it is said: **"Lo, all these things does God work, twice, thrice, with a man"** <note>Job 33:29</note>. 

After they have weighed the iniquities and merits of that creature, if the scales stand in balance, the attribute of **El** tips the scale toward the side of merit, as it is said: **"and Abundant in Kindness"**—meaning, He tilts toward kindness. If so, we find that the attribute of **El** grants kindness and mercy to that creature standing in judgment, even though they were worthy of neither mercy, nor grace, nor long-suffering. Nevertheless, He performs kindness with them when weighing their iniquities and merits. 

Once you know this, know that the attribute of **El** goes even further to perform many more acts of kindness and mercy with creatures, based on the secret of how the verse concludes: **"and Truth"** (*Emet*). And what is the meaning of **"and Truth"**? Consider a case where a person’s iniquities and merits were weighed, and their sins were so overwhelming that the attribute of Kindness could not prevail, and their iniquities tipped the scale toward the side of guilt. Even then, the attribute of **El**—which is the attribute of Kindness—grants kindness and mercy to that creature who is being punished in two ways. 

The first way: if that creature is liable to be "cut off" <term>Karet; a spiritual punishment of being severed from the divine source</term> and destroyed according to the letter of the law, the attribute of Kindness preserves all the merits and all the good things that creature did—even a single good conversation they held—and they lighten that creature's punishment so they do not suffer excessively. 

The second way: if the creature being punished is not liable for destruction or being cut off, at the end of the punishment, the attribute of Mercy scrutinizes even a small conversation to give them a good reward for what they did after the days of punishment have passed. Even though the attribute of Justice also does this—scrutinizing to do good just as it scrutinized to punish—for this reason, the attribute of Justice is also called **"Truth."** 

After we have informed you of these great principles regarding the attribute of **El** in this verse, we must return and inform you of a great general rule: wherever you find the name **El** written in the Torah, you must include within it <note>original: (ב)</note> all those attributes of kindness and mercy contained within it. Furthermore, you must know and contemplate that in every place <note>original: (ג)</note> these two attributes—the attribute of Kindness and the attribute of Mercy—intermingle as one. Similarly, the titles of both intermingle with one another. Guard this principle for every instance and do not forget it.

***

<margin>Between good and evil, and including it within the foundation of the intention to receive merit. So, too, sometimes the righteous are seized by the iniquity of their generation to serve as an atonement for them, so that they are not all destroyed. I have written on this regarding the matter of Peor and the "Broken-Necked Heifer." Or sometimes, the judgment is literally according to its name regarding "The righteous man who suffers," through the secret of reincarnation (Gilgul), as I also wrote in the section on Vayishev. It is all a judgment of Truth, a righteous and upright decree without injustice. It only remembers the law of Judgment... and regarding this, it says "The Holy Sword and God" to do good to those... for it is deep.</margin>

# Gate 7

That is to say, the seal of **Kindness** <note>original: *Chesed*</note> and **Fear** <note>original: *Pachad*, a name for the attribute of Severity or Justice</note> as one. What is the proof for this? As it is said: **"But the Lord God is Truth"** <note>Jeremiah 10:10</note>. Behold, it mentions the attribute of Abraham, which is **The Lord** <note>original: *YHWH*, representing Mercy/Kindness</note>, the attribute of Isaac, which is **God** <note>original: *Elohim*, representing Judgment/Fear</note>, and the attribute of Jacob, which is **Truth** <note>original: *Emet*</note>. Therefore, the verse says: **"The Lord God is Truth."** Indeed, we find that our father Jacob inherited the seal of **The Lord God**, through which the world was created, through which all creatures are sustained, and through which all people of the world are judged in a **judgment of truth**. Thus, we find our father Jacob held two attributes in his hand, called "Right" and "Left"—he held the attribute of **Kindness** and the attribute of **Punishment**; he held the **positive commandments** and the **prohibitive commandments**.

You find yourself learning that he held the attribute of the Lord, which is **Truth**, in the secret of **"But the Lord God is Truth"**—the seal of judgment, as it is written: **"The judgments of the Lord are truth"** <note>Psalm 19:10</note>, and the **Torah** <note>The Five Books of Moses/Divine Law</note> which is truth, as it is written: **"The Torah of truth was in his mouth"** <note>Malachi 2:6</note>. For Jacob stands in the place of all the Forefathers and held fast to the attributes of all three. And even though he who first brought forth and birthed an attribute is not the same as he who held it last, nevertheless, Jacob is found to be the one who binds all the attributes together. He is the **Middle Line** <note>original: *Kav Ha-Emtza’i*; in Kabbalah, the central pillar of the Sefirotic tree that balances Mercy and Judgment</note>. Just as the Name **The Lord** (blessed be He) stands in the middle, so our father Jacob stands in the middle. Because Jacob merited the Name **The Lord**, he was called by it. 

He merited that twelve righteous tribes should come from him (f) corresponding to the twelve **permutations** <note>original: *Tzirufim*; the different ways the four letters of the Name YHWH can be rearranged</note> of the Name **The Lord** (blessed be He). And just as the Name of **The Lord** is called **Truth**, so Jacob’s children were called a **"seed of truth"**—meaning, a seed that emerged from the Name of Truth, from him through whom they were carved, who is our father Jacob (peace be upon him). Regarding this, it is said: **"Yet I had planted you a choice vine, entirely a seed of truth"** <note>Jeremiah 2:21</note>. If so, contemplate this great principle and you will find that the three Forefathers (g) came into the world with full intention, and each one held fast to his attribute: Abraham to the attribute of **Kindness**, Isaac to the attribute of **Fear**, and Jacob to the attribute of **Truth** (h). Our sages interpreted one verse as: **"The Lord our God, the Lord is One"** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>—this one held his own, and that one held his own. 

Now that we have informed you of these great principles included within the three Forefathers, we must return and inform you of the secret of **Abraham’s Kindness** and the secret of **Jacob’s Truth**, as written in the verse: **"You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham"** <note>Micah 7:20</note>. This describes how the Lord (blessed be He) conducts Himself with Israel through these two attributes. Sometimes He conducts Himself with Israel through the **Kindness of Abraham**, and sometimes He conducts Himself through the **Truth of Jacob**. 

You must know how this works: know that sometimes Israel is found lacking and they are worthy of neither goodness nor mercy, because they are not occupying themselves with Torah or commandments. When they are judged in the **Heavenly Court**, the judgment dictates that they should be punished with every kind of blow. In that hour, the attribute of Abraham, which is the attribute of **Kindness**, hurries and stands in the Court and says: "What is the judgment of my children?" They say to it: "By law, it is determined they must be punished with every kind of blow." In that hour, the attribute of Kindness says: "If they can find no merit for my children, then I am their inheritance, for I am their father and they inherit me. Even if they are not worthy of receiving good according to the Law, do good for them from the side of **Kindness**." For the nature of Kindness is to do good even for those who are not worthy. Just as Abraham served the Lord (blessed be He) from the side of Kindness, so is the Lord worthy to reward his children from the side of their father’s Kindness. In this way, Israel is saved from many punishments. 

But if Israel is occupying themselves with Torah and commandments, the attribute of **Judgment of Jacob** <note>Here referring to the balanced "Truth" that rewards the deserving</note> hurries and says to the Court: "Give to my children according to the Law, which is **Truth**, all that they need, for they are righteous and worthy of having good done for them." This is the secret of **"You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham."**

# Gate 6

Unique in the world—and behold, Abraham was unique in the world, and God preceded him with the attribute of His **Kindness** <note>original: *Chesed*</note>, and it was fitting for Abraham to take hold of it, and I [God] in him. Then Abraham returned to the attribute of **Kindness** as an inheritance and benefited from his merit, as the scripture says: **"You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham"** <note>Micah 7:20</note>. The explanation of the verse is as follows: Know that our father Abraham, peace be upon him, performed the service of the Blessed Lord from the side of **Kindness** without a teacher or father teaching him, and without a prophetic mission coming to him from the Creator to rebuke or warn him. Rather, he observed, looked, searched, and understood on his own until he arrived at the knowledge of the kingdom of the Blessed Lord. Just as the Name [God] created the world from the side of **Kindness**, so did Abraham recognize his Creator from the side of **Kindness**. 

But our father Jacob, peace be upon him, did not recognize the Creator from the side of **Kindness** alone; rather, he recognized Him from the side of **Truth** <note>original: *Emet*</note>. Abraham made known the attribute of **Kindness**: how? Abraham came first and informed the creatures of the abundance of God’s kindness and His mercy over all His works—that He is the one who created them and sustains them, all from the side of His kindness. From this perspective, it is fitting for all human beings to serve Him, to plead before Him, and to accept the yoke of His kingdom, and all this is our duty to do. 

Afterward came Isaac and added to the knowledge the attribute of **Fear** <note>original: *Pachad*, representing Divine Justice or Severity</note>—warning that if they do not serve Him, He will punish them like a servant who rebels against his master (7). He cast awe and fear upon the creatures to bring them "under the wings of the Divine Presence" <note>term: *Shekhinah* — the indwelling presence of God in the physical world</note> by informing them of the fear of punishment for those who rebel against the Blessed Creator. This is the secret of the **"Fear of Isaac"** <note>Genesis 31:42</note>, for Isaac inherited the attribute of **Fear**. Therefore, he warned human beings and rebuked them so they would guard themselves from the Great Court that judges the wicked with the attribute of **Fear**, which is called the "punishments of Hell" <note>original: *Gehenna*</note>. And it says: **"Sinners in Zion are afraid"** <note>Isaiah 33:14</note> and so on. 

If so, we find Abraham rebuking the creatures from the side of **Kindness** and with the attribute of **Kindness**, while Isaac is found rebuking the creatures from the side of **Fear**. Each one rebuked according to his attribute: this one with the attribute of **Kindness** and reward, and that one with the attribute of **Fear** and punishment; this one with the **positive commandments** <note>248 [commandments], to bless them</note> and that one with the **prohibitive commandments**. 

And when our father Jacob, peace be upon him, came, he did not have a third attribute to take hold of. Instead, he took hold of both attributes—that of Abraham and that of Isaac: the attribute of **Kindness** and the attribute of **Fear** (30). He informed all who enter the world of the greatness of their truth. He held onto both of them in truth and with a whole heart, deviating neither to the right nor to the left. Therefore, Abraham is called **Kindness** according to his attribute, Isaac is called **Fear** according to his attribute, and Jacob is called **Truth** according to his attribute.

And behold, I am illuminating your eyes with a sealed and hidden secret: Jacob was the **Middle Line** <note>original: *Kav Ha-Emtzai* — the kabbalistic path that balances the extremes of Mercy and Judgment</note>. He is the secret (4) of the **Seal** <note>original: *Chotam*</note>. He took hold between two partitions as one who enters the middle: he took the attribute of Abraham, which is the **positive commandments** and is **Kindness**, and he took the attribute of Isaac, which is the **prohibitive commandments** and is the **Fear of Isaac**. He held both attributes equally, deviating neither to the right nor to the left. Because of this, he is called a **"Man of Truth"** because he conducted himself with the two attributes of his fathers in truth. 

The secret is: **"And Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents"** <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. It does not say "dwelling in a tent," but **"tents"** [plural]. "Tents" is the secret of the tent of Abraham, which is **Kindness**, and the tent of Isaac, which is **Fear**. This is what he meant when he said: **"Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had been with me"** <note>Genesis 31:42</note>. Because he held both attributes equally and turned neither right nor left, the attribute of **Truth** was given to him. This is like the "tongue of the balance" <note>the needle of a scale</note> when it stands equally between the two scales and does not lean right or left. Thus Jacob stood, and in his hand were the attribute of **Fear** and the attribute of **Kindness** equally, and he conducted himself with both in truth. When the Blessed Lord saw this, He gave Jacob His seal, which is **Truth**, like a king who finds a faithful servant and says to him, "Behold, my seal is handed over to you." Thus the Lord handed over to Jacob His seal, which is **Truth**, that is to say:

For without these portions, the world cannot exist—neither by **Kindness** alone according to its full power, nor by **Judgment** <note>original: *Din*</note> alone according to its full power. For without a foundation of grace [tempering] the judgment, he held everything together. For the entire world is for **Kindness**, yet they earned it all [through judgment]. Therefore, he was led by a balanced nature, and his "deciding factor" <note>original: *machria* — the element that tips or balances a scale</note> supported these attributes and their recognition. Therefore, he was chosen to take hold of both of them as one, and he appeared and led the world with this, through the **median** on the straight line. And by entering the middle, he explained these (3) attributes—that he was the intermediary between the Right and the Left. For this reason, Jacob is called a **"plain man"** <note>original: *ish tam*, also meaning "complete" or "perfect"</note>. (4) And he recognized the attribute of Abraham, which was **The Lord** <note>original: *YHWH*</note>, for wherever it says "The Lord God," it is a full Name, hinting that the attribute of **Judgment**...

# Gate 8

# Gate 7

Understand this very well. Now that we have informed you of this, we must explain the reason why the verse mentions the **attribute** <note>original: *middah*</note> of Jacob first. Know that the way of the world is reflected in this verse: if Israel are righteous and possess Torah and commandments, they are worthy of receiving good through the side of **Justice** <note>original: *Din*</note>, which is the **Truth** <note>original: *Emet*</note> of Jacob. If they are not, they receive through the side of the **Kindness** <note>original: *Chesed*</note> of Abraham, even if they are not worthy. This is the secret of the verse, "You will give truth to Jacob," and afterwards, "kindness to Abraham" <note>Micah 7:20</note>. Guard these great principles that we have explained to you in this gate. 

It remains for us to inform you why the verse mentions the attribute of Jacob, which is Truth, and the attribute of Abraham, which is Kindness, but does not mention the attribute of Isaac, which is **Fear** <note>original: *Pachad*</note>. Know that the attribute of Abraham is Kindness, and the attribute of Jacob is the secret of **Compassion** <note>original: *Rachamim*</note>, which is the secret of Truth; these needed to be mentioned in this verse. However, the attribute of Isaac, which is the attribute of Fear, did not need to be mentioned for the reason we stated above. 

And if you should challenge this, saying: "Is it not written: 'Then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham' <note>Leviticus 26:42</note>? Behold, all three are mentioned in this verse!" Know that in this verse, He does not mention their attributes, but rather the **Covenant** <note>original: *Berit*</note> He struck with them to do good for their children. The proof of this is also: "Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants, to whom You swore..." <note>Exodus 32:13</note>. Do you not see that the oath in this verse did not come because of the three Patriarchs themselves, but to do good for Israel? As it says, "And You spoke to them: 'I will multiply your seed.'" 

The matter is the same in the verse, "Then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, etc.," for the Covenant and the Oath are one and the same. But when He mentions the covenant of Jacob, the covenant of Isaac, and the covenant of Abraham, it means it is proper to do good for Israel because of the Covenant and the Oath from the side of Justice—like one who holds a deposit for his fellow and demands it back by law. Thus, we seek the Covenant of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob from before the Blessed Lord from the side of Justice. This is the secret of these two matters hinted at in one verse <note>Micah 7:20</note>: if Israel is not worthy to be given to from the side of Justice, give to them from the side of Kindness; this is "You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham." And if they are not worthy even from the side of Kindness, give to them from the side of Justice and from the side of the **Oath** <note>original: *Shevuah*</note> that You swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Therefore, at the end of this verse, it says: "Which You swore to our ancestors from days of old." But when He mentions the attribute of Abraham and the attribute of Jacob in one verse, the reason is as explained above. May the Lord teach us His correct path, Amen.

# Gate 8

...in the creation of the world, and upon it all the "sevens" <note>Groups of seven things in the physical and spiritual worlds, such as the seven days of the week or seven heavens.</note> were unified; from it and upon it is the drawing forth of their emanation and toward it is their longing. From it <note>Binah (Understanding)</note> until the attribute of **Foundation** <note>original: *Yesod*</note> there is a count of seven **Sefirot** <note>The ten creative forces or attributes of God in Kabbalah.</note>, because it is the link between the five upper ones and the seven lower ones. This is the secret of the "Third" relative to the upper ones, and the first or the seventh whether counting from top to bottom or bottom to top. These are the lower ones until the attribute of **Foundation** <note>original: *Yesod*</note>, excluding the attribute of **Kingship** <note>original: *Malchut*</note> which is the last. 

Behold, the secret of the connection of the eight upper Sefirot is found when we begin to count from the Sefirah of **Understanding** <note>original: *Binah*</note> in this manner: Understanding, Greatness, Power, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, and Foundation <note>original: *Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod*</note>. Whenever you find the Sefirah of Foundation mentioned in the Torah as being the "seventh," it is according to this path. Foundation is the seventh from below, and Understanding is the seventh from above. Understanding binds the six Sefirot into three, while Foundation binds the tenth Sefirah <note>Malchut</note> to the upper nine. 

Understand this very well, for these are the two joints of the **Chariot** <note>original: *Merkavah*; refers to the mystical structure of the divine realm</note>, the connection and the **Unity** <note>original: *Yichud*</note>. Regarding this, it is said: "On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. As mentioned here, the word "One" appears twice: once for the secret of the two joints of connection and unity for the ten Sefirot (a) in the secret of "One in three" and "One in seven." 

After you know this, know that wherever you find a "seventh" in the Torah, such as "seven years" or "seven times," it is the secret of the Sefirah from the Foundation up to Understanding, and in some places from Understanding down to Foundation. As it is said: (b) "For **six days** the Lord made the heavens and the earth" <note>Exodus 31:17</note>. It says "six days" and not "*in* six days" <note>The author notes that the Sefirot *are* the days, not just the time period in which creation happened.</note>. (c) Aside from these six, there are the **six profane days** <note>original: *yimei chol*</note> that surround the attribute of Foundation like a circle; they are on the outside like the image of **husks** <note>original: *Kelipot*; the outer shells of impurity that conceal divine light</note>, and therefore they are called "six profane days." 

However, the six Sefirot that begin from the Sefirah of Understanding and extend until the seventh, which is Foundation—all of them are **Holy** <note>original: *Kodesh*</note> and are not included in the "profane." This matter is also very, very deep and requires oral reception from mouth to ear. I am hereby hinting: from top to bottom and bottom to top, all the Sefirot are holy. Everything within the circle is holy, and everything outside the circle is profane. The Sages hinted at this secret in the order of the **Havdalah** <note>The "Separation" ceremony performed at the end of the Sabbath to distinguish the holy day from the coming work week.</note> when they said: "Between the seventh day and the six days of labor" (d), "Blessed is He who separates between holy and profane, between light and darkness, and between Israel and the nations." He who understands this will understand the secret of the circle.

# Gate 5

<margin>(8)</margin> Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world. <margin>(100)</margin> With thirty-two paths, Y-H-W-H <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God, often translated as 'The Lord.'</note> engraved—and one who knows how to direct their heart toward these verses and these signs will be able to understand the core principle. However, <margin>(9)</margin> this is not handed over to be understood except through oral tradition, from mouth to mouth.

<margin>(10)</margin> The secret of this core principle includes the order of all the hidden levels. Within it are included the secrets of the verse: **“In the beginning God created”** <note>original: *Bereshit Bara Elohim*</note>, representing the attribute of **Power** <note>original: *Gevurah*—the divine force of restriction and judgment.</note>; and **“In the beginning God created”** representing the attribute of **Kingship** <note>original: *Malchut*—the final Sefirah that manifests divine will in the physical world.</note>. For each one of these Sefirot birthed the orders of the world. In each and every one of them is included the secret of the verse **“In the beginning God created,”** and these matters are deep; not everyone is able to enter their depths.

<margin>(30)</margin> One who understands these principles will be able to understand the secret of the sages’ saying: **“The Torah has seventy faces”** <note>A famous rabbinic teaching that the scripture can be interpreted in seventy different ways, all of them true.</note>. If so, open your eyes to perceive, for in some places you will find written **“God”** <note>original: *Elohim*</note> and it hints at the Sefirah of **Understanding** <note>original: *Binah*</note> according to the hints we have written here. At other times, it hints at the attribute of **Power** <note>original: *Gevurah*</note>, which is appropriate for it; and at times <margin>(20)</margin> it hints at the attribute of **Kingship** <note>original: *Malchut*</note> when it is clothed in the garment of Power. 

All this applies when you find the name **God** (*Elohim*) on its own. However, when you find **God** adjacent to the word **Hosts** <note>original: *Tzabaot*</note>—such as in the phrase **“God of Hosts, restore us”** <note>Psalm 80:8</note>—it refers to when the "left crown" <note>An aspect of the Sefirah *Hod* (Splendor), which sits on the left side of the divine tree.</note> attaches itself to the attribute of Power, taking up weapons of war and donning garments of zeal, as it is said: **“The zeal of the Lord of Hosts will perform this”** <note>Isaiah 9:6</note>.

<margin>(50)</margin> We have already hinted at this in what preceded. In every place where you find the term **“Living God”** <note>original: *Elohim Hayyim*</note>, it is the secret of the attribute of **Foundation** <note>original: *Yesod*</note>, which draws life from the Sefirah of **Understanding** (*Binah*), because the Sefirah of Understanding is called **“Life of the Worlds,”** as we are destined to explain. Therefore, the attribute of Foundation is called by its name—**Living God**—when it draws life from the Sefirah of Understanding. Furthermore, the attribute of **Kingship** (*Malchut*), when it receives the flow of blessing and life from the attribute of Foundation <margin>(4)</margin>, is also called **Living God** in our tongue, for **“My name is within him.”** 

However, in every place where you find it written **“Other Gods”** <note>original: *Elohim Aherim*—referring to idols or external forces.</note>, its meaning is explained as "scattered forces," and there is no need to repeat these matters. Know that this Sefirah, which is written as *Y-H-W-H* but read as *Elohim* <note>In certain Kabbalistic contexts, the Tetragrammaton is vocalized with the vowels of the name Elohim to signify the union of mercy and judgment.</note>, counts and binds the nine upper Sefirot into one knot. It is also the cause for the unification of the tenth Sefirah with the ninth, and from it comes the flow and the blessing to the ninth. Behold, this Sefirah called **Understanding** <margin>(60)</margin> is the secret of the revelation of the Hidden Name within Creation.

Regarding the matter of the "End in its Beginning," at the time of the "Waters in Understanding," there is the cessation of the beginning of the drawing forth of Judgment (*Din*) in "Fear" <note>Another name for *Gevurah*.</note> which is called "Heavens." The general sign is that Understanding and Wisdom are the unification of all. It is that which <margin>(7)</margin> the "Gates of Understanding" were included in the world as explained in Gate 2.

# Gate 8

Observe the order of the separations <note>original: *Havdalah*—the ceremony marking the end of the Sabbath and the start of the new week</note> that the Sages alluded to at the conclusion of the Sabbath, and you will find that the six days of the week are outside the circle.
And so it is with the nations. And so it is with the darkness that separates between the holy and the mundane—both external and internal; and between Israel and the nations—both external and internal;
and between light and darkness—both external and internal; and between the seventh day and the six days of labor—both external and internal, in private. (A) The Sabbath was given <note>to Israel</note>, and the nations have no portion in it. **"It is a sign between Me and the children of Israel forever,"** and the nations have no portion in it. This is
what we established in the Sabbath prayer: (B) "And You, O Lord our God, did not give it to the nations of the lands, nor did You, our King, make it the inheritance of the worshippers of idols, and in its rest the uncircumcised shall not dwell, for You gave it to Your people Israel." (C) **"Lest you lift up your eyes to the heavens and see the sun..."** <note>Deuteronomy 4:19</note> which the Lord your God has allotted <note>to the nations</note>, but the Lord has taken you. This explains the "Generation of the Division" <note>The Tower of Babel</note>—**"When the Most High gave nations their inheritance..."** <note>Deuteronomy 32:8</note> **"For the Lord's portion is His people."** After we have alluded to these deep secrets for you, we shall return to the intent of this Gate. Know that
wherever you find in the Torah a counting of sevens, such as **"Seven complete Sabbaths shall they be, until the morrow of the seventh Sabbath you shall count fifty days,"**
and **"You shall count for yourself seven Sabbaths of years,"** it all refers to the seven Sefirot <note>Divine emanations</note> that span from the Sefirah of Understanding (*Binah*) until the Sefirah of Foundation (*Yesod*).
We begin from the Sefirah of Foundation and ascend until we reach the Sefirah of Understanding. Therefore, there are fifty days from the counting of the Omer until the Giving of the Torah, which correspond to the fifty years of the Jubilee year. (D) Fifty gates of Understanding (*Binah*) were created in the world.
And regarding that which was placed upon the children of Israel: the redemption from Egypt is mentioned fifty times in the Torah. **"So that you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life."** These (E) are the days of our lives. (F) The counting of seven weeks is fifty days.
**"In this Jubilee year, every man shall return to his possession."** "He shall have redemption," and "In the Jubilee he shall go out." And behold, through the attribute of Understanding—which is the secret of the Jubilee—we went out from Egypt, as we are destined to explain with God's help. And in the third month after the children of Israel went out from the land of

->Egypt, the Torah was given.<-

The whole matter is one single allusion to the concept of Sovereignty (*Malchut*): that the nations and the darkness are on the outside, while Israel is the foundation of the heels, etc. And the mundane is for the mundane—the "mundane" of the mundane—applying to both the external and internal;
meaning that there is darkness on the outside and darkness on the inside. (A) "The Sabbath was given in private": this is the secret that is internal and hidden, known from these
powers. This is what was established in the Sabbath prayer: (B) "And You did not give it, O Lord our God, to the nations of the lands," etc., to show that they have no portion in the 
Supernal Sabbath. However, regarding the internal living beings and the ministers <note>Guardian angels of the nations</note>, God allotted them their portion during the time of the Division <note>Babel</note>, but Israel alone He took for His own portion. Our God is above
the powers of the ministers, as explained above in Gate 5 regarding the explanation of the terms and titles. This is the secret of the verse (C) "Lest you lift up your eyes," etc.,
referring to the Generation of the Division that we alluded to. (D) Fifty gates of Understanding in the totality of the world: the matter of the fifty gates of Understanding was explained above in Gate 3.
In clarifying every explanation, the end of Understanding (*Binah*) is the fiftieth gate. And behold, we should also say that we rely on the explanation of its ascents—meaning the matter he mentions—and the substance of them all
was the attachment of Sovereignty (*Malchut*) to Understanding (*Binah*). And therefore, it included the six directions <note>original: *Zappu*—the six emotive Sefirot</note> which are the sixty workings themselves, the 150th gate. Therefore, he mentions all these matters
which are considered a "Treasure" <note>original: *Segulah*</note> alluded to it. "And fifty <note>armed</note> the children of Israel went up" <note>Exodus 13:18</note> is called "to all," and "fifty" is written because the redemption from Egypt was through it.
And regarding his statement, "These (E) are the days of our lives," etc.: this alludes to what the Kabbalists said, that the world will exist and encompass seven cycles, which are the seven Sabbatical cycles (*Shemitot*). For these seven Sefirot will each serve for one Sabbatical cycle. Because of this, it is called one encompassing world. And seven worlds total 
forty-nine [thousand] years until the 5000th year <note>the seventh millennium</note>, which corresponds to the Great Jubilee, which is its Understanding (*Binah*). Then its creative labor shall cease, and they shall return to their first days,
just as they were before the creation. "To his sister and to his place they shall return," and the souls will understand eternal rest, and the earth shall return
to chaos. For a prior Jubilee existed for all. In every seventh millennium of these cycles, it shall be holy with the sanctity of the Sabbatical year of the land's years.
(G) The world shall be (H) the Name. However, in the Crown (*Keter*) of Kindness (*Chesed*) is my people, like the matter of the Sabbath which has "six in it" and so on. We remember the mundane for the one, and therefore
it is said regarding the Sabbatical year: "A Sabbatical year for the Lord," and "A Sabbath for the Lord," just as with the Sabbath of Creation. For in the final millennium, it will conclude its standing in Beauty (*Tiferet*), and the spirits
and holy souls will be gathered. Afterward, He will renew the world with them, and the Crown (*Atarah*) shall return to its head, which is Understanding (*Binah*). And as for whichever of these worlds it may be,
its goodness and vitality will be stronger in its conclusion. The entire world was before Him so that the... [text breaks] would be diminished in it. May He be exalted forever and ever.
Between that of Israel, higher and higher. This is the reason the books of the 150 are gradually diminished, containing waves corresponding to voices. And in the seventh world,
which corresponds to the Great Sabbath, the entire group will be finished, and his portion will be in the highest level.

# Gate 8

The Circle: what is outside and what is inside • (1) He knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with Him <note>Daniel 2:22</note> • (2) Before He had made the earth or the open spaces <note>Proverbs 8:26</note>—the seventy princes <note>The celestial representatives of the seventy archetypal nations</note> are outside, and Israel is inside. (3) He encompassed him, He instructed him... He set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel <note>Deuteronomy 32:8, 10</note> • And no stranger shall eat of the holy thing • For the Lord's portion is His people • And you shall be to Me (4) a kingdom of priests and a holy nation <note>Exodus 19:6</note> • And let the children of Israel keep the Passover in its appointed season (5) • From these (6) the islands of the nations were divided in the earth • And the Lord said to Abraham: Go forth from your land... to the land (7) • And the general principle is the <term>Account of the Chariot</term> <note>original: *Ma'aseh Merkavah*—the mystical study of Ezekiel's vision</note> of Ezekiel: "And I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came from the north, a great cloud, and a fire flashing forth, and a brightness was about it, and out of its midst as it were the color of electrum <note>original: *Chashmal*—a mysterious celestial glow</note> out of the midst of the fire" (8) • He made darkness His hiding-place, His pavilion round about Him; darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies (9) • And His brightness was as the light; He had rays coming out of His hand, and there was the hiding of His power (10) • For there is an advantage to wisdom over folly, as the advantage of light over darkness (11) • The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light • Though I sit in darkness, the Lord is a light (12) to me • For behold, (13) darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but upon thee the Lord shall arise • One who knows how to understand the secret of these verses and their hints can contemplate the depth of these matters we have spoken of • And if you are worthy, you will yet hear their tradition mouth to mouth • (14) He who walked in darkness and had no light, let him trust in the name of the Lord.

->Protected<-

The inner aspect, which is the foundation for navigating the "days of labor" <note>weekdays</note> which are designated by the "Circle," exists within the place that separates the holy from the mundane. Even during the times of the mundane, when the nations are forced to use only the "profane" and "darkness," the "holy" and the "light" belong to Israel. For the source of the light is in the <term>Kingdom</term> <note>The Sefirah of *Malkhut*</note>, which serves as a foundation for Israel. The nations have no portion in it, for the external forces <note>original: *Chitzonim*—the "outer" spiritual shells or husks</note> surround it like a wall. He alluded to this by saying that on the seventh day—which is the secret of separation—these powers were distinguished. Between them, ultimately, on that very day, the Wise One was included. Therefore, it says "to him," meaning "in him," for it was good. 

(1) *He knows what*: This means He knows the essence of the darkness and the external light. From within, He included the internal powers, distinguishing them until (2) *Before He made* the earth and the *open spaces* mentioned before. These are the seventy princes of the nations who are outside in their portions, acting as walls. But Israel is inside, for their portion is from the highest, innermost source. (3) *He encompassed him*: For the walls surround the upper source. He set their boundaries below, around the partition, according to the number of the children of Israel. All of them are from the side of the mundane, and there is a boundary to their influence, just as there is the Sabbath for Israel amidst the six days of holiness. There are boundaries of Judgment according to the number of the children of Israel, but "no stranger shall eat of the holy thing"—they shall not eat or derive nurture from the inner holy place. For the portion of the nations is there—the seventy [princes]. 

(4) *A kingdom of priests and a holy nation*: For they were separated when they performed the Passover in its season (5). "In its season" implies they performed it for seven days corresponding to the seven unique and appointed days. This was the first "Passover" for them, the time they were separated as a holy nation and prepared for the [inner] powers. But (6) *from these* refers to those who separated to the "husk" <note>original: *Kelippah*</note> as explained above regarding the "bent branch." Through the unity of the letter *Gimel*, the islands of the nations were separated. Thus it was said to Abraham, "Go forth from your land"—to the holy land that I will show you. 

(7) *And the general principle*: To say that in their separation, these powers are those mentioned in the <term>Account of the Chariot</term> of Ezekiel. "And behold, a stormy wind came from the north..." mentions four primary levels, as written above regarding the "thick cloud." This explains the four <term>Kelippot</term> <note>Impure "shells" that conceal the divine light</note>. Corresponding to these four levels of holiness (the four Living Creatures), there is "in its midst like the color of electrum" <note>*Chashmal*</note>—meaning the Crown <note>*Keter*</note> that is hidden within these husks. This is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note>, for (8) *He made darkness His hiding-place*—this refers to the fourth husk that covers. Then the "rays" are revealed and received. All these revealed lights belong to the one who has the fear [of God]. On this, it says that these great ones receive light from it. But for now, there is no clear light in exile, and therefore it says of this light (9) *it shall be like light* in the future. "Rays from His hand" belong to the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel who are called to Him. 

(10) *For there is an advantage to wisdom over folly*: Wisdom is light and folly is darkness. (11) *The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light*: This refers to Israel. Even though we are now in the thick of darkness, "the Lord is a light (12) to me," for the day will yet come. (13) *For behold, darkness shall cover the earth... and upon you the Lord shall shine*: His hidden light. (14) *He who walked in darkness*: Those who walk in the darkness of exile will eventually depart from that rule and trust in the Lord, for there will yet be a great light for the Lord, as the verses we mentioned suggest. Or, this refers to the "hidden light" <note>original: *Or HaGanuz*</note>—one who walks in the darkness of these deep matters and his hand cannot reach to grasp their secret should trust in the name of the Lord.

(14) *Observe the order of the separations*: The Sages established the order of *Havdalah* <note>Separation ceremony at the end of Sabbath</note> at the conclusion of the Sabbath. You will find that all these matters we discussed are contained within it—separating between Israel and the nations, between light and darkness, and between the seventh day and the six...

# Gate 8

"He brought me out into a spacious place; He rescued me because He delighted in me" <note>Psalm 18:20</note>. "And their cry rose up to God from the bondage" <note>Exodus 2:23</note>. "And the children of Israel went up armed" <note>Exodus 13:18. The Hebrew word *chamushim* (armed) shares a root with *chamishim* (fifty), hinting at the 50 Gates of Understanding</note>. The attribute of Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term> ascended and was unified with the Sefirah of Understanding <term>Binah</term>. Through which Sefirah was the sea split? "And he moved... and he came... and he stretched out" <note>Exodus 14:19–21. These three verses each contain 72 letters, forming the mystical 72-fold Name of God</note>. (12) Kindness to Abraham <note>original: *Chesed le-Avraham*—referring to the Sefirah of Chesed</note>. Through which Sefirah was the Torah given? "And God spoke..." and "the mountain burned with fire." Which Sefirah is called the "Written Torah"? "The Torah of Truth was in his mouth" <note>Malachi 2:6</note>; "The judgments of the Lord are truth." You find then that the Written Torah, the judgments of truth, and Jacob (1) all rise in a single "reed"—the Middle Line <term>Kav Ha-Emtza'i</term> <note>The central pillar of the Sefirotic tree which balances the extremes of right/mercy and left/judgment</note>. "Israel, in whom I will be glorified" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note> and "to set you high above all the nations which He has made, for praise, for a name, and for glory."

Through which Sefirah did the prophets operate? "For my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts" <note>The title 'Lord of Hosts'—*YHVH Tzeva'ot*—is traditionally associated with the Sefirot of Victory (Netzach) and Splendor (Hod), the sources of prophecy</note>. "Have I not written for you three-fold things?" The Writings <note>Ketuvim</note>: "My dove, my undefiled, is but one" <note>Song of Songs 6:9</note>. It is a treasury of life, storehouses of blessing, the inheritance of Israel. Contemplate these deep hints and you will find how many goods the streams of Israel possess in every single one of the Ten Sefirot. The cause of inheriting all these goods is the Sefirah of Understanding <term>Binah</term>. Therefore, "you shall count fifty days" and it is all a Sabbath, a clinging of the Sefirah of Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term> to the Sefirah of Understanding <term>Binah</term>.

(2) "For the Leader, on stringed instruments, upon the eighth" <note>Psalm 6:1</note>. And the secret (3) is: "On the eighth day there shall be a solemn assembly <term>Atzeret</term> for you" <note>Numbers 29:35</note>, and "On the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly for the Lord your God." The ninth is His; the tenth is ours, because it is our inheritance and our portion. When the tenth is unified and clings to the ninth, all of Israel is as one, clinging to the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>. As it is said, "And you who cling to the Lord your God"—the scripture does not depart from its plain meaning. "You shall fear the Lord your God; Him you shall serve, and to Him you shall cling." "To Him you shall serve and to Him you shall cling"—you shall surely cling without a doubt.

As for what our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "Is it even possible for a person to cling to the Divine Presence?" It is indeed possible, and they revealed everything when they said: "A person should cling to the disciples of the wise" (4). It is well known who the disciples of the wise are: those taught by the Lord. This is the secret of the tenth Sefirah clinging to the ninth without a doubt. For whoever causes the "Assembly of Israel" <note>the people of Israel or the Sefirah of Malchut</note> to be unified with the Sefirah of Foundation <term>Yesod</term>, it is as if they are clinging to her, and she clings to the Foundation, and both of them together cling to the Lord, and the scripture does not depart from its plain meaning. **And after** we have explained this, we must enlighten your eyes with great principles, with the help of Him who illuminates the earth and those who dwell upon it. 

Know that the Sefirah of Understanding <term>Binah</term> is written as the four-letter name <note>YHWH</note> but pronounced as *Elohim* (God). It is the secret of the revelation of the three Upper Sefirot <note>Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding</note> through which the light of the Crown <term>Keter</term> and the Divine Will are revealed. This continues until the emanation, flow, and blessing reach the attribute of Foundation <term>Yesod</term>, which is the secret of the seven Sefirot. Or, the attribute of Foundation returns and pours out all types of flow and emanation of blessings into the attribute of Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term>, which is called *Adonai* (Lord). Therefore, Binah is called "Seven"—that is, the Sefirah that is sustained by the seven Sefirot above it, which are Understanding, Greatness <term>Chesed</term>, Might <term>Gevurah</term>, Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>, Victory <term>Netzach</term>, Splendor <term>Hod</term>, and Foundation <term>Yesod</term>. This is the meaning of "Bathsheba" <note>literally 'daughter of seven'</note> and "Beersheba" <note>literally 'well of seven'</note>. That is to say, a well that is filled from seven Sefirot. Likewise, the secret of Beersheba is called the Sefirah of <term>Binah</term> in terms of the flow and emanation, as it gushes all kinds of flow to the seven Sefirot beneath it. This is the rule: Beersheba is the secret of Binah pouring blessing to the seven lower Sefirot; Bathsheba is Malchut when she is filled with blessing from the seven Sefirot

# Gate 8

How did they depart from Egypt through **Understanding** <term>Binah; the third Sefirah, associated with the number fifty and the concept of liberation</term>? As it is said: "And the children of Israel went up *armed* <note>original: *v'chamushim*—a wordplay on *chamishim*, meaning fifty</note> from the land of Egypt." The sea was split through **Greatness** <term>Gedulah; another name for the Sefirah of Chesed or Kindness</term>, as it is said: "And Israel saw the **great** hand." And the mnemonic for this is "Kindness <note>Chesed</note> to Abraham." (A) "And he moved... and he came... and he stretched out..." <note>Exodus 14:19–21. These three verses, each containing 72 letters, are the source of the mystical 72-fold Name of God</note>
**Greatness** is **Kindness**. Through **Power** <term>Gevurah; the Sefirah of judgment and restraint</term> the Torah was given, as it is said: "And God <note>Elohim—the Name associated with Gevurah</note> spoke all these words, saying..." and "Now therefore, why should we die? For this **great fire** will consume us." (B) This is to say, "In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai." This refers to **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, which is the **third Sefirah** <note>counting from the top: Keter, Chokhmah, Binah</note> through which Israel left Egypt; on that day, they arrived at the wilderness of Sinai. One who knows the secret of these foundations will merit to "behold the **delight** of the Lord and to meditate in His temple" (C) "for this is the whole of man." (D) These are the **five Sefirot** <note>Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, and Hod</note>, and through them, they merited the gift of the Torah—the **Five Books of Moses**, five corresponding to five. (E) From there onward, we have the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings. (F) The **Torah** is one. The **Prophets** (G) as it says, "Have I not written for you **excellent things** <note>original: *shalishim*—literally 'officers' or 'triplicates'</note>?" The **Writings** (H) "My dove, my perfect one, is **one**," receiving from the nine "luminous lenses" <note>aspeklaria</note>. And behold, I am hinting: Which Sefirah was the cause of their departure from Egypt? (I) "**I Am That I Am**" <note>Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh</note>. To which Sefirah did their cry ascend? "From the straits I called to **Yah**." "And they cried out, and their plea ascended." (J) "Who would not fear You, O King of the nations?" In which Sefirah were they answered and went out? (K) "Answer me in a **spacious place**, O Lord <note>Yah</note>."

...until their souls are cleaved and return to the place of their quarry in the **fiftieth year**, the male portion of the **Great Jubilee** <term>Yovel; the 50th year of liberation, corresponding to Binah</term>, as we have explained. And this is what is meant by "the days of our lives." (F) The counting of the **seven weeks** in the Torah, fifty days, refers to **fifty thousand years**, for a "day" of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is a thousand years, as it is said: "For a thousand years in Your sight are like yesterday when it is past." And behold, each of the Sefirot is comprised of all of them; each ten of them results in one hundred, and each hundred comprised of ten results in one thousand. Thus, the "saw-wheel" <note>the cycle of emanations</note> returns to the eight kingdoms, to the **Crown** <term>Keter; the highest Sefirah</term>, for the letter *Kaph* (כ) <note>numerical value 20, but here discussed in its "extended" or "final" form</note> is spread out for "vision and trade" <note>a reference to the mystical reach of the Hebrew letters</note>. We must add that there is no other letter in the language of the Torah for a larger number. Since each is comprised of a thousand, there are **seven thousand**, and since each five is comprised of all, there are **ten thousand** of each, like the mystery of the "foundation of measures" for the arrangement of **Splendor** <term>Hod</term>, and there is no greater numbered name in the language. And behold, the seven corresponding to them, as will be clarified—each one includes them all in this way—and in it is **Kindness**, seven thousand, until they total **forty-nine thousand**, and they return to **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, which is the **fiftieth thousandth year**, the year of the "ascending generation" <note>the Jubilee of the cosmos</note>. And it is still as it is said: "The word He commanded to a **thousand generations**," for these are the true generations. These are the fifty thousand years of the "days of our life" that give us life. In the *Book of the System* <note>Sefer Ha-Ma'arekhet</note>, he elaborated on these cycles and Sabbatical years <note>Shemitot</note>, as did the **Recanati** <note>Rabbi Menahem Recanati, a 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note> in the portion of *Naso*. 

(A) "And he moved... and he came... and he stretched out" explains that **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> is within the three [verses], totaling **seventy-two** in the numerical value <term>Gematria</term> of the Names that emerge from these three verses. Regarding **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, the **Book of the Brightness** <term>Sefer Ha-Bahir; one of the earliest Kabbalistic texts</term> does not expound upon them; they are names for the hosts of the emanations of the attribute of Kindness, which is the secret of the "Upper Day." Correspondingly, the sea was split into **twelve paths**, and every part corresponds to a measure of these powers. This is why the sea was split through the attribute of **Greatness**, and the language of the verse "And Kindness is Greatness" is used because Greatness *is* Kindness.

(B) "In the **third month**," for Greatness was the third from Understanding <note>counting Binah, then Chokhmah, then Chesed/Gedulah in a specific descending order</note>, which is included in the name "Thirty" and in the power of Greatness. 

(C) "For this is the **whole of man**" explains that this is the purpose of every man: to perceive and know the secret of their actions and the Name, until he merits "beholding the delight of the Lord and visiting His temple," as it is said: "I will set him on high because he has known My Name." 

(D) These are the **five Sefirot**, meaning from Kindness <note>Chesed</note> until Power <note>Gevurah</note> <note>This likely refers to the five emotive attributes: Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod</note>, which are the five Sefirot through which the Torah was given.

He explains that the **Torah** is included in **Beauty** <term>Tiferet; the central Sefirah</term>, and from there the **Prophets** draw their nourishment through **Victory** <term>Netzach</term> and **Splendor** <term>Hod</term> <note>The source of prophecy</note>, and the **Writings** are categorized by the **Holy Spirit** which comes from **Sovereignty** <term>Malchut</term>, as mentioned at the beginning of Gate 3. Now he proceeds to explain through the verses: (F) "One Torah" from the verse "The **Torah of Truth** was in his mouth"; (G) **Prophets** from the verse "Have I not written for you **excellent things** <note>shalishim</note>?"; and (H) **Writings** from the verse "My dove is **one**," as he illustrated for you previously. 

He then returns to hint at the entire matter more clearly: that **Understanding** <note>Binah</note> was the source of the Exodus from Egypt, for the cause of their departure was the Name **I Am** (I) **That I Am**. This hints at the **Crown** <note>Keter</note>, because of their cry which ascended to **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term>, associated with the Name **Yah**, and their plea reached **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, which is included among the "Wise Ones." Through their inclusion in the triad of Understanding, they were answered and went out. The core of the secret is that **Sovereignty** <note>Malchut</note>, which is called "her plea," ascended to receive their cry, even reaching Wisdom. This is the meaning of (J) "**Who would not fear You, O King of the nations?**"—meaning "Who" <note>Mi, a name for Binah</note> is the Sovereignty over the "other nations," and it is **Understanding** <note>Binah</note> that oversees them all and writes in the Book of **Sovereignty** to seek [them]. Therefore, she was the one who brought the mentioned Israelites out. 

(K) "**Answer me in a spacious place, O Lord <note>Yah</note>**" refers to **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, which is the "spacious place" <note>merchav</note> of Wisdom, for it is called "Broad Streets" as will be seen. (L) To reach the reception, he explained they are [the powers of] *Chavak*...

# Gate 8

When these two **Sefirot** <term>Divine emanations</term> are in harmony with one another, the world exists in a state of **rectification** <term>Tikkun; a state of cosmic balance and repair</term>, fullness, and perfection. This is because all the **channels** <term>Tzinorot; the spiritual conduits through which divine light flows</term> are repaired, the Sefirot are unified, and blessing is sent down into the Sefirah of **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note>, which is called by the name **Adonai** <note>the Hebrew word for "Lord"</note>. However, this occurs in two ways. In some places you will find it written "Adonai YHVH," <note>original: אדנ"י יה"וה</note> as it says: "Lord YHVH, what will You give me?" (Genesis 15:2) <margin><unclear>Here is the explanation</unclear></margin> while in other places you find it written "YHVH Adonai," as it says: "YHVH is my strength" (Habakkuk 3:19). The secret is this: whenever the Sefirah of Kingship <note>Malchut</note> is adorned and perfectly rectified in its return below, we then call it **Adonai YHVH**—placing "Adonai" first. This is done to ascend from there to the level of **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, which is written as "YHVH" but pronounced as "Elohim" <note>God</note>. This is like the matter of **Abraham**, who would rectify and adorn the "Assembly of Israel" <note>Knesset Yisrael, a name for Malchut</note> through commandments and good deeds, in order to pour upon her the blessings from the abundance of **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, as he said: "Lord <note>Adonai</note> YHVH, what will You give me?" From where do we know that he rectified the path and adorned the attribute of Kingship? For it is said: "Because Abraham obeyed My voice (A) and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws" (Genesis 26:5). It is also written: "And he planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba" (Genesis 21:33). He began to plant the **saplings** <note>a metaphor for divine emanations</note> that the first Adam had "cut down" <note>a Kabbalistic term for causing a separation between the divine powers through sin</note>. And where did he plant them? In "Beersheba" <note>literally "Well of the Seven," a reference to Malchut which receives from the seven Sefirot above it</note>. Regarding him it is written (C): "And God went up from Abraham" (Genesis 17:22), and it is written (D): "And he built there an altar to YHVH" (Genesis 12:7). Because Abraham began to repair the damage and plant the "severed saplings," he began by saying "Adonai YHVH," rectifying the Sefirah of Kingship to pour into it and bring to it the abundance through the channels from the Sefirah of Understanding. This is the secret of what our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "'For the sake of the Lord <note>Adonai</note>'—for the sake of the Father <note>Abraham</note> who called You 'Master' <note>Adon</note>." 

And I am alluding to this: "Cause Your face to shine upon Your sanctuary that is desolate, for the sake of the Lord" (Daniel 9:17). That is to say: "Cause Your face to shine upon Your sanctuary that is desolate"—meaning, I ask only a small thing of You. For when the first Adam sinned, the **Shekhinah** <term>the Divine Presence</term> withdrew entirely. Then our father Abraham came and accepted it upon himself, and he became a "Throne for the Chariot," as it is said: "And God went up from Abraham." This continued until **Moses our Teacher** came and established a place for it in the Tabernacle, as it is said: "And I will meet with you there" (Exodus 25:22). Then **King Solomon** came and established it in the "House of Assembly," as it is said: "I have surely built You a house of habitation" (1 Kings 8:13). But when Israel sinned, it <note>the Shekhinah</note> traveled ten journeys away. **Daniel** then came and said: These journeys are not like the journeys of the first Adam. In the time of the first Adam, the Shekhinah had no fixed place; when Adam sinned, the Shekhinah withdrew. But once a place was established for the Shekhinah on earth, and once Solomon built the Holy Temple, even though it may withdraw at times, it never departs from its holy place forever, as it is said: "This is My resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it" (Psalm 132:14), and it says: "For the LORD has chosen Zion; He has desired it for His habitation" (Psalm 132:13). What is the meaning of "desired" <note>original: *ivah*</note>? It is like one who is far from the people of his household and **longs** <note>original: *mit'aveh*</note> for them. So too Solomon said: "A place for Your dwelling forever" (1 Kings 8:13). This means that even though He withdraws at times, He returns to this place, as it is said: "Thus says the LORD: I have returned to Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem" (Zechariah 8:3). And Jerusalem is called the "City of Truth" (G), the splendor of the LORD of Hosts, the Holy Mountain. And it says: "And I will betroth you to Me forever" (Hosea 2:21). Therefore, Daniel said: I ask of You a small request—that You return to Your place which is sanctified to You and from which it is impossible to be separated, for even though it has withdrawn from it...

# Gate 5

[the Sefirah] which is above her, and then she pours out blessings upon all beings above and below. Thus, you have learned that these two **Sefirot** <term>Divine emanations</term>, which are **Binah** <term>Understanding</term> and **Malchut** <term>Kingship</term>, are the cause of the revelation of the **Supreme Crown** <note>Keter Elyon, the highest and most hidden emanation</note> and the cause of the **Divine abundance** <term>Shefa; the spiritual flow of energy</term>, blessing, and sustenance for all existing things. The Sefirah of **Binah** draws the supreme flow from the Source to the seven Sefirot beneath it until the **Attribute of Malchut** <note>the lowest Sefirah, associated with the physical world</note> is filled with all types of flow and blessing. The Sefirah of Malchut then draws from every kind of blessing, flow, and emanation from the Sefirot above her, and then she provides for all beings above and below. This is because the Sefirah of Malchut is the secret of the "Great Provider" who sustains all created beings, as we explained in the first gate. Therefore, these two Sefirot—Binah and Malchut—are aligned with one another. From the attribute of Binah, all blessings come to the attribute of Malchut.

The secret of the verse **"A river went out of Eden"** (Genesis 2:10) is the secret of Binah, which emerges from the source of the Crown by way of **Chokhmah** <term>Wisdom</term>, which is called "Eden." This Binah is what is called **"Rehovot of the River"** <note>Rehovot means "broad places"; see Genesis 36:37</note>, whose purpose is to "water the Garden." The "Garden" is the Sefirah of Malchut, which receives all types of flow and blessing springing forth through the Sefirah of Binah. From there, the flow separates entirely; from the Sefirah of Malchut and below, the types of abundance divide to sustain all creatures according to the proper judgment. For up until the Sefirah of Malchut is the secret of the **True, Perfect Unity** <note>where the Godhead is unified</note>, but from the attribute of Malchut and below is the secret of the **"World of Separation"**.

**"And it became four heads"** (Genesis 2:10) refers to the secret of the four camps [of angels], from which all the various groups of created beings in the upper and lower worlds were divided within the world of angels—(9) and corresponding to them in the heavens, and corresponding to them on the earth. Everything follows the secret of the "four heads," which we will yet explain, with the help of the Blessed Creator. Therefore, know and believe that the Sefirah of Binah and the Sefirah of Malchut are both aligned with one another. When the attribute of Malchut is rectified through the **rectification of Israel** <term>Tikkun; the spiritual repair of the world</term> via the fulfillment of the **Torah and Commandments**, then the Sefirah of Binah appears to pour out all types of flow and blessing through the Sefirot until the Sefirah of Malchut is blessed and filled. Then, the inhabitants of the world find themselves in tranquility and security, and blessing is sent forth into all types of sustenance; thus, the blessing is found "clinging to the earth." This is the meaning of the verse **"If you walk in My statutes"** (Leviticus 26:3) and the order of all the blessings.

But if, Heaven forbid, Israel corrupted the order, transgressed the teachings, changed the law, and broke the covenant, then the Sefirah of Binah does not pour out blessing. It is as if—so to speak—the Sefirot are left in a state of deficiency because the source has been cut off. Consequently, the Sefirah of **Yesod** <term>Foundation; the channel of masculine energy</term> returns to gather itself and ascend to its place of longing in Binah, and the Sefirah of Malchut (3) is left alone, dry and lacking everything. Then the world finds itself in all kinds of curses. This is the matter of the curses mentioned in the Torah: that through the actions of Israel, the Sefirah of Malchut is stricken, as it says in the chapter (3) regarding the secret of **"the sorrow of our mother,"** and as it says: **"for your transgressions your mother was sent away"** (Isaiah 50:1). It is found that the Sefirah of **Tiferet** <term>Beauty/Splendor</term> is removed from the "stream" above it called Binah, and then the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael, another name for Malchut</note> is sent away and separated, as it says: **"He who plunders his father drives away his mother; he is a son who brings shame and disgrace"** (Proverbs 19:26). It also says: **"Because of the evil, the Righteous One is gathered in"** (Isaiah 57:1), the meaning of which I explained in the previous gates. It also says: **"A grumbler separates a close friend"** (Proverbs 16:28).

Therefore, it is found that the Sefirah of Malchut—all her longing, desire, and wish—is for the Sefirah of Binah, and both are aligned one against the other. In the **Jubilee year** <note>Yovel; the 50th year, associated with Binah</note>, they are united in a perfect union, and redemption comes to the Sefirah of Malchut, which is the secret of the "Land." This is what the scripture means: **"And in all the land of your possession, you shall grant redemption to the land"** (Leviticus 25:24). Once you know this, contemplate every place in the Torah where you find written **YHVH ADONAI** <note>original: יהוה אדנ"י</note>—both names adjacent to one another. You shall know and understand that these are the two Sefirot: one is the Sefirah of Binah, which is written as YHVH but [sometimes] called **Elohim** <term>God</term>, and the second is the Sefirah of Malchut, which is called **Adonai** <term>Lord</term>. This is the secret of YHVH ADONAI; understand this. Now, we must inform you that when they unite...
