### Gate 9

"All nations surrounded me" <note>original: "Goyim sevavuni," from Psalm 118:10</note> refers to the place where the guardian angels of the nations have a foothold. This is the mystery of the letter **Vav** <term>Vav; the sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the number six and the central column of the Sefirot</term> within the Name, which includes the six *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot; the ten divine attributes or emanations</term>. For the mystery of the **Vav** in the Name is called **YHVH** throughout the entire Torah. Your sign for this is: "Yours, O **YHVH**, is the **Greatness**, the **Might**, the **Beauty**, the **Victory**, and the **Splendor**" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>; **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note> is the "lower point." Regarding this, it is said, "All nations surrounded me," for all the guardian angels of the nations encompass the letter **Vav** of the Name. However, over the **Vav** and above—which is the mystery of **Yah** <note>the first two letters of the Name, Yod and He</note>—they have no power. "And you shall tread upon their high places" <note>Deuteronomy 33:29</note>, "I will cause you to ride on the high places of the earth, and feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father" <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>.

Because it is said, "All nations surrounded me," it is also said, "Amalek was the first of the nations" <note>Numbers 24:20</note>. Therefore, **(a)** he was the first to enter and exile the secrets of Israel, stretching out his hand against the last two letters of the Name: **Vav** and **He**. Consequently, "Because a hand is upon the throne of **Yah**, **YHVH** will have war with Amalek" <note>Exodus 17:16; the verse uses "Yah" and "Kes" instead of the full words for Lord and Throne, implying the Name is incomplete while Amalek exists</note>. When it says "war with **YHVH** against Amalek," one does not know who is against whom; **(b)** when it says "from generation to generation" <note>mi-dor dor</note>, the matter is revealed, and the place where the hand of Amalek stretched out is revealed. **(c)** The sign for this is: "A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever" <note>Ecclesiastes 1:4</note>. **(d)** "This is My name forever <note>original: le'olam</note>, and this is My memorial from generation to generation" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>. Therefore, "Remember, O **YHVH**, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, who said, 'Raze it, raze it, even to its foundation!'" <note>Psalm 137:7</note>.

Once you know this, you can contemplate what the prophets established in two places. Obadiah, who was also an Edomite <note>traditionally a convert from Edom</note>, said in his prophecy regarding Edom: "And deliverers shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, **(e)** and the kingdom shall be **YHVH's**" <note>Obadiah 1:21</note>. Zechariah said: "For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem to battle... and **YHVH** shall go forth and fight against those nations, as when He fought in the day of battle," and then, "**YHVH** shall be King over all the earth; on that day **YHVH** shall be one and His name one" <note>Zechariah 14:2-9</note>. And it says, "Amalek was the first of the nations." This is the mystery of "Because a hand is upon the throne of **Yah**, **YHVH** will have war with Amalek from generation to generation."

Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, established these two verses at the end of the *Verses of Praise* <term>Pesukei D'Zimra; a section of the morning prayer service consisting of Psalms and biblical songs</term>: "And deliverers shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, and the kingdom shall be **YHVH's**" and "**YHVH** shall be King over all the earth; on that day **YHVH** shall be one and His name one." In this place, they brought these two prophecies close to one another. Through the unification of these two prophecies, the Name, may He be blessed, becomes unified. He who understands the depth of what they established in this matter will understand the secret of "All nations surrounded me" through the Name **YHVH**, for "in the Name of **YHVH** I will cut them off" <note>Psalm 118:10</note>, as well as the secret of "Amalek was the first of the nations," the secret of the Torah portion *Remember* <note>Zakhor; Deuteronomy 25:17-19</note>, and the secret of the portion *The Crossing of the Jabbok* <note>Genesis 32:23-33</note>. Therefore, you should contemplate what is written in the Torah: "Because a hand is upon the throne of **Yah**"—it is through this that salvations, redemptions, and good things come to Israel. For when Israel is in exile, the distress, as it were, touches Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and the "Generation" <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> included in the mystery of **Vav-He**. Therefore, the name **Yah** <note>Yod-He</note> must save and redeem. The sign is: "The Lord <note>Yah</note> is my strength and song, and He has become my salvation" <note>Exodus 15:2</note>. And it says, "Out of the distress I called upon **Yah**" <note>Psalm 118:5</note>.

That which is hinted at in this portion can be understood from "And he led" <note>original: vayolekh</note>... and from the general rule of all that he learned and the hints in the verses. They are comprised of the names of the *Sefirot* and their places, until the mystery of **(a)** *entering first to exile the secrets of Israel*—meaning that they were originally within the "Crowns" and hidden in every order, and he revealed their secret and revealed their place to bring the inner to the outside and the outer to the inside. And they said **(b)** *when he says "And the foundation of the generation revealed the matter and revealed the place where the hand of Amalek stretched out"*—explaining that after "war of **YHVH** against Amalek," the judgment of His hand will appear "from generation to generation" <note>mi-dor dor</note>. This "generation to generation" refers to the *Foundation* <note>Yesod</note> and the *Kingdom* <note>Malkhut</note> which is called "Generation to Generation," as explained above in Gate 2 under the designation "All." And he said **(c)** *and since "a generation goes and a generation comes"*—for sometimes the flow of light departs from it and departs from Israel, and sometimes it is within it. The essence of the name "Generation" <note>Dor</note> refers to the **Diadem** <note>Ataret, another name for Malkhut</note>, and "the earth stands forever"—meaning that the Earth <note>Malkhut</note> always stands ready to receive. It also hints at "a generation goes and a generation comes" regarding the souls that go out from it into the world, and it stands eternally to receive. **(d)** "This is My name forever <note>le'olam/le'alem - to hide</note> and this is My memorial for generation and generation"—meaning, this is My name, the God of Abraham and Isaac from the beginning of the world and the thought of the Building, as in "a world of kindness shall be built" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>. And "this is My memorial," which is the kindness of Abraham, shall be remembered with "generation and generation," which is the Diadem that was His dwelling place. This is "He who dwells with them in the midst of their impurity" <note>Leviticus 16:16</note>. **(e)** "And the kingdom shall be **YHVH's**"—explaining that the Kingdom shall return to its precision when the deliverers ascend, who are the Lord God, in order to judge Amalek who carries his power, as explained above in Gate 2... and so too is the hint in the prophecies of Zechariah... when Amalek is [defeated], then everything will be [restored].

<header>Gate 9</header>

**"And the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot"** <note>Genesis 8:9</note>. Even though Israel stood at Sinai and their impurity <term>Zohama; the spiritual filth or "venom" left by the primordial serpent</term> ceased, the blemish of the moon <term>Pegam ha-Levanah; a Kabbalistic concept referring to the diminishment of the feminine divine presence, or Malkhut, which allows for the existence of evil</term> was never removed, except occasionally through "leaps" during the offering of certain **goats (a)**. Among these, the "primary goat" such as that of **Amalek** <note>The archetypal enemy of Israel in the Bible, representing doubt and the power of evil</note> is attached, as it is written, "Amalek was the first of the nations" <note>Numbers 24:20</note>. When **Amalek (b)** came, he added transgression to the blemish of the moon and "touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh" <note>Genesis 32:25</note>; **(c)** consequently, the Kingdom of the House of David was breached.

And behold, when the "plantings were cut down" <term>Kitzutz ba-Neti'ot; a metaphor for heresy or causing separation between the Sefirot</term> during the time of the first man <note>Adam</note>, and Amalek touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh, **(d)** the portion of "Remember" <term>Parashat Zachor; the biblical command to remember and wipe out Amalek</term> was established. Thus, the last two letters of the Name—as it were—are blemished by Amalek. The **reason (e)** is that the hand of the Lord touched them, as it says, "the hand of the Lord will be against you" <note>1 Samuel 12:15</note>, and it says **(f)** "the way of a serpent upon a rock" <note>Proverbs 30:19</note>. "And Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim" <note>Exodus 17:8</note>—meaning, through **weakness of hands (g)** <note>original: "Raphon Yadayim," a wordplay on the place name Rephidim</note>.

Therefore, it was necessary to say that both the ancient serpent and Amalek touched the last two letters, which are ***Vav*** and ***He***. Nothing remained of the Name that they did not stretch their hand against except the letters ***Yod*** and ***He*** <note>Yah</note>, because there is no place for the celestial princes <note>the guardian angels of the nations</note> to take hold of them, for they are "above," as we have explained. **(h)** Therefore, it says, "Because a hand is upon the throne of Yah" <note>Exodus 17:16; original: "Ki Yad al Kes Yah"</note>—they touched the "throne" <term>Kise; representing the Sefirah of Malkhut</term> and caused a blemish in it, so it remained only *Kes* <note>the word "throne" (Kisse) is written defectively as "Kes" in this verse</note>. They touched the last two letters, and only *Yah* remained. Therefore, "upon the throne of Yah." **(i)** Whoever understands this will understand the secret of the "Remember" portion and the secret of the **crossing (j)** of the **Jabbok**, for everything is included in these places. And here I am hinting: All...

---

...like the ancient serpent, and the serpent itself, its attachment and power is "from generation to generation" <note>Exodus 17:16</note>, which are the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> and Kingdom <note>Malkhut</note>...
**Secret:** **(a)** The "certain goats" are the goats of the New Moon and the goats of the sin offerings. They come to remove the accusations of the prosecutors <note>demonic forces</note> who are called "goats" <note>original: "se'irim," which can also mean satyrs or demons</note>. The "primary goat" was Samael <note>the chief angel of the "other side"</note>, and he is the head of all the goats. He attaches himself and waits by those goats so that his power is nullified and the blemish is removed through those sacrifices, so he has no opening to prosecute or blemish the Splendor <note>Hod</note>... **(b)** When Amalek came, he added transgression to the moon's blemish—meaning, he added accusation to the blemish of the first man and further separated the Crown <term>Atarah; another name for Malkhut</term>, which is the "hollow of Jacob's thigh," from its Foundation <note>Yesod</note>... **(c)** Consequently, the Kingdom of the House of David was breached—meaning the Crown was separated, for the Kingdom of David depends on that place... **(d)** Because of this accusation and separation, the "Remember" portion was established, meaning we should remember and specify this to return and establish the Male with the Female <note>the union of the divine attributes</note>... **(e)** The reason "the hand of YHVH touched them" refers to the "weak hand" <note>original: "Yad Kehah," a kabbalistic term for a diminished state of power</note> Israel had when they were separated... **(f)** "The way of a serpent upon a rock" refers to the knowledge of Samael... **(g)** "In Rephidim"—at a time when there was a "weakness of hands" <note>spiritual laxity</note>... **(h)** "A hand upon the throne of Yah"—the place of his touching was the Throne, which is the Crown, causing a separation from the upper letters, so *Kes* remained and *Yah* remained. **(i)** One who understands this understands the secret of the "Remember" portion... and the secret of the **Jabbok Crossing** <note>Genesis 32:23</note>. For there, the guardian angel of Esau <note>Samael</note> attached himself to destroy Jacob... he saw he could not prevail because Jacob is "above" in the Middle Column <term>Kav ha-Emtza'i; the balancing path of the Sefirot</term>, so he "touched the hollow of his thigh," which is the Crown, where he had a place to take hold... even though Jacob came and repaired it at this crossing, as our Sages said. **Jabbok** <note>Y-B-Q</note> in numerical value <term>Gematria</term> equals the three names: **Eheyeh, YHVH, Adonai** <note>21 + 26 + 65 = 112, which is the value of Y-B-Q</note>, which must be repaired and joined together in a perfect union. Even so, he could not remove the blemish completely... the word "And he passed" <note>Vayavor</note> refers to the number of the 72 Names... and these three names included in the word Jabbok have 12 letters, corresponding to the 12 permutations of the Name. Here you have the entire secret.

# Gate 9
### Page 98

For Wisdom and Understanding <note>original: *Chokhmah* and *Binah*</note> are the roots of the **Attribute of Justice** <term>Midat Ha-Din; the divine quality of strict law and limit</term>, even though it is not yet complete Justice. Complete Justice begins from **Greatness** and **Might** <term>Gedulah (also known as Chesed/Kindness) and Gevurah (Strength/Severity)</term>, which are the realms where the surrounding ministers <note>angelic forces or spiritual powers</note> take hold and where the Sanhedrins and houses of judgment are established, as we have explained. 

Nevertheless, some degree of judgment exists within the Name **Yah** <note>Yod-Heh, the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>, but it acts with gentleness and not as a final verdict. A final verdict only issues from **Greatness** and **Might** and below. Therefore, the psalmist says: "If You, **Yah**, should mark iniquities, **Adonai**, who could stand?" <note>Psalm 130:3</note>. 

The explanation of this verse is: if **Yah**, which is the **World of Mercy**, were to "keep" or "guard" our sins—meaning, if we were to encounter the strictness of Judgment <note>the attribute of Gevurah</note> while those sins were being handed over to the power of **Malkhut** <term>Kingship; the lowest Sefirah</term>, which is represented by the Name **Adonai**—who could endure? Who could survive?

We have already explained in the first Gate that when the attribute of **Malkhut** is awakened to finalize judgment upon created beings, it consumes everything "from soul to flesh," as we explained regarding the verse: "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:14</note>. We expanded greatly on the explanation of this matter. Therefore, if You "guard" sins through **Yah**, which is the World of Mercy, then regarding **Adonai**, which is the World of Judgment: who could stand before You? Who could survive?

And now, we have placed in your hand the "keys" for every place in the Torah where you find the Name **Yah**. From what we have handed over, you can reflect on other places and understand one thing from another. You must also know the path opened in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an early mystical text</note>: "With thirty-two mystical paths of wisdom, **Yah**... engraved... the Lord of Hosts" <note>original: *Adonai Tzabaot*</note> and so on. 

Why was it necessary to mention the Name **Yah** in that context? The reason is that **Yah** is the secret of the three highest Sefirot, the World of Mercy. The Tetragrammaton <note>Y-H-V-H</note> is the secret of **Tiferet** <term>Beauty; the central pillar of the Sefirotic tree</term>, the place to which our teacher Moses (peace be upon him) was attached and the source from which the Patriarchs drew their sustenance. **Tzabaot** <note>Hosts</note> is the secret of the sustenance of the Prophets. This order of the levels of the Sefirot is counted here, and we will elaborate on this, God willing.

Now that we have provided these principles regarding the Name **Yah**, we shall enter into an explanation of the other Names by which this Sefirah is called in the Torah, so that you may understand, know, and gain insight, with the help of God.

Know that this Sefirah is called in the Torah **Yesh** <term>Existence/Is; original: יש</term>. You must understand the reason: the first Sefirah, which is **Keter** <term>Crown</term>, is hidden from the eyes of all living things, and no one can contemplate it. For this reason, it is called **Ayin** <term>Nothingness; original: אין</term>, as we will explain later with the Creator’s help. If a person comes to ask a question about it, the answer to their question is "Nothing" <note>Ayin</note>—meaning, there is no one who can contemplate its deep and exalted secret. Therefore, it is not designated by a specific letter, but only by a hint: the "thorn" <note>the small stroke at the top</note> of the letter *Yod*.

However, the beginning of the expansion of thought and the first revelation of order is the second Sefirah, called **Chokhmah** <term>Wisdom</term>. In this place, it is possible to ask, for even though it is not fully revealed, it is not entirely hidden (a) <gloss>like the first Sefirah, for it has some revelation and knowledge through Understanding (Binah), according to the selections gathered from Wisdom</gloss> like the first. In this second Sefirah, which is Wisdom, lies the secret of the beginning of the "Question." 

Because the first is so hidden it is called **Ayin** ("Nothing"); the second, because there is some room for inquiry following the expansion of the emanation of the Sefirot from the Crown, is called **Yesh** ("Being" or "There is"). 

Our father Jacob already revealed the secrets of this Sefirah, for it was more fitting for him than for Abraham or Isaac. This is because his inheritance ascends through the **Middle Pillar**, which is **Da'at** <term>Knowledge</term>, up to the World of Mercy. Thus: "And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder was set on the earth, and its top reached to heaven... and behold, the Lord stood over it." Jacob awoke from his sleep and said: "Surely the Lord **is** [**Yesh**] in this place" <note>Genesis 28:12-16</note>. It was fitting for him to hint at this matter, as it is said of him: "I will cause you to ride on the high places of the earth." I am hinting at the vision of this dream where it is said (b) <gloss>"And you shall spread out to the west and to the east," etc., which was not said to the other Patriarchs. As we have learned, this refers to the expansion in all directions—up, down, right, and left—as explained several times in Gate 5.</gloss> and he "rose above the daughters of the land" and said, "Surely the Lord is [**Yesh**] in this place." The explanation of this portion is long, and we are not presently engaged in its full commentary.

<meta>The previous page established that while the Name "Yah" (the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton) represents a high level of Mercy, the lower realms—specifically the "Attribute of Justice"—are where judgment is finalized. This page explores how the Name "Yah" acts as a "Broad Place" that provides refuge from the "Narrow Straits" of the worldly nations and the forces of judgment.</meta>

# Gate 9

From the "Strait" <note>original: *Metzar*; meaning a narrow place or distress</note>, which is the secret of the boundaries belonging to the seventy angelic princes of the nations who surround [Israel]. "All her pursuers overtook her between the straits" <note>Lamentations 1:3</note>. Therefore, "From the strait I called to **Yah**" <note>Psalm 118:5</note>, for He has no "straits" or boundaries, as He is the place of the **Broad Places** <term>Rehovot; a reference to the expansive nature of the higher Sefirot</term> and the River. This is the ascent of Mercy, where the heavenly princes and their bodies have no place to take hold. Only Jacob, who represents the **Middle Line** <term>Tiferet; the Sefirah that balances Mercy and Judgment</term>, can grasp this level, ascending even higher than Abraham and Isaac. This is why it is written: "I will make you ride on the heights of the earth and feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father" <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>. And regarding this it says, "From the strait I called to **Yah**."

When the verse says, "**Yah** answered me in a broad place," it refers to the three highest Sefirot <note>Keter (Crown), Chokhmah (Wisdom), and Binah (Understanding)</note>. These are never fully revealed to the world. The third, which is **Binah** <term>Understanding</term>, is revealed only partially and not in its entirety. This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, meant when they said: "Fifty gates of Understanding were created in the world, and all were given to Moses except for one" <note>Talmud Rosh Hashanah 21b</note>. This one missing gate is equal to all the other forty-nine gates combined. Because **Binah** is the third Sefirah, the two higher Sefirot—which are never seen at all—act through it. **Binah** is called the "Broad Places of the River" <note>original: *Rehovot Ha-Nahar*</note>, and through it come all salvations and redemptions, as we have explained. Therefore, "**Yah** answered me in a broad place" refers to that third Sefirah called **Broad Places**.

Isaac also said, "For now **Yahweh** has made room for us" <note>Genesis 26:22</note>. This verse is of great necessity. Behold, it was through **Binah**, which is "Broad Places" and the secret of the Fifty [Gates], that we went out of Egypt <note>original: *Mitzrayim*; a word sharing the root with *Metzar*, meaning "straits"</note>. It is the secret of all salvations and redemptions, as we explained. Therefore: "**Yah** is my strength and song, and He has become my salvation" <note>Exodus 15:2</note>. The Torah said this as a hint, but the Prophet revealed it more clearly, saying: "Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid; for **Yah**, **Yahweh**, is my strength and song; He also is become my salvation" <note>Isaiah 12:2</note>. In that place, there is no room for fear, for there are no "straits" <note>distress or boundaries</note> there. The Torah said, "**Yah** is my strength," and the Prophet explained that when the flow of **Yah** <note>the first two letters</note> takes hold of the last two letters <note>Vav and Heh</note>, the name **Yahweh** becomes One—this is the complete salvation.

One who understands this will understand the secret of "A hand upon the throne of **Yah**, **Yahweh** will have war [with Amalek]" <note>Exodus 17:16</note>, and the secret of "And the kingdom shall be **Yahweh's**" <note>Obadiah 1:21</note>, and the secret of "On that day **Yahweh** shall be one and His name one" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>—with a complete Name, **Y-H** with **V-H**.

Now that we have informed you of these high principles, we must explain the secret of what Hezekiah said in his prayer: "I said: I shall not see **Yah**, **Yah** in the land of the living" <note>Isaiah 38:11</note>. What does "I shall not see **Yah**" mean? Since he was told, "You shall die and not live," Hezekiah said: "Behold, I will not see the World to Come," which is the World of Life <gloss>(a)</gloss>, represented by the Name **Yah**, as we explained above. He meant that even if he were worthy of seeing the Sefirah of **Malkhut** <term>Kingship</term>, which is the last one, he felt he lacked the merit to see even that. The reason is that the Sefirot emanating from the Name **Yah** shine there. **Malkhut** is called the "Land of the Living" because it receives the flow from the World of Life, which is the secret of **Yah**, in which **Binah** is included. 

"I shall behold man no more with the inhabitants of the world" <gloss>(b)</gloss> <note>Isaiah 38:11</note>. This is the secret of the **First Adam** <note>Adam HaRishon</note>, who returned in repentance and ceased from sin. You will hear more of this, God willing. If so, reflect: whenever you find the name **Yah**, even though it is the secret of the Sefirah of **Chokhmah** <term>Wisdom</term>, it alludes to the **World of Mercy**, which is the secret of the three highest Sefirot. While some small amount of Judgment exists in **Chokhmah** and **Binah**, the **Crown** <note>Keter</note> is entirely pure Mercy. Even though it is the World of Mercy <gloss>(c)</gloss>, a small amount of Judgment is nonetheless mixed into the Name **Yah**,

In the First Wisdom, and His will in the Last Wisdom; and after we have handed over to you these great principles regarding the word "Wisdom," we must inform you of the remaining matters included in this Sefirah <term>Sefirah: One of the ten divine attributes or emanations through which the Infinite interacts with the world</term>, with the help of Heaven. This is the place where there is no power to contemplate at all, for no created being, above or below, can know how the Divine Desire spreads through the emanation of the Sefirot. And Moses, our teacher—peace be upon him—asked: *"Please, make known to me Your ways"* <note>Exodus 33:13</note>. This is the secret of *"I will proclaim the name of YHVH before you"* <margin>original: (א) and therefore He said: "And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious," meaning it is by His Will, and no one knows how to speak of it.</margin>. <meta>This page continues the exploration of the Ninth Gate, shifting from the concept of the Divine Will to the distinction between the "First Wisdom" (Chochmah) and the "Last Wisdom" (Malchut). It explains why the tenth Sefirah is sometimes given the same name as the second, and how the letters of the Divine Name (YHVH) represent these cosmic states of union and separation.</meta>

# Gate 9

That the tenth Sefirah <term>Sefirah: A divine attribute or channel through which the Infinite light is filtered</term>, which is called **Sovereignty** (Malchut), is also sometimes called **Wisdom** (Chochmah), as it is said: *"And God gave wisdom to Solomon"* <note>1 Kings 5:9; here Solomon represents the lower manifestation of wisdom</note>. However, the **Supreme Wisdom**, which is the secret of the letter *Yud* (י) of the Divine Name, was hidden even from Moses our teacher—peace be upon him—and no creature can enter it. For he did not attain the fiftieth of the Gates of **Understanding** (Binah), and Wisdom is even "further" <note>deeper or more internal</note> than Understanding. Regarding this Wisdom, which is the secret of the *Yud* of the Name, the Kabbalists said: "Wisdom is at the beginning." And regarding the Last Wisdom, which is the secret of the *He* (ה) of **Sovereignty**, they said: "Wisdom is at the end." This is to say that the first light of the Name, which is the letter *Yud*, and this last light, which is the letter *He*, are both uniquely called by the name "Wisdom." Therefore, they said "Wisdom at the beginning and Wisdom at the end." Since the First Wisdom is the furnace where thought is abstracted from the **Crown** (Keter), it has no measure or limit compared to anything that follows it. About it, it is said: *"Wisdom—from where (Ayin) shall it be found?"* <note>Job 28:12</note>. "From where" <note>original: "Ayin," which also means "Nothingness"</note> is the secret of the spreading of thought from the Crown. *"God understood its way"* <note>Job 28:23</note>, but not its place. Contemplate this: "God understood its way"—it is through **Understanding** (Binah) that one enters to perceive the Supreme Wisdom; *"And He knows its place"*—"He" refers to the secret of the **Crown**, from which Wisdom is certainly drawn; He knows its place. This is the Wisdom that is the beginning of the expansion of thought, the head of **Emanation** (Atzilut). Of it, it is said: *"YHVH founded the earth with wisdom, established the heavens with understanding; by His knowledge the depths were broken"* <margin>original: (ב) We are not currently explaining these verses, but above in chapter 5 you will find them somewhat explained through the "covering of knowledge," and also at the beginning of Gate 8.</margin>. We are not dealing with the literal explanation of these verses now. What you must know and contemplate is that wherever you find "Wisdom," you must know and discern whether it refers to the Supreme Wisdom or the Last Wisdom. Know that this is the Wisdom that is never separated from Understanding in the higher worlds, for both of them are Divinity within the Sefirah of the Crown, which is the world of Mercy—the place where there is neither sadness, nor anger, nor separation, but only "glory and majesty, strength and joy." Because these two Sefirot, **Wisdom** and **Understanding**, are eternally united, the name *Yah* (יה) <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note> never changes. But if, Heaven forbid, Israel sins and causes a separation for the "Last Wisdom," they separate her from the *Yud*, as it is said: *"A grumbler separates the Chief"* <note>Proverbs 16:28</note>. Therefore, the "Last *He*" sometimes becomes separated from the *Vav* (ו). When she is separated from the *Vav*, the *Vav* is gathered upward and is not seen, since its mate—the "Last *He*"—is separated from it. This is the meaning of *"I will hide My face from the house of Jacob"* <note>Isaiah 8:17</note>. Since the **Divine Presence** (Shekhinah), which is the letter *He*, is in exile, the letter *Vav* is not seen; only *Yah* (יה) remains alone, the place where there is no separation. This is the secret of *"Because of the evil, the righteous one is gathered"* <margin>original: (ג) "The righteous one is gathered"—this is the "point" of the lower *Vav*. This is because when the "Last He" is in exile, the Name is not "Shalom" (Peace/Whole) and the Throne is not whole.</margin>. For when the *Vav*—which is **Beauty** (Tiferet)—is divided, the "Righteous One" is gathered, which is the point of the lower *Vav* <note>Referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note>. When we said that the First Wisdom is specified in many places in the Torah in well-known verses, it does not mean that even if the verse is specific to one thing, the Last Wisdom is not also hinted at within it. Often, a verse speaks of the First Wisdom while hinting at the Last Wisdom, such as: *"YHVH founded the earth with wisdom, established the heavens with understanding."* Which of these two Sefirot is greater? Surely it is Wisdom. If so, why does it say "With Wisdom He founded the earth" <note>the lower realm</note>, while the heavens, which are higher, were "With Understanding"? Rather, the matter speaks of the First Wisdom but hints at the Last Wisdom. "With Wisdom He founded the earth"—this is the secret of Wisdom, which contains more mercy than Understanding <margin>original: (ד) And it was a necessity for human beings in their exile, and therefore with it He "founded the earth." According to this, it mentions the First Wisdom (which is the essence of the earth) because the main guidance and completion of the earth is through it.</margin>, and it is a necessity for human beings. But the heavens, where there is nothing but uprightness and purity, He established with a measure that has more "Judgment" (Din) than Wisdom <note>referring to Understanding/Binah</note>. Likewise, *"YHVH founded the earth with wisdom"* speaks of the Last Wisdom, which is the essence of the "Earth" <note>Malchut</note>. *"Established the heavens with understanding"* (ה) is the secret of the attribute of Judgment to some degree, corresponding to the heavens. Thus, the matter speaks of Wisdom...

<meta>This page continues the discussion from Gate 9, focusing on the relationship between the higher Sefirot—Crown (Keter) and Wisdom (Chochmah)—and the realm of Understanding (Binah). # Gate 9

You enter to draw from the depth of the well of **Thought**, but the one who draws stands outside. The sign for this is: *“Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out”* <note>Proverbs 20:5</note>. For there is no way to draw water from the depth of **Thought** except through **Understanding** (*Binah*). One who understands this should reflect on what we said previously: that no person has ever entered further than the realm of **Understanding**—not even Moses our teacher. Even if he attained anything of the two upper Sefirot <term>Sefirot: The ten divine emanations or attributes in Kabbalah</term> that are beyond them, he stood outside and drew from them only by means of the Sefirah of **Understanding**.

Regarding this, it is said: *“That which was is far off, and exceeding deep; who can find it out?”* <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>. Behold, we have already explained the secret of **"Who"** (*Mi*) in the previous gates. “Deep, deep” refers to the two upper Sefirot: **Crown** (*Keter*) and **Thought** (*Machshavah*), which is cleaved to it, for there is no end, limit, boundary, or measure to the World of Mercy. If a seeker attains anything of them, he will only "find it" through the Sefirah called **"Who"** (*Mi*), which is **Understanding**. This is the meaning of: *"Exceeding deep, **Who** (Mi) can find it out?"*

I shall now hint at the usage of the word **"Who"** (*Mi*):
1. *“Out of **whose** (Mi) womb came the ice?”* <note>Job 38:29</note>. The "Ice" is the secret of the final letter *He* (ה) of the Divine Name, for its waters have congealed.
2. **"Who"** (*Mi*) is the limit given for inquiry. Up to this point, one may ask; from here and beyond, it is like "placing a finger in the eye" <note>An idiom meaning it is dangerously beyond human perception</note>.
3. *“**Who** (Mi) can utter the mighty acts of the Lord?”* <note>Psalms 106:2</note>.
4. *“**Who** (Mi) created these?”* <note>Isaiah 40:26</note>.
5. *“For ask now of the days that are past... since the day that God created man upon the earth.”* <note>Deuteronomy 4:32</note> You are asking of **"Who"** (*Mi*), who was consulted and who gave understanding.
6. The sign: *“Then (Az) sang Moses and the children of Israel.”* <note>Exodus 15:1</note> The word *Az* (אז) alludes to the structure of the Sefirot. *“Your throne is established from then (me-Az).”* <note>Psalms 93:2</note>
7. I shall further hint: **One and one; one and two; one and three; one and four; one and five; one and six; one and seven.** <note>This refers to the High Priest’s counting while sprinkling blood in the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur</note>.
8. *“He shall go out and leave it upon the golden [altar].”*
9. *“For it is the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippurim).”* It is literally the Day of Atonement <note>In Kabbalah, the "Day of Atonement" is a manifestation of the Sefirah of Binah/Understanding</note>.
10. **Nothing** (Ayin) from above to below, and **nothing** from below to above. During that service on the Day of Atonement, he did not intend to sprinkle upwards or downwards, but rather like one who lashes with a whip <note>A specific ritual motion described in the Mishnah, Yoma 5:3</note>.

And Solomon commanded and said on the day that the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) was established in speech and fixed in its place below, then Solomon said: *“The Lord said that He would dwell in the thick darkness. I have surely built You a house of habitation.”* <note>1 Kings 8:12-13</note> The sign for this is: *“Like Rachel and like Leah, who both built the house of Israel.”* <note>Ruth 4:11</note> Rachel and Leah represent the Sabbatical year and the Jubilee—the "Lower *He*" and the "Upper *He*" of the Divine Name.

We must also awaken your attention to what our Sages said: "It **arose** in Thought" <note>A phrase used in Midrash to describe God's primordial intent for creation</note>. They did not say it "descended." Know that the secret of "arose in Thought" means that the Supreme Thought—called the **Will** (*Ratzon*)—is without limit. This second Sefirah does not move to go outside the world of **Understanding**. Rather, this Thought remains secluded and is always beautifully situated in the **Supreme Crown**. If a seeker needs to draw something from it, he must **ascend** to it through **Understanding** and enter it to draw from it. But Thought itself never "descends" below. All this applies to all the creatures created in the world.

->Regarding<-

the **Point**, which is the beginning of the line. The lower, inner point is explained as being the visualization of a dot within the imaginative thought. Such is the definition of a "point" in every context: something that cannot be divided at all, not even in thought. This is not only because of its extreme thinness and smallness, but because it has no dimension, boundary, measure, extension, or form.

Therefore, this measure, according to the sustenance given within it, is called a **"Thought-Point."** It is a descent that is beautiful for that which is above it. For this reason, they compared it to this point and called it "deep," etc. And **Wisdom** they compared to a "deep hand" <note>original: "Yad" (Hand), possibly a scribal variant for 'point' or 'power'</note> which is like a point.

The secret of the "Ice" is the secret of the "Lower *He*," for its waters were congealed through this. The waters of Understanding were congealed and became like a solid floor. This power comes from the secret of the "First *He*" and the "Final *He*" <note>The two letters He in the name YHVH</note>. Regarding the verses that mention the language of **"Who"** (*Mi*), they return to **Understanding**.
1. *"In **Who** (Mi) was the power of inquiry given?"*
2. *"And **who** (Mi) can utter the mighty acts of the Lord?"*
3. *"Since the day God created man on the earth,"* you investigate **Understanding**, which includes all things. It hints that "upon her" all things depend.
4. The sign: *"Then (Az) sang Moses."* This hints at **Understanding** with the nine Sefirot below it. It tells us that his staff's protection reached as far as Understanding, but not above it.

He continues to hint at this secret through the counting of the Day of Atonement:
The **"One"** stands by itself, connecting with the Crown above it. Then "One and one," as **Wisdom** and **Understanding** connect with the seven below them. "One and two" with **Kindness** (*Hesed*), "One and three" with **Power/Fear** (*Gevurah*), and so on. This is the secret of: *"The Lord sent from above to below."* Likewise, the transition from below to above: **Sovereignty** (*Malchut*) is fixed in the **Foundation** (*Yesod*). This is the secret of "One and..." until it connects with **Understanding**, which includes the two above it. On the Day of Atonement, all are counted, for the number of transitions occurs on that day. The reason is that the Day of Atonement is a "deep place," hinting at the Atonement that comes from the day which is **Understanding**, as mentioned in its place in Gate 8. This is why it says: *"He shall leave it on the golden [altar],"* referring to the "Golden Sovereignty" within the array of the Sefirot.

# Gate 9

<meta>catchword: enters</meta>
<meta>signature: Kamon</meta>

At the end of the prayer, [we say], *“May the words of my mouth... be acceptable,”* <note>Psalm 19:15</note> which contains the secret of why we pray, “May it be Your Will.” This means that the matter for which we pray should be renewed from the **Source of Will** and **Thought**, just as the world was renewed from that same source. One who understands this—of him it is said: *“He who has clean hands grows stronger and stronger”* <note>Job 17:9</note>. He will know that all the miracles and wonders performed in the times of the Prophets, or the Sages of the Mishnah and the Talmud <term>Tannaim and Amoraim: The rabbinic sages who authored the Mishnah and Gemara</term>, were all possible because they reached the **Source of Will** through their prayer.

The sages of past generations who were concerned about a “change in the Divine Will,” or those who knew the nature of the source called “Will,” were not actually troubled by the idea of a change in Will <margin>(A) Because the one who knows the nature of Will knows there is no change in it. For everything that occurs within it was always present in this holy Will; it is only that the righteous person’s Kindness was summoned to him and he drew it down through his spiritual awakening. All paths require an awakening from below to influence those above so they may be received... thus, there is no change of Will or change of nature here, for that which was hidden from the beginning in the Will has now become revealed.</margin> (A). For the one who knows what “Will” is knows that there is no change in it. However, anyone who merits to have their prayer reach this Source can produce what they need without limit. This is the meaning of: *“And he shall obtain favor [Will] from the Lord”* <note>Proverbs 18:22</note>—meaning, he brings forth and draws down his desire from the **Source of Will**, from the Infinite (*Ein Sof*).

One who understands this will not find the changing of nature or the renewal of signs and wonders in the world to be a difficult concept (B) <margin>(B) Like a room hidden by the King that contains every kind of thing in the world...</margin>. For example: when there is a room containing every kind of thing in the world, anyone who merits to have the key in his hand can produce what he needs from it. What “change of will” is there in that?

This Sefirah <term>Sefirah: One of the ten divine emanations in Kabbalah</term> is called **Depth** (*Omeq*) (C) <margin>(C) Meaning the depth of thought; the essence of the intellect can grasp it through the power of its depth.</margin>, meaning the depth of **Thought**. Do not err and think that the word “depth” in this context refers to something lowly or deep down. Rather, the intention of the term “deep” is something wondrous and far beyond reach, as it is said: *“That which was is far off, and exceeding deep; who can find it out?”* <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>.

This is the secret of *“Out of the depths have I called You, O Lord”* <note>Psalm 130:1</note>—meaning, from the depth of **Thought**, which is the Will that has no end or limit. In this way, it is stated in the *Book of Formation* <term>Sefer Yetzirah: An ancient, foundational text of Jewish mysticism</term>: “The depth of the beginning, the depth of the end.” This reveals that the term “depth” refers to something that has no end or boundary. It is not a term for the lowly alone; rather, for anything that is lofty, the term “depth” is used to support its loftiness, indicating that its height is beyond measure. Similarly, when it speaks of matters that are below, it supports the idea that it descends very far down. In short: the term “depth,” wherever you find it, supports the subject it is describing—if it is above, then it is exceedingly high; if it is below, then exceedingly low; if to the sides, then exceedingly wide. Regarding this, the *Book of Formation* says: “The depth of the rising, the depth of the setting, the depth of the East, the depth of the West.”

If so, contemplate the meaning of *“Out of the depths have I called You, O Lord”*—meaning, from the depth of the **Will**, which is the first letter of the Divine Name <note>The letter Yod (י) of the Tetragrammaton (YHWH)</note>. It is called the **Letter of Thought**, as we intend to explain with God's help. Therefore, it says: *“How very deep are Your thoughts”* <note>Psalm 92:6</note>, using the language of “depth” in relation to **Thought**. One who understands this will understand the verse: *“He reveals deep things out of darkness”* <note>Job 12:22</note> and *“He reveals the deep and secret things”* <note>Daniel 2:22</note>.

This Sefirah is called **Thought**, meaning a “Conceptual Point” (D) <margin>(D) Which is the secret of the beginning of the expansion of the Desire...</margin>, which is the secret of the beginning of the expansion of the Desire in the emanation of Creation and Thought. This is the first *Yod* of the Name, which is a *Yod* (E) <gloss>(E) A conceptual point, internal and hidden within the Supernal Crown, included within the Infinite.</gloss>—an internal conceptual point hidden within the **Supernal Crown** (*Keter Elyon*), included within the **Infinite** (*Ein Sof*). For from this point upward is the World of Absolute Mercy, which has no end, finish, limit, or measure. It expands in the secret of its breadth and depth through its cleaving to the **Crown**. Regarding this, it is said: *“How very deep are Your thoughts.”* It says “Your thoughts” in the plural, for they are the secret of the **Thirty-Two Paths of Thought**, and there is no one who can contemplate them. They are called the “Depth of the Height,” meaning they expand from the **Crown**, which is the Supreme Height. No one can contemplate them except like one who draws water with a bucket from a deep well that has no end. The one who draws does not enter the well himself to draw; rather, he draws water from the well using the bucket. Thus, no creature can contemplate the secret of the depth of **Thought** except by means of **Understanding** (*Binah*), which is like the bucket that

# Gate 9

(ו) Regarding that which Moses our teacher <note>Hebrew: *Moshe Rabbenu*, peace be upon him</note> asked—to attain an understanding of the Divine through the **contemplation of Thought**—it was hidden from him. The response given to him was: *"I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy on whom I will show mercy"* <note>Exodus 33:19</note>. This matter is not known to any created being. To this, the Scripture alludes: *"Many things have You done, O Lord my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us; there is none to be compared unto You; if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered"* <note>Psalm 40:6</note>. 

In every instance where you find the term **"wonders"** <note>Hebrew: *Nifla'ot*</note>, it refers to a matter that is concealed from creatures and is known to none but Him, blessed be He. Regarding this it is written: *"To Him who alone does great wonders"* <note>Psalm 136:4</note>—certainly "alone." And of this it is written: *"Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain it"* <note>Psalm 139:6</note>. Furthermore, the angel said to Manoah: *"Why do you ask my name, seeing it is hidden [wonderful]?"* <note>Judges 13:18; Hebrew: *Peli*</note>. This implies: "I have no fixed name except within Thought." As it says: *"Awesome in praises, doing wonders"* <note>Exodus 15:11; Hebrew: *Oseh Pele*</note>; and *"Wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom"* <note>Isaiah 28:29</note>. 

Even regarding matters that a human has the capacity to grasp, but which are currently hidden from them, the term **"wonder"** is used: *"If a matter is too hidden [wonderful] for you in judgment"* <note>Deuteronomy 17:8; Hebrew: *Yippale*</note>. Also: *"Behold, I will proceed to do a marvelous work among this people, even a marvelous work and a wonder; for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid"* <note>Isaiah 29:14</note>. Concerning such things, it is said: *"How deep are Your thoughts"* <note>Psalm 92:6</note>. This verse alludes to both **Wisdom** and **Understanding** <term>Chokhmah and Binah: The two highest cognitive Sefirot or divine emanations</term>; all is contained therein. Within this verse is also captured the secret of "the righteous who suffers and the wicked who prospers." And this Sefirah is called:

## Awe
<note>Hebrew: *Yirah*</note>

This means that one who reaches the point of thinking about this supreme and deep place must feel awe and dread, lest their thoughts become agitated, rushing to contemplate more than is appropriate. Regarding this, it is said in the *Book of Formation* <term>Sefer Yetzirah: An ancient Jewish mystical text</term>: *"Bridle your mouth from speaking and your heart from thinking; and if your heart runs, return it to its place."* For this place is the site of awe and fear when contemplating its nature and depths. 

When Jacob reached this place, which is called *Yesh* <note>Literally "Being" or "Is"; a term for the primordial source</note>, he was awestruck and terrified, saying: *"Surely the Lord is in this place... and he was afraid, and said: How awesome is this place!"* <note>Genesis 28:16-17</note>. Even though the Sefirah of **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> is specifically called "Awesome," it is because it ascends upward and is held within the **Crown** <term>Keter: The highest Sefirah, representing the Divine Will</term> in the secret of **Will**, which is the secret of **Awe**. From there it is also said of Moses: *"For he was afraid to look upon God"* <note>Exodus 3:6</note>; he was afraid to gaze into the depth of his thought and thus set a boundary for his contemplation. 

Happy is the one who reaches the level of Awe like Moses our teacher. When the Lord came to reveal the secrets of His hidden places to Israel through the **Gates of Understanding** <note>Sha'arei Binah</note> during the Giving of the Torah, He warned them not to gaze into that depth—meaning, they should not stretch their thoughts to contemplate the depth of the Divine Thought, lest their hearts be overwhelmed and they *"break through unto the Lord"* <note>Exodus 19:21</note>. They acted accordingly, as it is said: *"And the people stood afar off, but Moses drew near unto the thick darkness"* <note>Exodus 20:21</note>. 

Know that all of Israel who stood at Sinai had different levels and measures for their perceptions, as hinted in the verse: *"And He said to Moses: Come up unto the Lord..."* (ז) *"And Moses alone shall come near unto the Lord; but they shall not come near"* <note>Exodus 24:1-2</note>. Because there are many levels in the expansion of thought within the Sefirah of **Will**, He told them that each should reach the boundary appropriate for them. This is what Moses meant when he said to them: *"For God has come to test you, and that His fear may be before your faces, that you sin not"* <note>Exodus 20:20</note>. 

I shall now explain these two verses through their hidden meanings: *"To test you"* <note>Hebrew: *Nassot*</note>—He came to test them with the power of what they could endure. It is like a person who tests a sword to see its cutting power. So did God "test" you when He was revealed to you, so that you might test yourselves to see how much strength you have to gaze at His greatness and the intensity of His perception. But when you came to the test, you fled, saying you did not have the strength to stand before this great vision, as it is said: *"And you came near to me, all of you..."*

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the highest realms of the Divine, specifically focusing on the concept of "Divine Thought" (Machshavah) as a boundary that human intellect cannot cross. # Gate 9

(ו) According to what **"ascended in Thought,"** <note>original: *alah be-machshavah*</note> as is said in the Talmud: "Thus it ascended in Thought." <note>A phrase used in the Talmud to describe a divine decree that transcends human logic.</note> Sometimes the *Sefirah* of **Kingdom** <note>Hebrew: *Malchut*, the lowest of the ten divine emanations</note> elevates and rises until it reaches **Understanding** <note>Hebrew: *Binah*, the third emanation</note>, and it is then found clinging to **Thought**. In such cases, they also say of it: "Thus it ascended in Thought."

(ז) However, regarding the **Contemplation of the Chariot**, <note>Hebrew: *Tzfiyat ha-Merkavah*, a form of early Jewish mysticism focused on the vision of God's throne-chariot.</note> the language of **"descent"** is used, as it is said: "He descended to the Chariot." The reason "descent" is used is that the one who contemplates the Chariot first enters a high, exalted place—up to the source of light from which they receive the flow of the vision—(ח) and then returns and "descends" to view the Chariot. These matters are exceedingly deep. If you are worthy, God willing, you will yet grasp great principles within them.

The final word on this is that **Thought** never separates from the **Crown** <note>Hebrew: *Keter*, the highest Sefirah, representing the Divine Will</note>. The secret is that one letter includes both of them: the letter ***Yod*** and its **tip** <note>Hebrew: *kotzo shel Yod*. Kabbalists view the tiny point at the top of the letter Yod as a symbol for the most hidden, infinite level of God.</note>; understand this very well. If one is worthy of ascending, they ascend by means of **Understanding** (*Binah*).

The conclusion of the matter: it "ascended *in* Thought" but did not "ascend *above* Thought." For all things created in the world "ascended in Thought," but they did not rise above it, because there is no one who can enter it except for **Who** <gloss>(Binah)</gloss> <note>The Hebrew word for "Who" (*Mi*) is a common Kabbalistic code for the Sefirah of Binah.</note>. Now, incline your ear and hear what is possible for you to hear regarding this matter:

Every place where it is said "it ascended in Thought," it is a phrase of **mockery** <note>meaning a dismissal of the questioner’s premise</note>, for the gates are locked before you in this matter. This is because the mystery is closed and sealed in the Upper Chamber where no creature can enter; this is the chamber of **Deep Thought**, which is called **Will Without Limit**. Therefore, "muzzle your mouth from speaking." <note>A quote from *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient mystical text.</note>

This is what was said regarding **Rabbi Akiva** in the matter of the visions of **Moses our Teacher**, peace be upon him. When Moses saw that they <note>the Romans</note> were combing Rabbi Akiva's flesh <note>with iron combs during his martyrdom</note>, he said: "This is Torah, and this is its reward?!" God said to him: **"Silence! For thus it ascended in Thought."** This means: your question is not in a place where you can grasp an answer; rather, be silent. And what is the reason? Because "it ascended in Thought"—it is in a place where you cannot ascend, and it is not the way of Thought to descend from its place to reach you, because it clings to the **World of Mercy** in the **Highest Crown**. If so, be silent.

Now we have delivered into your hand a great principle for every place you find the phrase "thus it ascended in Thought": these matters are hidden, and no creature can contemplate them. This is because **Thought** has no "viewing" <note>it cannot be looked into from the outside</note> at all, as there is no way to enter it, and it has no end or limit. If so, how can one who has a limit measure something that has no limit? Regarding such things it is said: *"How very deep are Your thoughts!"* <note>Psalm 92:6</note>.

In this matter is held the mystery of **"the wicked who prospers and the righteous who suffers."** Blessed be the Master of the Will, the end of whose zeal and wisdom cannot be grasped. Just as He said regarding Rabbi Akiva, "Silence, thus it ascended in Thought," the sign of this matter is in this Psalm: *"How great are Your works, O Lord, how very deep are Your thoughts! A brutish man knows not..."* and so on, until *"When the wicked spring up..."* And what is the reason? *"But You, O Lord, are on high forever."* This means: this matter is in the **Height of Thought**, and there is no one who can reach the matter, for "thus it ascended in Thought."

Even though man has no power to grasp the contemplation of Thought, the righteous have a tradition by "hearing of the ear." Therefore it says: *"When evildoers rise up against me, my ears shall hear"* <note>Psalm 92:12</note> and *"The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree."* Behold, everything is explained through hints. And this is...

For even though it is not called to it generally, it must also hint to itself, as is its law in the book *The System* <note>Hebrew: *Sefer Ma'arekhet ha-Elohut*, a foundational 14th-century Kabbalistic text</note> at the end of the "Gate of Destruction." And so it hints: it shall be, it was, it is. It is missing like the branch of his right hand, and this is for the "primacy of the King of kings."

**Part as a whole:** The explanation is that if he intended to open one [gate] above, like the point of the upper curtain, and the nature below it... <note>The text here becomes highly technical and uses abbreviated Rabbinic Hebrew (Rashi script style logic).</note> first toward the top, and the nature beneath it, this one near that one... **Tower:** The explanation is that it seems to me he placed this **Kingdom** one below the other, meaning Kingdom in another place, and such is the order of the *Sefirot*.

(א) **"According to what ascended in Thought":** The explanation is according to what the **"Actives"** ascended—which are **Understanding** (*Binah*) and **Kingdom** (*Malchut*)—to produce "Will" from it to perform the action or the necessary separation.

(ב) **"But for the 'Production' [Contemplation] of the Chariot":** The explanation is that one who wants to grasp and know the matters of the **Work of the Chariot** <note>Ma'aseh Merkavah</note>, the language of **"descent"** is used.

(ג) **"And returns and descends and views the Chariot":** The explanation is that he returns and descends in his vision from above to below. This is like one who wants to see all the affairs of a great city; he must ascend to a high tower and view from it, and he knows everything above.

...who guards his body and soul so that no blemish falls upon them. Thus it is found that he refines his body and ignites his soul, purifying his inner chambers <note>original: *tuchotav* - a biblical term for the innermost parts of a person</note> so that he may find favor in the eyes of the Living God. And this is the level of **Fear** that was spoken of regarding Abraham after the ten trials he was tested with, all of which he accepted out of love. As it is said: "Now I know that you are a fearer of God" <note>Genesis 22:12, spoken after the Binding of Isaac</note>. This is the level above which there is no higher level **(D)**, and it is greater than love. This is the attribute of Fear that clings to a specific *Sefirah* <note>one of the ten divine emanations</note> which is the mystery of the **Will** and **Thought**. 

Now that we have informed you of this, you must contemplate the mystery of **External Fear** and the mystery of **Inner Fear**. 

**External Fear** <note>Hebrew: *Yirah Chitzonit*</note> is when a person restrains himself from transgressions out of fear of the severity of the punishment. However, such a person is not necessarily attached to the positive commandments—those for which there is no immediate punishment for neglect. 

**Inner Fear** <note>Hebrew: *Yirah Pnimit*</note> is when one desires to fulfill the positive commandments in order to carry out the word of his Creator. For such a person, distancing himself from transgressions is easy; therefore, he surrenders himself, his wealth, his wife, and his children to the service of the King. All of this stems from the greatness of his "cleaving" <note>Hebrew: *devekut* - spiritual attachment</note> to the Name, may He be blessed.

Behold, this is the mystery of the verse "And you shall walk in His ways" <note>Deuteronomy 28:9</note>, which our Sages, of blessed memory, interpreted as: "Just as He is gracious, you also be gracious; just as He is merciful, you also be merciful." That is to say: accustom yourself to adorn yourself with the jewelry commonly worn in the King's house, so that you may be worthy to enter His palace and serve before Him. For if you do not wear those garments and those jewels, they will not receive you in the King's house. And what are these jewels? They are all the various types of positive commandments. This is the mystery of "walking in His ways" and the mystery of "You shall be holy" <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>—and this is the mystery of **Inner Fear**.

Abraham inherited this level at the **Binding** <note>The *Akedah*, the binding of Isaac</note>, which is higher than love. For Abraham’s service had always been through love, as it says: "Abraham my lover" <note>Isaiah 41:8; the author notes the Hebrew uses *Ohavi* (the one who loves Me) rather than *Ahuvai* (the one I love)</note>. **(E)** And it says: "To grant an inheritance to those who love Me" <note>Proverbs 8:21</note>. This is the world that King Hezekiah was afraid he would not merit, as he said: "I said, I shall not see the Lord in the land of the living" <note>Isaiah 38:11</note>.

If so, guard these great principles we have told you: 
1. **External Fear**
2. **Love** (which is above it)
3. **Inner Fear** (which rises above Love)

Therefore, the "God of Abraham" is the mystery of **Inner Fear**, which is the mystery of **Wisdom** <note>The Sefirah of *Chokhmah*</note>, from which the essence of his attribute—**Greatness** <note>The Sefirah of *Chesed* or Kindness</note>—originates. At the time of the Binding, he came to cling to it, as it is said: "For now I know that you are a fearer of God." The text uses the name *Elohim* <note>The Divine Name associated with Judgment and Rigor</note> because one only enters this attribute **(F)** through a "trial" <note>Hebrew: *nisayon*</note>, which comes through the attribute of *Elohim*. Therefore, it is called **Fear**, lest one does not emerge from the judgment fit to enter it. Thus, Abraham was tested by *Elohim*: "And God [*Elohim*] tested Abraham" <note>Genesis 22:1</note>. Similarly, at the standing at Mount Sinai, it says: "For God [*Elohim*] has come to test you" <note>Exodus 20:17</note>.

Now open your eyes and contemplate every place in the Torah where you find the word "Fear" and see which side it leans toward:
* Is it toward the side of **External Fear**, to which all types of punishments, plagues, and afflictions are bound? 
* Or is it toward the side of **Inner Fear**, to which all types of abundance, emanation, blessing, and life are bound?

One who understands the essence will understand the high standing of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, and the mystery of "The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever" <note>Psalm 19:10</note>, and the mystery of "Happy is the man who fears the Lord, who walks in His ways" <note>Psalm 112:1 / Psalm 128:1</note>. For the explanation of the verse—since it says "Happy is the man who fears the Lord"—why does it add "who walks in His ways"? It means that the "Fear" we are speaking of in this context is the mystery of **Inner Fear**, which is "walking in His ways," defined as "delighting greatly in His commandments." 

Therefore, he opened these two verses with "Happy" <note>Hebrew: *Ashrei*</note> because it is a beloved portion, and many great principles depend on this source. Contemplate all the verses where "Fear" is mentioned.

This *Sefirah* is called in the Torah **"Eden,"** <note>Hebrew: *Eden*</note> meaning the beginning of the expansion of **Thought**. It is the source from which all the *Sefirot* were revealed from the **Supreme Crown** <note>Keter</note>. It is the fountain and the source from which all existing things are found through the revelation of the higher *Sefirot* **(G)**. And the term *Eden*...

...and so on. "And now, why should we die, for [this great fire] will consume us" <note>quoting Deuteronomy 5:22</note> and so on. For you have undergone a "trial" <note>Hebrew: *Nisayon* - referring to the test at Sinai</note> through that divine speech, and you fled from it because of its great strength and grandeur. Therefore, "God has come in order to test you" <note>Exodus 20:17</note> and "so that His fear shall be upon your faces, so that you do not sin." From now on, you shall be afraid to contemplate the greatness of His perception or to enter beyond your designated partition, lest you sin against the Heavens and become liable for destruction. 

This is the meaning of "so that His fear shall be upon your faces." Since you stood in the trial and feared the fire, saying "Why should we die? Why should we die?", therefore from now on His fear shall be upon your faces so that you do not gaze beyond the boundary appropriate for your perception.

I am now alluding [to the verse]: "He said to man: Behold, the **fear** of the Lord is **Wisdom** (*Chochmah*), and to turn from evil is **Understanding** (*Binah*)" <note>Job 28:28</note>. Humility is the secret of the **Crown** (*Keter*), which is the "tip of the [letter] *Yod*," and the "reward" <note>Hebrew: *Ekev* - literally 'heel' or 'consequence'</note> of the end is the sign of the child.

Both are within the secret of the letter ***Yod***, for within it, Humility and Wisdom are included, and Fear is grasped between the two of them—it is the place of connection and attachment. Thus, these two verses are well explained. 

The third verse is: "Behold, the fear of the Lord is Wisdom" **(D)**, for Fear is the highest level among the levels. And if you should say **(E)**: "But is not one who serves out of **love** greater than one who serves out of **fear**?" Know that the Love and the Fear that cling to Divine service are one matter. For Fear has two faces: there is **External Fear** and there is **Inner Fear**. 

**External Fear** exists as long as a person has not yet perceived the Greatness (may He be blessed). He acts out of fear of punishment and suffering; this is External Fear. He is like one who restrains himself from killing or stealing out of fear that they might kill him. Behold, this fear is not "certain" <note>meaning it is not derived from a pure spiritual source</note>; nevertheless, it is a good intention. 

Even so, there is an **Inner Fear** greater than this, which is the fear that comes by way of perception. How so? If a person merits to perceive the greatness of the Creator (may He be blessed) and the magnitude of His awesome deeds, the goodness, the levels, and the types of flow (*shefa*) and blessings attached to the magnitude of His perception and His height. When he recognizes His high level, he will recognize the "seed" of his own body—that he is but a **maggot and a worm**. Then the man will dread and be afraid to rebel against a King as great as He. He will say: "Who brought me this far, to recognize and gaze upon the great and awesome King, the **King of Kings, the Holy One Blessed be He**, while I am a lowly, light, and despised creature? What am I? What is my life, that I should be worthy of the greatness of this place?" 

Thus, it is found that he is afraid lest he not be worthy to be accepted into the palace of the King of Kings, the Holy One Blessed be He. Consequently, he strives and repairs himself, scouring his soul and beautifying it, perhaps he might find favor in the eyes of the Lord and He will accept him to serve in the King's palace. And behold, when a man clings to this fear, he finds himself bound to His high level.

# Gate 9

This refers to the language of the **Source**, from which the word and the mystery are drawn. "A river goes out of Eden" <note>Genesis 2:10</note>—meaning, a river emerges from the Source and the Fountain. The term "Eden" <note>Hebrew: *Eden*</note> is related to the expression used regarding Sarah when her "source" <note>a euphemism for her menstrual cycle/fertility</note> had ceased and then returned to her; she said, "After I have withered, shall I have **rejuvenation**?" <note>Hebrew: *Ednah*; Genesis 18:12</note>. This implies that the Source was renewed within her.

We have already explained that "A river goes out of Eden" refers to the Sefirah of **Binah** <note>Understanding</note>. "Going out of Eden" means it emerges from **Chokhmah** <note>Wisdom</note>, which is the mystery of the Source drawn from the **Supreme Crown** <note>Keter</note>. 

"To water the garden" <note>Genesis 2:10</note> means to provide divine flow to the Sefirah of **Malkhut** <note>Kingship</note>. **Binah**, which is the mystery of the River, waters **Malkhut**, which is the Garden, by means of the seven Sefirot: **Gedulah** <note>Greatness/Mercy</note>, **Gevurah** <note>Might</note>, **Tiferet** <note>Beauty</note>, **Netzach** <note>Victory</note>, **Hod** <note>Splendor</note>, and **Yesod** <note>Foundation</note>. This is the mystery of the seven [levels] that exist between the first letter *He* (ה) of the Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note> and the final *He* (ה). 

From **Malkhut** and below is the **World of Separation** <note>see Sefer ha-Bahir, page 17</note>. "And from there it was parted and became four heads" <note>Genesis 2:10</note> refers to the mystery of the four camps of the **Shekhinah** <note>the Divine Presence</note> that separate from the mystery of the **World of Unity**. This is the mystery of (A) the four letters in Unity, and the "four heads" in Separation.

Now, we must inform you of what is written in the Torah: "The Lord God planted a garden in Eden from the east" <note>Genesis 2:8</note>. (B) How is this possible? For we have said that it [Eden] is the mystery of the world of **Keter** <note>Crown</note>, which is the world of **Thought** that "no eye has ever seen" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>—so how can you say the Garden is planted *within* Eden? 

(C) Furthermore, our Sages revealed this matter in the chapter "One may not stand" <note>Talmud, Berakhot 30b/34b</note>: (D) Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said, "What is 'Eye has not seen'? This is the **wine preserved in its grapes** from the six days of Creation." Resh Lakish said, "This is Eden, which no eye has ever seen." And if you ask, "Where did Adam live?"—he lived in the Garden. And if you ask, "Is the Garden not Eden?"—the verse teaches: "A river goes out of Eden to water the garden." Thus ends their words.

Contemplate the words of the Master [the author] of blessed memory in this place. He says that Eden is one thing and the Garden is another. If so, how can the literal meaning of the verse be settled? For they did not finish explaining it in the Talmud. 

Here, I will provide a hint: "And the Lord God planted a garden in Eden." He planted the roots of the Garden—which is the mystery of the Sefirah of **Malkhut**—within Eden, which is the mystery of the **Beginning of Thought** <note>Chokhmah</note>. This is because the end of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> and the end of Intelligence <note>Binah</note> are one unified whole. This is the mystery of the "planting." 

How so? The final letter *He* (ה) of the Name has its "plantings" extending into the letter *Vav* (ו), and from there they spread and go until the first letter *He* (ה), and from there they draw nourishment from the letter *Yod* (י) <note>it is known that the *Keter* surrounds the *Yod* and the power of the *Ein Sof* is there</note>, which is the first letter of the Name. This is the mystery of "And the Lord God planted a garden in Eden"—it is a great mystery, hidden and sealed within the four letters of the Name. 

From where is all this drawn? "From the east" <note>Hebrew: *Mi-Kedem*</note>—this is the mystery of the **tip of the Yod** <note>representing Keter, the highest point</note>. A wealthy person <note>or a wise one</note> knows how to direct the path according to the order of the Garden's planting, from the level of the Sefirah of **Malkhut** up to the Sefirah of **Chokhmah**, which is the mystery of the True One. (E) ~~Gate of the matters of my handiwork~~ to be glorified. If you understand what we hinted at in the *Faithful Shepherd* <note>Ra'aya Meheimna</note> <insert>Section 100</insert>, the literal meaning will be settled. What the Sages of blessed memory interpreted regarding it also settles upon "Eden to its ground," as a river goes out from it to water the Garden. The truth is that it is so: Adam lived in the Garden, and not in Eden. (F) And the reason is "Eye has not seen." (G) [This mystery] is hidden within many things in Creation; if you are worthy, you will receive a "drop to the mouth" of deep and sealed traditions regarding them, which we hinted at in the word *Adonai* <note>Lord</note>. The things we have written are merely hints and parables. 

The Sages of blessed memory already hinted at great principles regarding this in the Midrash. You must also consider that there is another difficult verse: "You were in Eden, the garden of God" <note>Ezekiel 28:13</note>, which implies that Eden *is* the Garden. I am now untying the knots of doubt: **Hiram**, king of Tyre, ascended in the Beginning of Thought, which is Eden, and he is the "Grapes." <note>Note: 'Wine preserved in its grapes'</note>. And this is a <margin>hidden</margin> matter.

**Commentary (Sha'ar Cheshbon):**

**(A) Four letters in Unity, etc.** This means the four letters of the Name [Y-H-V-H] which are hinted at in the unity of the Sefirot. Correspondingly, in the World of Separation, there are the four winds [directions] of the world, as mentioned at the beginning of the Gate.

**(B) And behold, Eden is for those who say** that it is the mystery of the world of **Keter**, because it is the source of the "workings" there, the world of the Crown.

**(C) Furthermore, the Sages revealed the matter.** Meaning, they revealed that Eden and the Garden are two distinct levels: the Garden is one, and Eden is another.

**(D) Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: "Preserved in its grapes."** The explanation is that **Binah** is called this because it is "preserved" by itself—Keter and Chokhmah—from any [unbalanced] extension from there. "Preserved" <note>Meshumar</note> is from the language of "guarding" <note>Mishmeret</note>. "Eye has not seen" refers to **Binah**, for it is the guard of the "six days of Creation" <note>the lower six Sefirot</note> that follow it. My understanding is only slight, based on the mention of the "dwelling place" as a model of the [primordial] days. It is also called "Wine" because there is a measure of "Judgment" <note>Din</note> within it. The reason for this is that through it, all the paths that are hidden in the mystery are spread out and revealed to the world, just as wine brings joy. It is the joy of the intellect and the connection...
